Title: Ad sales boost Time Warner profit
Article_Text: Quarterly profits at US media giant TimeWarner jumped 76% to $1.13bn (£600m) for the three months to December, from $639m year-earlier.  The firm, which is now one of the biggest investors in Google, ...
Summary: TimeWarner's quarterly profits jumped 76% to $1.13bn, driven by high-speed internet connections and advert sales. The company's film division saw profits slump 27% due to box-office flops. TimeWarner is projecting operating earnings growth of around 5% for 2005.

Title: Dollar gains on Greenspan speech
Article_Text: The dollar has hit its highest level against the euro in almost three months after the Federal Reserve head said the US trade deficit is set to stabilise.  And Alan Greenspan highlighted the US govern...
Summary: The dollar has reached its highest level against the euro in almost three months after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's speech, citing a stabilizing US trade deficit and government willingness to curb spending. The dollar's value has been affected by concerns about the deficit and China's currency peg. The US Federal Reserve's interest rate decision has also contributed to the dollar's increase.

Title: Yukos unit buyer faces loan claim
Article_Text: The owners of embattled Russian oil giant Yukos are to ask the buyer of its former production unit to pay back a $900m (£479m) loan.  State-owned Rosneft bought the Yugansk unit for $9.3bn in a sale f...
Summary: The owners of Yukos are asking the buyer of its former production unit, Rosneft, to repay a $900m loan, as Rosneft faces similar repayment demands from foreign banks. The loan was secured by Yugansk, which was sold to Rosneft in a sale forced by Russia to settle a tax claim. Rosneft intends to take action against Yukos to recover tax claims and debts.

Title: High fuel prices hit BA's profits
Article_Text: British Airways has blamed high fuel prices for a 40% drop in profits.  Reporting its results for the three months to 31 December 2004, the airline made a pre-tax profit of £75m ($141m) compared with ...
Summary: British Airways reported a 40% drop in profits due to high fuel prices, but still beat market expectations. The airline expects a rise in full-year revenues and has introduced fuel surcharges to offset increased costs. BA's shares closed up four pence at 274.5 pence.

Title: Pernod takeover talk lifts Domecq
Article_Text: Shares in UK drinks and food firm Allied Domecq have risen on speculation that it could be the target of a takeover by France's Pernod Ricard.  Reports in the Wall Street Journal and the Financial Tim...
Summary: Shares in UK drinks and food firm Allied Domecq have risen on speculation that it could be the target of a takeover by France's Pernod Ricard. Pernod is seeking acquisitions but refused to comment on specifics. Allied Domecq has a capitalisation of £5.7bn, while Pernod has a market value of 7.5bn euros.

Title: Japan narrowly escapes recession
Article_Text: Japan's economy teetered on the brink of a technical recession in the three months to September, figures show.  Revised figures indicated growth of just 0.1% - and a similar-sized contraction in the p...
Summary: Japan's economy experienced a technical recession in the three months to September, with revised figures showing 0.1% growth and a similar-sized contraction in the previous quarter.

Title: Jobs growth still slow in the US
Article_Text: The US created fewer jobs than expected in January, but a fall in jobseekers pushed the unemployment rate to its lowest level in three years.  According to Labor Department figures, US firms added onl...
Summary: The US created fewer jobs than expected in January, but the unemployment rate fell to its lowest level in three years. The job gains were below market expectations, but still pushed the unemployment rate down to 5.2%. The administration's first term jobs record ended in positive territory.

Title: India calls for fair trade rules
Article_Text: India, which attends the G7 meeting of seven leading industrialised nations on Friday, is unlikely to be cowed by its newcomer status.  In London on Thursday ahead of the meeting, India's finance mini...
Summary: India's finance minister, Palaniappan Chidambaram, criticized the restrictive trade policies of the G7 nations and called for reform of the United Nations, the World Bank, and the IMF. He also expressed support for floating exchange rates to help countries cope with economic shocks. The IMF warned that India's budget deficit was too large and would hamper the country's economic growth.

Title: Ethiopia's crop production up 24%
Article_Text: Ethiopia produced 14.27 million tonnes of crops in 2004, 24% higher than in 2003 and 21% more than the average of the past five years, a report says.  In 2003, crop production totalled 11.49 million t...
Summary: Ethiopia's crop production increased by 24% in 2004 compared to 2003, with good rains, fertilizers, and improved seeds contributing to the rise. However, 2.2 million Ethiopians still need emergency assistance, and the country will require additional food aid. The Food and Agriculture Organisation recommends buying food assistance locally to support domestic markets and farmers.

Title: Court rejects $280bn tobacco case
Article_Text: A US government claim accusing the country's biggest tobacco companies of covering up the effects of smoking has been thrown out by an appeal court.  The demand for $280bn (£155bn) - filed by the Clin...
Summary: A US government claim accusing tobacco companies of covering up the effects of smoking has been rejected by an appeal court, with the court ruling that the case could not be brought under federal anti-racketeering laws.

Title: Ask Jeeves tips online ad revival
Article_Text: Ask Jeeves has become the third leading online search firm this week to thank a revival in internet advertising for improving fortunes.  The firm's revenue nearly tripled in the fourth quarter of 2004...
Summary: Ask Jeeves' revenue nearly tripled in the fourth quarter of 2004, exceeding $86m, due to a revival in internet advertising. This trend is also seen in rival Google and Yahoo, which earned $204m and $187m respectively. However, the shares of both Ask Jeeves and Doubleclick fell by 4% due to excessive expectations.

Title: Indonesians face fuel price rise
Article_Text: Indonesia's government has confirmed it is considering raising fuel prices by as much as 30%.  Millions of Indonesians use kerosene for basic cooking, and prices have been heavily subsidised for years...
Summary: Indonesia's government is considering raising fuel prices by up to 30% to curb subsidies and redirect funds to aid programmes for the poor. The move comes after the government spent a significant amount on fuel subsidies in 2004. A potential price hike is expected to face public backlash.

Title: Peugeot deal boosts Mitsubishi
Article_Text: Struggling Japanese car maker Mitsubishi Motors has struck a deal to supply French car maker Peugeot with 30,000 sports utility vehicles (SUV).  The two firms signed a Memorandum of Understanding, and...
Summary: Mitsubishi Motors has agreed to supply Peugeot with 30,000 SUVs, with production to take place in Japan, as the company seeks to boost sales and reduce losses.

Title: Telegraph newspapers axe 90 jobs
Article_Text: The Daily and Sunday Telegraph newspapers are axing 90 journalist jobs - 17% of their editorial staff.  The Telegraph Group says the cuts are needed to fund an £150m investment in new printing facilit...
Summary: The Daily and Sunday Telegraph newspapers are cutting 90 journalist jobs, 17% of their editorial staff, to fund an £150m investment in new printing facilities. The National Union of Journalists has called for the management to recall the notice of redundancy. The company had ignored the 90-day consultation period required for companies planning more than 10 redundancies.

Title: Air passengers win new EU rights
Article_Text: Air passengers who are unable to board their flights because of overbooking, cancellations or flight delays can now demand greater compensation.  New EU rules set compensation at between 250 euros (£1...
Summary: The European Union has implemented new rules requiring airlines to offer compensation to passengers affected by overbooking, cancellations, or flight delays. The compensation ranges from 250 to 600 euros, depending on the flight length. Airlines have criticized the legislation, claiming it could lead to higher prices.

Title: China keeps tight rein on credit
Article_Text: China's efforts to stop the economy from overheating by clamping down on credit will continue into 2005, state media report.  The curbs were introduced earlier this year to ward off the risk that rapi...
Summary: China is continuing to clamp down on credit to curb its overheating economy, which has seen rapid expansion and soaring prices. The government has a 7% growth target, but insists that the overshoot does not mean a 'hard landing'. China's low exchange rate has made its exports cheap on world markets.

Title: Parmalat boasts doubled profits
Article_Text: Parmalat, the Italian food group at the centre of one of Europe's most painful corporate scandals, has reported a doubling in profit.  Its pre-tax earnings in the fourth quarter were 77m euros (£53m; ...
Summary: Parmalat has reported a doubling in profit to 77m euros, but has also been fined 11m euros for violating takeover rules. The company's debt is close to 12bn euros, but its brands have continued to perform strongly. A complex financial position is being unwound through legal action.

Title: India's rupee hits five-year high
Article_Text: India's rupee has hit a five-year high after Standard & Poor's (S&P) raised the country's foreign currency rating.  The rupee climbed to 43.305 per US dollar on Thursday, up from a close of 43.41. The...
Summary: India's rupee has reached a five-year high after Standard & Poor's raised its foreign currency rating, with the currency gaining almost 1% in the past three sessions.

Title: India widens access to telecoms
Article_Text: India has raised the limit for foreign direct investment in telecoms companies from 49% to 74%.  Communications Minister Dayanidhi Maran said that there is a need to fund the fast-growing mobile marke...
Summary: India has raised its foreign direct investment limit in telecoms companies from 49% to 74% to fund the growing mobile market. The government aims to increase mobile users from 95 million to 200-250 million by 2007. Foreign investors need government approval to exceed 49% stake.

Title: Call centre users 'lose patience'
Article_Text: Customers trying to get through to call centres are getting impatient and quicker to hang up, a survey suggests.  Once past the welcome message, callers on average hang up after just 65 seconds of lis...
Summary: A survey by Dimension Data found that customers are becoming increasingly impatient with call centres, hanging up after just 65 seconds of listening to canned music. The number of abandoned calls has increased, with a sixth of callers giving up, and poor training is a major issue, leading to a high churn rate and low resolution rates.

Title: Rank 'set to sell off film unit'
Article_Text: Leisure group Rank could unveil plans to demerge its film services unit and sell its media business, reports claim.  Rank, formerly famous for the Carry On series, will expose the shake-up at the anno...
Summary: Leisure group Rank is considering demerging its film services unit and selling its media business, with Goldman Sachs valuing the demerged Deluxe Film unit at £300m. The move comes after the group has focused on fewer businesses and embarked on a major cost-cutting programme. Rank aims to concentrate on its gaming, bars and hotels business.

Title: Sluggish economy hits German jobs
Article_Text: The number of people out of work in Europe's largest economy has risen for the tenth straight month as growth remains stubbornly slow.  German unemployment rose 7,000 in November to 4.464 million peop...
Summary: Germany's unemployment rate rose 7,000 in November to 10.8% of the workforce, with stagnant growth stifling the job market. The government has introduced measures to encourage job creation, including the 'one-euro jobs' scheme. High oil prices and the euro's value are also affecting the economy.

Title: Mixed signals from French economy
Article_Text: The French economy picked up speed at the end of 2004, official figures show - but still looks set to have fallen short of the government's hopes.  According to state statistics body INSEE, growth for...
Summary: The French economy experienced a 0.7-0.8% growth in the three months to December, surpassing the 0.6% forecast, according to INSEE statistics. This would be the best quarterly showing since early 2002, leaving GDP up 2.3% for the full year, short of the government's 2.5% target. The positive figures mark a trend of improving economic indicators, with the European Central Bank also expressing optimism for the eurozone.

Title: US trade gap hits record in 2004
Article_Text: The gap between US exports and imports hit an all-time high of $671.7bn (£484bn) in 2004, latest figures show.  The Commerce Department said the trade deficit for all of last year was 24.4% above the ...
Summary: The US trade deficit hit an all-time high of $671.7bn in 2004, with the deficit with China being the largest ever recorded with a single country. The deficit narrowed by 4.9% in December, but economists expect it to continue widening in 2005. The US consumer's appetite for imported goods reached record levels last year.

Title: Yukos loses US bankruptcy battle
Article_Text: A judge has dismissed an attempt by Russian oil giant Yukos to gain bankruptcy protection in the US.  Yukos filed for Chapter 11 protection in Houston in an unsuccessful attempt to halt the auction of...
Summary: A US judge has dismissed Yukos' attempt to gain bankruptcy protection in the US, ruling that the company did not have enough US presence to establish jurisdiction. Yukos had sought to halt the auction of its Yugansk division, which was sold to pay off $27.5bn in unpaid taxes. The company claims the sale was illegal and is seeking damages.

Title: Safety alert as GM recalls cars
Article_Text: The world's biggest carmaker General Motors (GM) is recalling nearly 200,000 vehicles in the US on safety grounds, according to federal regulators.  The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration ...
Summary: General Motors is recalling nearly 200,000 vehicles in the US due to potential malfunctions with the braking systems, including 155,465 pickups and SUVs from the 2004 and 2005 model years. The recall also affects 19,924 Cadillac XLR coupes and 17,815 Buick Raniers. GM stressed that it did not know of any injuries related to the problems.

Title: Steel firm 'to cut' 45,000 jobs
Article_Text: Mittal Steel, one of the world's largest steel producers, could cut up to 45,000 jobs over the next five years, its chief executive has said.  The Netherlands-based company is due to complete its $4.5...
Summary: Mittal Steel, a global steel producer, may cut up to 45,000 jobs over the next five years as part of its acquisition of US firm ISG, according to its CEO Lakshmi Mittal. The company aims to reduce its workforce by 7,000 to 8,000 annually. The acquisition is expected to create a combined company with annual sales of $32bn and a production capacity of 70 million tonnes.

Title: Strong demand triggers oil rally
Article_Text: Crude oil prices surged back above the $47 a barrel mark on Thursday after an energy market watchdog raised its forecasts for global demand.  The International Energy Agency (IEA) warned demand for Op...
Summary: Crude oil prices surged back above $47 a barrel mark after the International Energy Agency raised its forecasts for global demand. The IEA warned demand for Opec's crude in the first quarter would outstrip supply. The price increase was also driven by weaker Russian oil giant Yukos and lower US crude supplies.

Title: UK firm faces Venezuelan land row
Article_Text: Venezuelan authorities have said they will seize land owned by a British company as part of President Chavez's agrarian reform programme.  Officials in Cojedes state said on Friday that farmland owned...
Summary: Venezuelan authorities plan to seize land owned by the Vestey Group as part of President Chavez's agrarian reform programme, citing idle large rural estates. The government claims the company does not possess valid documents proving its ownership of the land. The Vestey Group insists it has complied with Venezuelan law and will cooperate with the authorities.

Title: Soaring oil 'hits world economy'
Article_Text: The soaring cost of oil has hit global economic growth, although world's major economies should weather the storm of price rises, according to the OECD.  In its latest bi-annual report, the OECD cut i...
Summary: The OECD has cut its growth predictions for major economies due to soaring oil costs, but believes the global economy can regain momentum. Global growth is forecast to reach 3.6% in 2004 and 2.9% in 2005. A dip in oil prices and improving jobs prospects are expected to boost consumer confidence and spending.

Title: Irish markets reach all-time high
Article_Text: Irish shares have risen to a record high, with investors persuaded to buy into the market by low inflation and strong growth forecasts.  The ISEQ index of leading shares closed up 23 points to 6661.89...
Summary: Irish shares have reached a record high, driven by low inflation and strong growth forecasts, with the ISEQ index closing up 23 points to 6661.89. Several major companies, including Allied Irish Banks and Bank of Ireland, saw their market value hit recent highs. Analysts attribute the growth to benign economic conditions and a discount valuation compared to European markets.

Title: Japanese banking battle at an end
Article_Text: Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Financial has withdrawn its takeover offer for rival bank UFJ Holdings, enabling the latter to merge with Mitsubishi Tokyo.  Sumitomo bosses told counterparts at UFJ of its dec...
Summary: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial has withdrawn its takeover offer for UFJ Holdings, allowing the latter to merge with Mitsubishi Tokyo Financial Group. The deal would create the world's biggest bank with assets of about 189 trillion yen. Sumitomo's exit ends the most high-profile fight in Japanese bank history.

Title: Rich grab half Colombia poor fund
Article_Text: Half of the money put aside by the Colombian government to help the country's poor is benefiting people who do not need it, a study has found.  A total of 24.2 trillion pesos ($10.2bn; £5.5bn) is earm...
Summary: A study found that half of the Colombian government's subsidies for the poor are benefiting the wealthy, rather than those in need. The government aims to reduce poverty levels from 53% to 36% with a better distribution of cash. The study's findings suggest that revising government expenditure in areas such as pensions and public services could help.

Title: Rover deal 'may cost 2,000 jobs'
Article_Text: Some 2,000 jobs at MG Rover's Midlands plant may be cut if investment in the firm by a Chinese car maker goes ahead, the Financial Times has reported.  Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp plans to shift...
Summary: A Chinese car maker, Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp, plans to shift production of the Rover 25 to China and export it to the UK, potentially leading to 2,000 job cuts at MG Rover's Midlands plant. The deal, worth £1bn, is seen as Rover's last chance to save its Longbridge plant. Rover bosses are confident the deal will be signed in March or early April.

Title: Ad firm WPP's profits surge 15%
Article_Text: UK advertising giant WPP has posted larger-than-expected annual profits and predicted that it will outperform the market in 2005.  Pre-tax profits rose 15% from a year ago to reach £546m ($1.04bn), ah...
Summary: UK advertising giant WPP has posted larger-than-expected annual profits and predicted that it will outperform the market in 2005. Pre-tax profits rose 15% from a year ago to reach £546m ($1.04bn). The company also predicted that it will buy the NOP World market research unit for up to £350m.

Title: US gives foreign firms extra time
Article_Text: Foreign firms have been given an extra year to meet tough new corporate governance regulations imposed by the US stock market watchdog.  The Securities and Exchange Commission has extended the deadlin...
Summary: The US Securities and Exchange Commission has extended the deadline for foreign firms to meet corporate governance regulations until July 15, 2006, in response to protests from European and other business leaders. The new rules, part of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, require firms to certify their financial reporting in line with US rules. The SEC has taken into consideration the fact that foreign companies are already working to meet more onerous financial reporting rules in their home countries.

Title: Japanese mogul arrested for fraud
Article_Text: One of Japan's best-known businessmen was arrested on Thursday on charges of falsifying shareholder information and selling shares based on the false data.  Yoshiaki Tsutsumi was once ranked as the wo...
Summary: Yoshiaki Tsutsumi, Japan's former richest man, was arrested on charges of falsifying shareholder information and selling shares based on false data. He was once a powerful industrialist with close connections to politicians and was involved in several high-profile business scandals. Tsutsumi faces criminal charges and the possibility of a prison sentence.

Title: Deutsche Telekom sees mobile gain
Article_Text: German telecoms firm Deutsche Telekom saw strong fourth quarter profits on the back of upbeat US mobile earnings and better-than-expected asset sales.  Net profit came in at 1.4bn euros (£960m; $1.85b...
Summary: Deutsche Telekom reported strong fourth quarter profits driven by upbeat US mobile earnings and better-than-expected asset sales. Net profit rose to 1.4bn euros, while sales increased 2.8% to 14.96bn euros. The company also reduced debt to 35.8bn euros.

Title: Chinese wine tempts Italy's Illva
Article_Text: Italy's Illva Saronno has agreed to buy 33% of Changyu, the largest wine maker in China.  Changyu said in a statement to the Shenzhen stock exchange that Illva will pay 481.42m yuan ($58.16m; £30.7m),...
Summary: Italy's Illva Saronno has agreed to buy 33% of Changyu, the largest wine maker in China, for 481.42m yuan. The deal is subject to government approval. Chinese wine sales are growing, with sales in 2003 up 25% at 61.1bn yuan.

Title: Umbro profits lifted by Euro 2004
Article_Text: UK sportswear firm Umbro has posted a 222% rise in annual profit after sales of replica England football kits were boosted by the Euro 2004 tournament.  Pre-tax profit for 2004 was £15.4m ($29.4m). Um...
Summary: UK sportswear firm Umbro has posted a 222% rise in annual profit after sales of replica England football kits were boosted by the Euro 2004 tournament. The company has signed a new four-year agreement with Scottish club Rangers and plans to grow sales both in the UK and internationally.

Title: Fed chief warning on US deficit
Article_Text: Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan has warned that allowing huge US budget deficits to continue could have "severe" consequences.  Speaking to the House Budget Committee he urged Congress to take...
Summary: Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan warned of severe consequences if huge US budget deficits continue, urging Congress to cut the deficit by increasing taxes or changing promised benefits for retirees. The US economy is growing, but budget concerns are clouding the outlook. Greenspan called on Congress to reinstate offsetting rules to prevent further deficits.

Title: UK Coal plunges into deeper loss
Article_Text: Shares in UK Coal have fallen after the mining group reported losses had deepened to £51.6m in 2004 from £1.2m.  The UK's biggest coal producer blamed geological problems, industrial action and "opera...
Summary: Shares in UK Coal have fallen after the company reported deeper losses, blaming geological problems, industrial action, and operating flaws. The company hopes to return to profit in 2006 and has introduced new wage structures and maintenance regimes to improve earnings. UK Coal operates 15 mines across the UK.

Title: Saudi ministry to employ women
Article_Text: Women will be employed in Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry for the first time this year, Foreign Minister Prince Saud Al-Faisal has been reported as saying.  The move comes as the conservative country ...
Summary: Saudi Arabia is hiring women for the first time in its foreign ministry, according to Foreign Minister Prince Saud Al-Faisal. The move comes as the country opens up to working women, despite slow progress. Women now make up over half of university graduates but only 5% of the workforce.

Title: Japan economy slides to recession
Article_Text: The Japanese economy has officially gone back into recession for the fourth time in a decade.  Gross domestic product fell by 0.1% in the last three months of 2004. The fall reflects weak exports and ...
Summary: The Japanese economy has officially gone back into recession for the fourth time in a decade, with a 0.1% decline in the last three months of 2004. The government revised growth figures, citing weak exports and a slowdown in consumer spending. Despite the disappointing figures, politicians remain optimistic about an economic boost later in the year.

Title: US crude prices surge above $53
Article_Text: US crude prices have soared to fresh four-month highs above $53 in the US as refinery problems propelled petrol prices to an all-time high.  US light sweet crude futures jumped to $53.09 a barrel in N...
Summary: US crude prices have reached fresh four-month highs above $53, driven by refinery problems, particularly a fire at Western Refining Company's refinery in Texas, which shut down petrol production. The surge in US gasoline futures to a record high of $1.4850 a gallon has also contributed to the price increase. The market's sensitivity to petrol production issues is heightened as the approach to Spring anticipates rising demand for fuel ahead of the holiday season.

Title: Industrial output falls in Japan
Article_Text: Japanese industrial output fell in October while unemployment rose, casting further doubt on the strength of the country's economic recovery.  Production dropped 1.6% in October, reflecting a decline ...
Summary: Japanese industrial output fell 1.6% in October due to a decline in exports, while unemployment rose 0.1% to 4.7%. The economy has grown for six quarters but growth slowed in the last quarter amid weaker global demand. Japan's government remains optimistic due to strong domestic demand.
Key_Entities: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry

Title: Ryanair in $4bn Boeing plane deal
Article_Text: Budget airline Ryanair has placed an order for 70 Boeing 737-800 planes, in a deal valued at $4bn (£2.1bn) which should lead to 2,500 new Ryanair jobs.  It also has an option for a further 70 aircraft...
Summary: Ryanair has ordered 70 Boeing 737-800 planes worth $4bn, which should lead to 2,500 new jobs. The new planes will help the airline cut operating costs further. Ryanair expects unit operating costs to fall each year for the next five years.

Title: Parmalat to return to stockmarket
Article_Text: Parmalat, the Italian dairy company which went bust after an accounting scandal, hopes to be back on the Italian stock exchange in July.  The firm gained protection from creditors in 2003 after reveal...
Summary: Parmalat, the Italian dairy company, aims to re-list on the Italian stock exchange in July after gaining protection from creditors in 2003. The company's re-listing plan involves converting creditors' debts into shares through two new share issues. Creditors will vote on the plan later this year.

Title: BMW cash to fuel Mini production
Article_Text: Less than four years after the new Mini was launched, German car maker BMW has announced £100m of new investment.  Some 200 new jobs are to be created at the Oxford factory, including modernised machi...
Summary: BMW has announced £100m of new investment in its Oxford factory, creating 200 new jobs and potentially increasing car production to over 200,000. The investment is a response to rising demand and could help reduce waiting lists. The company has invested £280m in Mini production since its launch in 2001.

Title: Bad weather hits Nestle sales
Article_Text: A combination of bad weather, rising raw material costs and the sluggish European economy has hit sales at Swiss food and drink giant Nestle.  Revenue dipped 1.4% to 86.7bn Swiss francs ($74.6bn; £39....
Summary: Nestle's revenue dipped 1.4% to 86.7bn Swiss francs in 2004 due to bad weather and rising raw material costs, but profits margins were boosted by strong performance in the Americas and China. The company plans to raise its dividend and buy back shares. Nestle forecasts organic earnings growth of 5% in 2005.

Title: Fiat mulls Ferrari market listing
Article_Text: Ferrari could be listed on the stock market as part of an overhaul of Fiat's carmaking operations, the Financial Times has reported.  It said Fiat was set to restructure its business after reaching a ...
Summary: Fiat is considering restructuring its carmaking operations, which could include listing Ferrari on the stock market, as part of a settlement with GM. The company is making a loss despite strong sales of Alfa Romeo. Fiat may transfer Maserati to its Alfa Romeo division to exploit commercial synergies.

Title: Italy to get economic action plan
Article_Text: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi will unveil plans aimed at kickstarting the country's sputtering economy on Thursday night in Rome.  He will present an "Action Plan for the Development of Ita...
Summary: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi will unveil an 'Action Plan for the Development of Italy' to kickstart the country's economy, focusing on boosting R&D spending, competitiveness of small firms, and bankruptcy laws. The government aims to tackle the problems hindering Italy's entrepreneurial spirit and growth. The plan includes measures to open up markets, infrastructure, research, and making incentives available.

Title: Weak dollar hits Reuters
Article_Text: Revenues at media group Reuters slipped 11% during 2004, mainly due to the weakness of the dollar, the group said.  The company said it was optimistic about growth even as revenues slipped 11% from £3...
Summary: Reuters reported a 11% decline in revenues to £2.89bn in 2004, mainly due to the weakness of the dollar, but beat profit forecasts and cut debt. The company is optimistic about growth and expects further gradual improvement in the second quarter. It plans to deliver £105m of savings over the coming year.

Title: Hyundai to build new India plant
Article_Text: South Korea's Hyundai Motor has announced that it plans to build a second plant in India to meet the country's growing demand for cars.  The company didn't give details of its investment but it said t...
Summary: Hyundai Motor plans to build a second plant in India to meet growing demand for cars, with the new plant expected to produce 150,000 cars a year. The move is expected to boost annual production capacity to 400,000 units and drive sales growth to 250,000 in 2005 and 400,000 by 2010. The new plant will be built near the existing one in Chennai, Tamil Nadu.

Title: SA unveils 'more for all' budget
Article_Text: The South African government has put tax cuts and increased social spending at the centre of its latest budget.  Aiming to both stir economic growth and aid the country's poor, finance minister Trevor...
Summary: The South African government has unveiled a budget with tax cuts and increased social spending, aiming to stimulate economic growth and aid the poor. Finance minister Trevor Manuel said the focus is on benefiting all South Africans, not just a few. The budget includes cuts in corporate and personal taxes, as well as increases in spending on health, education, and housing.

Title: BMW drives record sales in Asia
Article_Text: BMW has forecast sales growth of at least 10% in Asia this year after registering record sales there in 2004.  The luxury carmaker saw strong sales of its three marques - BMW, Mini and Rolls-Royce - i...
Summary: BMW has forecast sales growth of at least 10% in Asia this year, building on record sales in 2004. The company is launching a revamped 3-Series saloon class and aims to boost annual sales in Asia to 150,000 by 2008. BMW is confident about its prospects in the region despite a 16% sales decline in China last year.

Title: Economy 'stronger than forecast'
Article_Text: The UK economy probably grew at a faster rate in the third quarter than the 0.4% reported, according to Bank of England deputy governor Rachel Lomax.  Private sector business surveys suggest a stronge...
Summary: The UK economy likely grew faster than the 0.4% reported in the third quarter, according to Bank of England deputy governor Rachel Lomax. Private sector surveys suggest a stronger economy, while official data shows a rapid slowdown in UK house price growth. The Bank of England is calling for faster delivery of data to make more effective policy decisions.
Key_Entities: House of Lords Economic Affairs Committee

Title: Electrolux to export Europe jobs
Article_Text: Electrolux saw its shares rise 14% on Tuesday after it said it would be shifting more of its manufacturing to low-cost countries.  The Swedish firm, the world's largest maker of home appliances, said ...
Summary: Electrolux's shares rose 14% after the company announced it would relocate 10 of its 27 plants in western Europe and North America to Asia, eastern Europe, and Mexico. The company is speeding up its restructuring programme to save £190m-£265m annually. Electrolux plans to spin-off its outdoor products unit into a new separate company.

Title: Worldcom ex-boss launches defence
Article_Text: Lawyers defending former WorldCom chief Bernie Ebbers against a battery of fraud charges have called a company whistleblower as their first witness.  Cynthia Cooper, WorldCom's ex-head of internal acc...
Summary: Cynthia Cooper, a former WorldCom executive, testified that external auditors Arthur Andersen approved WorldCom's accounting practices, and that former CEO Bernie Ebbers was unaware of the fraud. Cooper's testimony contradicts that of former financial chief Scott Sullivan, who said Ebbers ordered accounting adjustments. Ebbers faces 85 years in jail if convicted.

Title: Insurance bosses plead guilty
Article_Text: Another three US insurance executives have pleaded guilty to fraud charges stemming from an ongoing investigation into industry malpractice.  Two executives from American International Group (AIG) and...
Summary: Nine US insurance executives have pleaded guilty to fraud charges in an investigation led by New York attorney general Eliot Spitzer

Title: Further rise in UK jobless total
Article_Text: The UK's jobless total rose for the second month in a row in December, official figures show.  The number of people out of work rose 32,000 to 1.41 million in the last three months of 2004, even as 90...
Summary: The UK's jobless total rose for the second month in a row in December, with 1.41 million people out of work, while average earnings rose 4.3% in the year to December. The manufacturing sector continued to suffer, with 104,000 workers axed during the last quarter of 2004. Analysts forecast that the Bank of England will raise rates this year.

Title: Wembley firm won't make a profit
Article_Text: Shares in Multiplex Group, which is building the new Wembley stadium, fell as much as 19% after it said it would not make any money on the project.  The Australian firm said it would only break even o...
Summary: Shares in Multiplex Group fell 19% after the company announced it would not make a profit on the new Wembley stadium project due to increased costs. The company cut profit targets for the project and expects to break even on the £458m rebuild. Multiplex will have to win legal claims against subcontractors to recoup any profit.

Title: Cars pull down US retail figures
Article_Text: US retail sales fell 0.3% in January, the biggest monthly decline since last August, driven down by a heavy fall in car sales.  The 3.3% fall in car sales had been expected, coming after December's 4%...
Summary: US retail sales fell 0.3% in January, driven down by a heavy fall in car sales, but excluding the car sector, sales were up 0.6%. Sales are expected to rise in 2005, but at a slower rate than in 2004. Consumer spending remains strong, according to analysts.

Title: Lufthansa may sue over Bush visit
Article_Text: German airline Lufthansa may sue federal agencies for damages after the arrival of US president George W Bush disrupted flights.  Lufthansa said that it may lose millions of euros as a result of Air F...
Summary: German airline Lufthansa may sue federal agencies for damages after US President George W Bush's arrival disrupted flights at Frankfurt airport, causing millions of euros in potential losses.

Title: EU aiming to fuel development aid
Article_Text: European Union finance ministers meet on Thursday to discuss proposals, including a tax on jet fuel, to boost development aid for poorer nations.  The policy makers are to ask for a report into how mo...
Summary: European Union finance ministers will discuss proposals to boost development aid for poorer nations, including a tax on jet fuel, at a meeting on Thursday. The plan aims to increase aid to 0.7% of annual gross national income by 2015. Airlines have opposed the proposal, citing industry pressures.

Title: German business confidence slides
Article_Text: German business confidence fell in February knocking hopes of a speedy recovery in Europe's largest economy.  Munich-based research institute Ifo said that its confidence index fell to 95.5 in Februar...
Summary: German business confidence fell to 95.5 in February, its first decline in three months, due to a weak domestic economy and reluctance of consumers to spend. The outlook in manufacturing and retail sectors worsened. Despite the decline, the economy minister expects a modest economic upswing to continue.

Title: FAO warns on impact of subsidies
Article_Text: Billions of farmers' livelihoods are at risk from falling commodity prices and protectionism, the UN's Food & Agriculture Organisation has warned.  Trade barriers and subsidies "severely" distort the ...
Summary: The UN's Food & Agriculture Organisation has warned that billions of farmers' livelihoods are at risk due to falling commodity prices and protectionism, leading to food insecurity for 2.5 billion people in developing countries. The FAO report criticises high tariffs and subsidies, recommending that developing countries reduce their own tariffs to encourage trade. Global agricultural subsidies exceed $300bn annually.

Title: India seeks to boost construction
Article_Text: India has cleared a proposal allowing up to 100% foreign direct investment in its construction sector.  Kamal Nath, Commerce and Industry Minister, announced the decision in Delhi on Thursday followin...
Summary: India has cleared a proposal allowing up to 100% foreign direct investment in its construction sector, aiming to boost foreign investment in other sectors and create employment for construction workers. The government hopes the new policy will benefit steel and brick-making industries. Foreign investors will be allowed to develop a smaller area of land they acquire, with a minimum construction area of 50,000 square meters.

Title: Boeing unveils new 777 aircraft
Article_Text: US aircraft firm Boeing has unveiled its new long-distance 777 plane, as it tries to regain its position as the industry's leading manufacturer.  The 777-200LR will be capable of flying almost 11,000 ...
Summary: Boeing has unveiled its new long-distance 777 plane, the 777-200LR, which can fly almost 11,000 miles non-stop, linking cities such as London and Sydney. The company hopes airlines will prefer smaller aircraft over longer distances. Boeing plans to offer twin-engine planes that can fly direct to many airports, eliminating the need for connecting flights.

Title: Circuit City gets takeover offer
Article_Text: Circuit City Stores, the second-largest electronics retailer in the US, has received a $3.25bn (£1.7bn) takeover offer.  The bid has come from Boston-based private investment firm Highfields Capital M...
Summary: Circuit City Stores has received a $3.25bn takeover offer from Boston-based private investment firm Highfields Capital Management, which already owns 6.7% of the company's shares. The bid aims to take the Virginia-based firm private, eliminating public transparency. Shares in the retailer rose 19.6% following the announcement.

Title: Japan turns to beer alternatives
Article_Text: Japanese brewers are increasingly making money from beer-flavoured drinks rather than beer itself  Beer and spirits are heavily taxed in Japan, driving breweries to search for alternatives. Japan's lo...
Summary: Japanese breweries are shifting focus to beer-flavoured drinks due to high taxes on beer and spirits, with market growth predicted to reach 84% this year. Asahi Breweries is launching a new drink called Shinnama, while Sapporo and Suntory already have established products in the market. Happoshu, a low-cost beer alternative, has been a mainstay of brewery profits for years.

Title: S Korean consumers spending again
Article_Text: South Korea looks set to sustain its revival thanks to renewed private consumption, its central bank says.  The country's economy has suffered from an overhang of personal debt after its consumers' cr...
Summary: South Korea's economy is expected to recover due to increased private consumption, with credit card spending rising 14.8% year-on-year. The central bank has kept interest rates low to support the economy, citing improved consumer confidence and retail sales. Economic growth is predicted to reach 4% this year.

Title: German growth goes into reverse
Article_Text: Germany's economy shrank 0.2% in the last three months of 2004, upsetting hopes of a sustained recovery.  The figures confounded hopes of a 0.2% expansion in the fourth quarter in Europe's biggest eco...
Summary: Germany's economy shrank 0.2% in the last three months of 2004, contradicting hopes of a sustained recovery. The country's growth for the whole of 2004 was 1.6%, down from an earlier estimate of 1.7%. Germany's economy has been reliant on exports to recover, but rising euro values have depressed competitiveness.

Title: Turkey-Iran mobile deal 'at risk'
Article_Text: Turkey's investment in Iran's mobile industry looks set to be scrapped after its biggest mobile firm saw its investment there slashed by MPs.  Iran's parliament voted by a large majority to cut Turkce...
Summary: Turkey's investment in Iran's mobile industry may be scrapped after Iran's parliament slashed Turkcell's stake in a new mobile network on national security grounds. The move follows an earlier vote by MPs to give themselves a veto over foreign investments. Turkcell has expressed concerns about the decision.

Title: EU ministers to mull jet fuel tax
Article_Text: European Union finance ministers are meeting on Thursday in Brussels, where they are to discuss a controversial jet fuel tax.  A levy on jet fuel has been suggested as a way to raise funds to finance ...
Summary: European Union finance ministers are meeting to discuss a proposed jet fuel tax to raise funds for poverty reduction, despite opposition from airlines and aviation bodies. The EU has promised to consult with airlines before implementing the tax. Ministers will also discuss regulations governing European public spending.

Title: Palestinian economy in decline
Article_Text: Despite a short-lived increase in Palestinian jobs in 2003, the economy is performing well below its potential, said a World Bank report.  Unemployment stood at 25%, compared with 10% before the upris...
Summary: A World Bank report states that the Palestinian economy is performing below its potential, with high unemployment rates and a close link between closures and economic problems. The report attributes last year's 6% growth rate to a brief easing of violence and closures. The Palestinian Authority is urged to revive its reform programme and maintain financial discipline.

Title: China had role in Yukos split-up
Article_Text: China lent Russia $6bn (£3.2bn) to help the Russian government renationalise the key Yuganskneftegas unit of oil group Yukos, it has been revealed.  The Kremlin said on Tuesday that the $6bn which Rus...
Summary: China lent Russia $6bn to help the Russian government renationalise the key Yuganskneftegas unit of oil group Yukos, and Rosneft signed a long-term oil supply deal with China's CNPC. The deal sees Rosneft receive $6bn in credits from China's CNPC to pay off loans. The Chinese decision might have been influenced by the possibility of litigation from Yukos, Yugosk's former owner.

Title: Deadline nears for Fiat-GM deal
Article_Text: Fiat and General Motors (GM) have until midnight on 1 February to settle a disagreement over a potential takeover.  The deadline marks the point at which Fiat will gain the right to sell its car divis...
Summary: Fiat and General Motors have a deadline to settle a disagreement over a potential takeover, with Fiat gaining the right to sell its car division to GM if no agreement is reached. GM is offering $2bn to extricate itself from the arrangement. Fiat's finance arm was sold, halving GM's stake in the company.

Title: ID theft surge hits US consumers
Article_Text: Almost a quarter of a million US consumers complained of being targeted for identity theft in 2004, official figures suggest.  The Federal Trade Commission said two in five of the 635,173 reports it h...
Summary: Almost a quarter of a million US consumers complained of being targeted for identity theft in 2004, with the total cost of fraud reported by consumers being $546m. Identity theft was the top table for the fifth year in a row. The biggest slice of ID fraud cases concerned abuses of people's credit. Internet auctions were the second biggest source of fraud complaints.

Title: Argentina, Venezuela in oil deal
Article_Text: Argentina and Venezuela have extended a food-for-oil deal, which helped the former to overcome a severe energy crisis last year.  Argentine President Nestor Kirchner and Venezuelan President Hugo Chav...
Summary: Argentina and Venezuela have extended a food-for-oil deal to prevent another energy crisis, while also formalizing a co-operation deal between energy firms and agreeing to create a Latin American television network.

Title: BMW to recall faulty diesel cars
Article_Text: BMW is to recall all cars equipped with a faulty diesel fuel-injection pump supplied by parts maker Robert Bosch.  The faulty part does not represent a safety risk and the recall only affects pumps ma...
Summary: BMW is recalling all cars with faulty diesel fuel-injection pumps supplied by Robert Bosch, which do not pose a safety risk. The recall affects pumps made in December and January, with a potential production loss of up to 3,600 vehicles. Bosch expects to restart production of the part by 2 February.

Title: Takeover rumour lifts Exel shares
Article_Text: Shares in storage and delivery firm Exel closed up 9% at a two-and-a-half year high on Tuesday on speculation it is to receive an imminent takeover bid.  The talk in the City is that US giant United P...
Summary: Shares in Exel closed up 9% at a two-and-a-half year high on speculation of an imminent takeover bid, with US giant UPS and Deutsche Post mentioned as likely bidders.

Title: Yukos accused of lying to court
Article_Text: Russian oil firm Yukos lied to a US court in an attempt to stop the Russian government selling off its key production unit, the court has heard.  The unit, Yugansk, was sold to pay off a $27.5bn (£14....
Summary: A US court heard that Russian oil firm Yukos lied to the court in an attempt to stop the sale of its key production unit, Yugansk, to pay off a $27.5bn back tax bill. The sale went ahead despite an order to stop it, and the unit was eventually sold to state-controlled oil firm Rosneft for $9.4bn. Yukos is suing several companies and the Russian government for their role in the sale.

Title: Mexican in US send $16bn home
Article_Text: Mexican labourers living in the US sent a record $16.6bn (£8.82bn) home last year.  The Bank of Mexico said that remittances grew 24% last year and now represent the country's second-biggest source of...
Summary: Mexican labourers living in the US sent a record $16.6bn home last year, with remittances growing 24% and now representing the country's second-biggest source of income after oil. The growth is attributed to better records and greater prosperity of Mexican expatriates in the US. Remittances now account for over 2% of the country's GDP.

Title: Home loan approvals rising again
Article_Text: The number of mortgages approved in the UK has risen for the first time since May last year, according to lending figures from the Bank of England.  New loans in December rose to 83,000, slightly high...
Summary: Mortgage lending in the UK rose in December, contradicting a survey that said approvals were at a five-year low, and may indicate the market is stabilizing but still experiencing house price softness.

Title: Manufacturing recovery 'slowing'
Article_Text: UK manufacturing grew at its slowest pace in one-and-a-half years in January, according to a survey.  The Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply (CIPS) said its purchasing manager index (PMI) fe...
Summary: UK manufacturing grew at its slowest pace in one-and-a-half years in January, according to a survey, with the PMI falling to 51.8 from 53.3 in December. The strong pound and rising oil and metals prices had kept costs high. The sector's employment index fell to 48.3, its lowest level since June 2003.
Key_Entities: Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply

Title: Worldcom boss 'left books alone'
Article_Text: Former Worldcom boss Bernie Ebbers, who is accused of overseeing an $11bn (£5.8bn) fraud, never made accounting decisions, a witness has told jurors.  David Myers made the comments under questioning b...
Summary: A witness testified that Bernie Ebbers, former Worldcom CEO, never made accounting decisions, as defence lawyers try to distance him from the allegations of $11bn fraud. Ebbers' team aims to portray him as an affable boss, while prosecutors claim he was responsible for hiding losses to protect shares. Ebbers faces a substantial jail sentence if found guilty.

Title: Metlife buys up Citigroup insurer
Article_Text: US banking giant Citigroup has sold its Travelers Life & Annuity insurance arm to Metlife for $11.5bn (£6.1bn).  The sale is a further move by Citigroup away from its 1990s strategy of offering every ...
Summary: Citigroup has sold its Travelers Life & Annuity insurance arm to Metlife for $11.5bn, a move to focus on other businesses. The sale gives Metlife access to a larger distribution network. The deal includes Smith Barney retail brokerages and Citibank branches.

Title: Europe blames US over weak dollar
Article_Text: European leaders have openly blamed the US for the sharp rise in the value of the euro.  US officials were talking up the dollar, they said, but failing to take action to back up their words. Meeting ...
Summary: European leaders have blamed the US for the rise in the value of the euro, citing concerns that it's harming exports. The dollar is near an all-time low, and US officials have been accused of not backing up their words. European leaders are calling for action to address the issue.

Title: French wine gets 70m euro top-up
Article_Text: The French government is to hand its struggling wine industry 70m euros ($91m) in aid to help it battle falling sales and damaging overproduction.  The financial package is aimed at assisting vintners...
Summary: The French government is providing 70m euros in aid to its struggling wine industry to help it battle falling sales and overproduction. The package includes preferential loans and funding to promote French wine abroad. However, wine makers and farmers expressed disappointment with the support.

Title: Russia gets investment blessing
Article_Text: Soaring oil sales and a budget surplus mean Russian debt is no longer a risky investment, one of the world's leading credit rating agencies says.  Standard & Poor's has classed Russian bonds as "inves...
Summary: Russian debt is no longer considered a risky investment, with Standard & Poor's classifying Russian bonds as 'investment grade'. The country's government finances are solid, outweighing the risk, and it is now a net creditor. The improved rating reflects the government's growing tax revenues from energy sales.

Title: Iranian MPs threaten mobile deal
Article_Text: Turkey's biggest private mobile firm could bail out of a $3bn ($1.6bn) deal to build a network in Iran after MPs there slashed its stake in the project.  Conservatives in parliament say Turkcell's sta...
Summary: Turkey's biggest private mobile firm, Turkcell, may give up on a $3bn deal to build a network in Iran after MPs slashed its stake in the project from 70% to 49%. The deal was signed in September, but a parliamentary commission has ruled that Turkcell's stake is too high due to alleged business ties with Israel.

Title: Argentina closes $102.6bn debt swap
Article_Text: Argentina is set to close its $102.6bn (£53.51bn) debt restructuring offer for bondholders later on Friday, with the government hopeful that most creditors will accept the deal.  The estimated loss to...
Summary: Argentina is closing its $102.6bn debt restructuring offer for bondholders, with most creditors expected to accept the deal. The offer includes an estimated loss of up to 70% of the original bond value. The government hopes the deal will enhance the country's credibility and attract more foreign investment.

Title: US economy shows solid GDP growth
Article_Text: The US economy has grown more than expected, expanding at an annual rate of 3.8% in the last quarter of 2004.  The gross domestic product figure was ahead of the 3.1% the government estimated a month ...
Summary: The US economy expanded at an annual rate of 3.8% in the last quarter of 2004, beating the government's estimate of 3.1%. The growth was driven by stronger spending on capital equipment and a smaller-than-expected trade deficit. The GDP figure also topped economists' forecast of 3.5% growth.

Title: Profits slide at India's Dr Reddy
Article_Text: Profits at Indian drugmaker Dr Reddy's fell 93% as research costs rose and sales flagged.  The firm said its profits were 40m rupees ($915,000; £486,000) for the three months to December on sales whic...
Summary: Dr Reddy's Indian drugmaker reported a 93% fall in profits due to rising research costs and declining sales. The company's sales fell 8% to 4.7bn rupees, with its generics business also experiencing a 8.6% decline. Research and development spending rose 37% to 705m rupees.

Title: Burren awarded Egyptian contracts
Article_Text: British energy firm Burren Energy has been awarded two potentially lucrative oil exploration contracts in Egypt.  The company successfully bid for the two contracts, granted by government owned oil fi...
Summary: British energy firm Burren Energy has been awarded two oil exploration contracts in Egypt, expanding its global portfolio. The company has a presence in Egypt and recently acquired a stake in an Indian oil firm. Burren Energy also holds contracts in Turkmenistan and the Republic of Congo.

Title: 'Strong dollar' call halts slide
Article_Text: The US dollar's slide against the euro and yen has halted after US Treasury Secretary John Snow said a strong dollar was "in America's interest".  But analysts said any gains are likely to be short-li...
Summary: The US dollar's slide against the euro and yen has halted after US Treasury Secretary John Snow said a strong dollar was in America's interest, but analysts say gains are likely to be short-lived due to significant US economic problems.

Title: IMF 'cuts' German growth estimate
Article_Text: The International Monetary Fund is to cut its 2005 growth forecast for the German economy from 1.8% to 0.8%, the Financial Times Deutschland reported.  The IMF will also reduce its growth estimate for...
Summary: The International Monetary Fund is reducing its growth forecast for the German economy from 1.8% to 0.8% and for the eurozone economy from 2.2% to 1.6%. The German economy has been faltering due to high unemployment levels and weak demand. The IMF's draft World Economic Outlook highlights a marked deterioration in Germany's economy.
Key_Entities: European Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development

Title: GM, Ford cut output as sales fall
Article_Text: US car firms General Motors (GM) and Ford have been forced to cut production in the face of falling car sales.  US sales at GM sank 12.7% in February compared to a year ago while Ford sales dropped 3%...
Summary: US car firms General Motors and Ford have cut production due to falling car sales, with Asian carmakers like Toyota and Nissan performing well. Sales across the industry fell to 1.25 million vehicles, with high fuel prices blamed for low sales of big trucks and SUVs. Foreign rivals gained market share, while Chrysler was the only Detroit-based automaker to see an increase in sales.

Title: Ebbers denies WorldCom fraud
Article_Text: Former WorldCom chief Bernie Ebbers has denied claims that he knew accountants were doctoring the books at the firm.  Speaking in court, Mr Ebbers rejected allegations he pressured ex-chief financial ...
Summary: Former WorldCom CEO Bernie Ebbers denied allegations that he pressured CFO Scott Sullivan to falsify company financial statements, downplaying their working relationship and claiming Sullivan made accounting decisions on his own.

Title: Australia rates at four year high
Article_Text: Australia is raising its benchmark interest rate to its highest level in four years despite signs of a slowdown in the country's economy.  The Reserve Bank of Australia lifted interest rates 0.25% to ...
Summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised interest rates 0.25% to 5.5%, its first move in over a year, to curb inflation, despite signs of a slowdown in the economy. The move was criticized by some analysts, who pointed to a decline in economic growth in the last quarter. Consumer spending remains strong, but inflationary pressures are a concern.

Title: US company admits Benin bribery
Article_Text: A US defence and telecommunications company has agreed to pay $28.5m after admitting bribery in the West African state of Benin.  The Titan corporation was accused of funnelling more than $2m into the...
Summary: US defence and telecommunications company Titan has agreed to pay $28.5m after admitting bribery in Benin. The company pleaded guilty to falsifying accounts and violating US anti-bribery laws. Titan agreed to pay $13m in criminal penalties and $15.5m to settle a civil lawsuit.

Title: US insurer Marsh cuts 2,500 jobs
Article_Text: Up to 2,500 jobs are to go at US insurance broker Marsh & McLennan in a shake up following bigger-than-expected losses.  The insurer said the cuts were part of a cost-cutting drive, aimed at saving mi...
Summary: US insurance broker Marsh & McLennan is cutting up to 2,500 jobs as part of a cost-cutting drive following a $676m loss for the last three months of 2004. The company is also halving its dividend payment and spinning off its private equity unit. The layoffs are expected to lead to annual savings of more than $375m.

Title: US seeks new $280bn smoker ruling
Article_Text: The US Justice Department is to try to overturn a court ruling that threw out its claim for $280bn (£149bn) in damages from tobacco firms.  Earlier this month, a three-judge appeal court panel rejecte...
Summary: The US Justice Department plans to appeal a court ruling that rejected its claim for $280bn in damages from tobacco firms, which was filed in 1999 by the Clinton administration. The government argues that tobacco firms lied about the dangers of smoking and conspired to promote the habit. A three-judge panel rejected the claim, but the government will ask the full US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia to hear the case.
Key_Entities: US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia

Title: Budget Aston takes on Porsche
Article_Text: British car maker Aston Martin has gone head-to-head with Porsche's 911 sports cars with the launch of its cheapest model yet.  With a price tag under £80,000, the V8 Vantage is tens of thousands of p...
Summary: Aston Martin has launched its cheapest model, the V8 Vantage, priced under £80,000, with a waiting list for its more expensive DB9 model already 18 months long.

Title: Golden rule 'intact' says ex-aide
Article_Text: Chancellor Gordon Brown will meet his golden economic rule "with a margin to spare", according to his former chief economic adviser.  Formerly one of Mr Brown's closest Treasury aides, Ed Balls hinted...
Summary: Chancellor Gordon Brown will meet his golden economic rule with a margin to spare, according to his former chief economic adviser Ed Balls. Balls hinted at a Budget giveaway on 16 March, saying it would build on current tax credit rules. A rate rise ahead of the expected May election would not affect the Labour Party's chances of winning.

Title: Liberian economy starts to grow
Article_Text: The Liberian economy started to grow in 2004, but "sustained and deep reform efforts" are needed to ensure long term growth, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has said.  An IMF mission made the co...
Summary: The Liberian economy started to grow in 2004, with a 2% GDP increase, thanks to a strong recovery in rubber production and post-conflict reconstruction. However, the IMF remains cautious about a lack of transparency in government actions. The organization is calling for strengthened institutions and effective management of the national budget.

Title: Slowdown hits US factory growth
Article_Text: US industrial production increased for the 21st month in a row in February, but at a slower pace than in January, official figures show.  The Institute for Supply Management (ISM) index fell to 55.3 i...
Summary: US industrial production increased for the 21st month in a row in February, but at a slower pace than in January, according to official figures. The Institute for Supply Management (ISM) index fell to 55.3 in February, from an adjusted 56.4 in January. The sector's growth rate is slowing, but overall, the picture is improving.

Title: Lufthansa flies back to profit
Article_Text: German airline Lufthansa has returned to profit in 2004 after posting huge losses in 2003.  In a preliminary report, the airline announced net profits of 400m euros ($527.61m; £274.73m), compared with...
Summary: German airline Lufthansa has returned to profit in 2004 after posting huge losses in 2003, with net profits of 400m euros. The airline's operating profits were ten times more than in 2003. Lufthansa's recovery was despite tough competition and a dip in demand following the Iraq war and SARS virus.

Title: Japanese growth grinds to a halt
Article_Text: Growth in Japan evaporated in the three months to September, sparking renewed concern about an economy not long out of a decade-long trough.  Output in the period grew just 0.1%, an annual rate of 0.3...
Summary: Japan's economy experienced a 0.1% growth rate in the three months to September, falling short of expectations, but marking a sixth straight quarter of expansion. The growth was driven by domestic demand, but was hindered by faltering exports and corporate investment. The economy remains dependent on exports for its recovery.

Title: Unilever shake up as profit slips
Article_Text: Anglo-Dutch consumer goods giant Unilever is to merge its two management boards after reporting "unsatisfactory" earnings for 2004.  It blamed the poor results on sluggish decision making, a rise in d...
Summary: Unilever reported unsatisfactory earnings for 2004, citing sluggish decision making, a rise in discounted retailers, and a wet European summer. The company plans to merge its management boards and simplify its leadership structure to improve profits. Annual pre-tax profit fell 36% to 2.9bn euros.

Title: France Telecom gets Orange boost
Article_Text: Strong growth in subscriptions to mobile phone network Orange has helped boost profits at owner France Telecom.  Orange added more than five million new customers in 2004, leading to a 10% increase in...
Summary: France Telecom's profits rose 5.5% to 18.3bn euros in 2004, driven by strong growth in mobile phone subscriptions and broadband services. The company added 5.4 million new customers to Orange, its mobile network, and reduced its debt from 72bn euros to 43.9bn euros. France Telecom plans to buy out minority shareholders in data services provider Equant.

Title: Brussels raps mobile call charges
Article_Text: The European Commission has written to the mobile phone operators Vodafone and T-Mobile to challenge "the high rates" they charge for international roaming.  In letters sent to the two companies, the ...
Summary: The European Commission has written to mobile phone operators Vodafone and T-Mobile, challenging their high international roaming rates, alleging abuse of dominant market position in the German mobile phone market. Vodafone is already appealing against allegations of unfair and excessive UK roaming rates. The Commission aims to ensure European consumers are not overcharged when using their mobile phones abroad.

Title: WorldCom director admits lying
Article_Text: The former chief financial officer at US telecoms firm WorldCom has admitted before a New York court that he used to lie to fellow board members.  Speaking at the trial of his former boss Bernard Ebbe...
Summary: The former CFO of WorldCom, Scott Sullivan, has admitted to lying to fellow board members to cover up the company's financial hole, which was overstated by $11bn. Scott Sullivan is testifying against his former boss, Bernard Ebbers, who is on trial for fraud and conspiracy. Ebbers pleads not guilty and could face an 85-year sentence if convicted.

Title: Glaxo aims high after profit fall
Article_Text: GlaxoSmithKline saw its profits fall 9% last year to £6.2bn ($11.5bn), but Europe's biggest drugmaker says a recovery during 2005 is on the way.  Cheap copies of its drugs, particularly anti-depressan...
Summary: GlaxoSmithKline's profits fell 9% to £6.2bn in 2004 due to cheap copies of its drugs and a weak dollar, but the company expects a recovery in 2005 with its new drug pipeline.

Title: Japan bank shares up on link talk
Article_Text: Shares of Sumitomo Mitsui Financial (SMFG), and Daiwa Securities jumped amid speculation that two of Japan's biggest financial companies will merge.  Financial newspaper Nihon Keizai Shimbun claimed t...
Summary: Shares of Sumitomo Mitsui Financial and Daiwa Securities jumped amid speculation of a potential merger between the two Japanese financial companies. The firms have denied plans to merge, but are exploring ways to work more closely together. A combined company would have assets of over $1,000bn.

Title: Car giant hit by Mercedes slump
Article_Text: A slump in profitability at luxury car maker Mercedes has prompted a big drop in profits at parent DaimlerChrysler.  The German-US carmaker saw fourth quarter operating profits fall to 785m euros ($1b...
Summary: Mercedes-Benz's fourth quarter operating profits fell to 785m euros, while parent DaimlerChrysler's profits rose due to a strong performance from the Chrysler group. The company blamed high launch costs and losses from its Mercedes Smart mini-car range for the decline. DaimlerChrysler expects significant improvements in profitability in 2006.

Title: Ericsson sees earnings improve
Article_Text: Telecoms equipment supplier Ericsson has posted a rise in fourth quarter profits thanks to clients like Deutsche Telekom upgrade their networks.  Operating profit in the three months to 31 December wa...
Summary: Ericsson has posted a rise in fourth quarter profits due to clients upgrading their networks, but shares fell due to a lower-than-forecast profit margin. The company reported a 9% increase in sales for the quarter. Ericsson remains optimistic about its earnings outlook.

Title: Bank opts to leave rates on hold
Article_Text: The Bank of England has left interest rates on hold at 4.75% for a sixth month in a row.  The Bank's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) decided to take no action amid mixed signals from the economy. But ...
Summary: The Bank of England has left interest rates on hold at 4.75% for a sixth month, amid mixed signals from the economy. Economists predict a further rise in borrowing costs later this year, but the MPC is waiting for a clearer picture. Inflation has been rising faster than expected, hitting 1.6% in December.

Title: Nigeria to boost cocoa production
Article_Text: The government of Nigeria is hoping to triple cocoa production over the next three years with the launch of an ambitious development programme.  Agriculture Minister Adamu Bello said the scheme aimed ...
Summary: Nigeria aims to triple cocoa production to 600,000 tonnes by 2008 with a government-backed development programme, which includes subsidies for farming chemicals and seedlings. The programme also aims to encourage cocoa processing and local consumption. Ghana, the world's second-largest cocoa exporter, recently broke records with $1.2bn-worth of exports.

Title: US interest rates increased to 2%
Article_Text: US interest rates are to rise for the fourth time in five months, in a widely anticipated move.  The Federal Reserve has raised its key federal funds rate by a quarter percentage point to 2% in light ...
Summary: The Federal Reserve has raised its key federal funds rate by a quarter percentage point to 2% in light of mounting evidence that the US economy is regaining steam. US companies created twice as many jobs as expected in October, while exports hit record levels in September. Another rise could be in store for December, some economists warned.

Title: US bank in $515m SEC settlement
Article_Text: Five Bank of America subsidiaries have agreed to pay a total of $515m (£277m) to settle an investigation into fraudulent trading share practices.  The US Securities and Exchange Commission announced t...
Summary: Five Bank of America subsidiaries have agreed to pay $515m to settle an investigation into fraudulent trading share practices, with the SEC also bringing fraud charges against two ex-senior executives of Columbia Distributor.

Title: Train strike grips Buenos Aires
Article_Text: A strike on the Buenos Aires underground has caused traffic chaos and large queues at bus stops in the Argentine capital.  Tube workers walked out last week demanding a 53% pay rise and in protest aga...
Summary: A strike by Buenos Aires underground workers has caused traffic chaos and protests, with the workers demanding a 53% pay rise and opposing the installation of automatic ticket machines. The private firm Metrovias has offered an 8% increase in wages. The strike is ongoing, with the Argentine Work Ministry mediating the conflict.

Title: Bargain calls widen Softbank loss
Article_Text: Japanese communications firm Softbank has widened losses after heavy spending on a new cut-rate phone service.  The service, launched in December and dubbed "Otoku" or "bargain", has had almost 900,00...
Summary: Japanese communications firm Softbank has widened losses due to heavy spending on a new cut-rate phone service called Otoku, which has received almost 900,000 orders. The firm had an operating loss of 7.5bn yen in the three months to December. Softbank expects to move into profit in 2006 without the Otoku marketing spend.

Title: WMC profits up amid bid criticism
Article_Text: Australian mining firm WMC Resources has seen a fivefold rise in profits while continuing to be the target of a hostile takeover bid.  WMC said it made net profits of 1.33bn Australian dollars ($1bn; ...
Summary: Australian mining firm WMC Resources has seen a fivefold rise in profits to A$1.33bn in 2004, while facing a hostile takeover bid from Swiss Xstrata. The Australian government is reportedly against the deal, citing national interest grounds. WMC has spun off its aluminium operations to make itself a more attractive target.

Title: Barclays profits hit record level
Article_Text: Barclays, the UK's third-biggest bank, has seen annual pre-tax profits climb to record levels boosted by a sharp rise in business at its investment arm.  Profits for the year to 31 December rose 20% t...
Summary: Barclays' annual pre-tax profits rose 20% to a record £4.6bn, driven by a strong performance from its investment arm. The bank's UK retail business saw a 1% fall in profits due to margin pressure and spending on branches. Barclays' outlook for 2005 is positive, but growth may be slower due to softer economies and interest rate rises.

Title: Yukos owner sues Russia for $28bn
Article_Text: The majority owner of embattled Russian oil firm Yukos has sued the Russian government for $28.3bn (£15.2bn).  The Kremlin last year seized and sold Yukos' main production arm, Yugansk, to state-run o...
Summary: The majority owner of Yukos, Group Menatep, has sued the Russian government for $28.3bn, claiming the government's seizure of the company's main production arm, Yugansk, was illegal. The Russian government sold Yugansk to state-run oil group Rosneft to offset a massive back tax bill, but critics say this is part of an attempt to bring the energy industry back under state control. The lawsuit is based on the 1994 Energy Charter Treaty.

Title: Qantas sees profits fly to record
Article_Text: Australian airline Qantas has posted a record fiscal first-half profit thanks to cost-cutting measures.  Net profit in the six months ending 31 December rose 28% to A$458.4m ($357.6m; £191m) from a ye...
Summary: Qantas has posted a record fiscal first-half profit of A$458.4m, driven by cost-cutting measures, but warned that earnings growth will slow in the second half due to the impact of the Indian Ocean tsunami and higher fuel costs.

Title: Iraq to invite phone licence bids
Article_Text: Iraq is to invite bids for two telephone licences, saying it wants to significantly boost nationwide coverage over the next decade.  Bids have been invited from local, Arab and foreign companies, Iraq...
Summary: Iraq is inviting bids for two telephone licences to boost nationwide coverage over the next decade, aiming to increase the country's telephone service penetration rate from 4.5% to 25% within 10 years.

Title: Aviation firms eye booming India
Article_Text: India's defence minister has opened the country's Aero India 2005 air show with an invitation for global aerospace firms to outsource jobs to the nation.  Pranab Mukherjee said such companies could ta...
Summary: India's defence minister Pranab Mukherjee invited global aerospace firms to outsource jobs to the nation, citing highly skilled workers and low wages. The Aero India 2005 air show saw over 240 firms from 31 countries attend, with analysts predicting $35bn in aviation market spending over the next 20 years. Several major firms, including Boeing, Airbus, and Lockheed Martin, signed deals with Indian companies.

Title: Russian oil merger excludes Yukos
Article_Text: The merger of Russian gas giant Gazprom and oil firm Rosneft is to go ahead, but will not include Yugansk, which was controversially bought last year.  The merger, backed by Russian authorities, will ...
Summary: The merger of Gazprom and Rosneft will not include Yugansk, which was bought last year, and will allow foreigners to trade in Gazprom shares. The state will get a controlling share of Gazprom in exchange for Rosneft. Yugansk will operate as a separate, state-owned oil firm.

Title: Brazil buy boosts Belgium's Inbev
Article_Text: Belgian brewing giant Inbev has seen its profits soar thanks to its acquisition of Brazil's biggest beer firm Ambev last year.  Inbev, which makes Stella Artois, said pre-tax profits for 2004 rose 56%...
Summary: Belgian brewing giant Inbev has seen its profits soar after acquiring Brazil's biggest beer firm Ambev, with pre-tax profits rising 56% to 1.16bn euros in 2004.

Title: Salary scandal in Cameroon
Article_Text: Cameroon says widespread corruption in its finance ministry has cost it 1bn CFA francs ($2m; £1m) a month.  About 500 officials are accused of either awarding themselves extra money or claiming salari...
Summary: Cameroon's finance ministry has been accused of widespread corruption, costing the country 1 billion CFA francs per month. Prime Minister Ephraim Inoni has vowed to tackle the issue, promising tough punishments for those found guilty. The scam is believed to have started in 1994.

Title: US adds more jobs than expected
Article_Text: The US economy added 337,000 jobs in October - a seven-month high and far more than Wall Street expectations.  In a welcome economic boost for newly re-elected President George W Bush, the Labor Depar...
Summary: The US economy added 337,000 jobs in October, exceeding expectations and boosting the stock market. The jobs growth was driven by sectors other than manufacturing, and the unemployment rate rose slightly. The news had an immediate impact on the stock market, with the Dow Jones index gaining 45.4 points.

Title: Feta cheese battle reaches court
Article_Text: A row over whether only Greece should be allowed to label its cheese feta has reached the European Court of Justice.  The Danish and German governments are challenging a European Commission ruling whi...
Summary: The European Court of Justice is hearing a case over whether Greece should be the only country allowed to label its cheese as feta. The Danish and German governments are challenging a European Commission ruling that gave Greece sole rights to use the name. The ruling applies to feta cheese made in Greece, but critics say it's a generic term used for cheese produced widely outside the country.

Title: Ukraine revisits state sell-offs
Article_Text: Ukraine is preparing what could be a wholesale review of the privatisation of thousands of businesses by the previous administration.  The new President, Viktor Yushchenko, has said a "limited" list o...
Summary: Ukraine is preparing to review the privatisation of thousands of businesses by the previous administration, with the government planning to renationalise 3,000 firms. The review aims to address allegations of corruption and unfair sales to allies of the last administration. President Viktor Yushchenko has said a limited list of companies will be targeted, but Prime Minister Yulia Tymoshenko has stated that the government will return to the state companies that were illegally sold to private hands.

Title: Bank set to leave rates on hold
Article_Text: UK interest rates are set to remain on hold at 4.75% following the latest meeting of the Bank of England.  The Bank's rate-setting committee has put up rates five times in the past year but rates have...
