Summary: UK interest rates are set to remain on hold at 4.75% following the latest meeting of the Bank of England, amid signs of a slowdown in the economy. Economic growth slowed in the previous quarter, with manufacturing output falling and consumer confidence slipping. House prices also fell in October, marking the biggest monthly fall since 2001.

Title: Winter freeze keeps oil above $50
Article_Text: Oil prices carried on rising on Wednesday after cold weather on both sides of the North Atlantic pushed US crude prices to four-month highs.  Freezing temperatures and heavy snowfalls took crude oil p...
Summary: Oil prices rose on Wednesday after cold weather on both sides of the North Atlantic pushed US crude prices to four-month highs, with US crude trading at $51.39 a barrel. The decline in the US dollar has also contributed to the rising oil price. Opec members said they saw no reason to cut their output given high prices.

Title: German jobless rate at new record
Article_Text: More than 5.2 million Germans were out of work in February, new figures show.  The figure of 5.216 million people, or 12.6% of the working-age population, is the highest jobless rate in Europe's bigge...
Summary: Germany's jobless rate reached 12.6% in February, the highest since the 1930s, with over 5.2 million people out of work. The government is implementing labour market reforms, including the 'Hartz-IV' programme, to tackle high unemployment. The latest figures are based on the International Labour Organisation's methodology.

Title: Ore costs hit global steel firms
Article_Text: Shares in steel firms have dropped worldwide amid concerns that higher iron ore costs will hit profit growth.  Shares in Germany's ThyssenKrupp, the UK's Corus and France's Arcleor fell while Japan's ...
Summary: Shares in steel firms have dropped worldwide due to concerns over higher iron ore costs, which may hit profit growth. Record profits for steelmakers are expected to slow down. The price of iron ore has risen by 72% for some suppliers, sparking worries about steel makers' ability to increase product prices.

Title: BMW reveals new models pipeline
Article_Text: BMW is preparing to enter the market for car-style people carriers, the firm's chief has told BBC News.  Speaking at a BMW event ahead of the Geneva motor show, Helmut Panke predicted demand for such ...
Summary: BMW is preparing to enter the market for car-style people carriers, with Helmut Panke predicting high demand in Europe. The company plans to shift away from traditional saloon cars and van-style seven-seat vehicles. A decision on BMW's entry into the new market is due in the first half of 2005.

Title: Asian banks halt dollar's slide
Article_Text: The dollar regained some lost ground against most major currencies on Wednesday after South Korea and Japan denied they were planning a sell-off.  The dollar suffered its biggest one-day fall in four ...
Summary: The dollar regained some lost ground against major currencies after South Korea and Japan denied plans to sell off their dollar reserves. The dollar's slide began after a South Korean parliamentary report suggested boosting holdings of currencies like the Australian and Canadian dollar. The US currency has been struggling despite positive economic data.

Title: Weak dollar trims Cadbury profits
Article_Text: The world's biggest confectionery firm, Cadbury Schweppes, has reported a modest rise in profits after the weak dollar took a bite out of its results.  Underlying pre-tax profits rose 1% to £933m ($1....
Summary: Cadbury Schweppes reported a modest rise in profits in 2004, with underlying pre-tax profits rising 1% to £933m, driven by growth in confectionery brands and cost-cutting measures.

Title: Oil prices fall back from highs
Article_Text: Oil prices retreated from four-month highs in early trading on Tuesday after producers' cartel Opec said it was now unlikely to cut production.  Following the comments by acting Opec secretary general...
Summary: Oil prices retreated from four-month highs after Opec said it was unlikely to cut production, citing high oil prices. US light crude fell 32 cents to $51.43 a barrel, while Brent crude fell 32 cents to $49.74 a barrel. Opec members will meet on 16 March to discuss production levels.

Title: Winn-Dixie files for bankruptcy
Article_Text: US supermarket group Winn-Dixie has filed for bankruptcy protection after succumbing to stiff competition in a market dominated by Wal-Mart.  Winn-Dixie, once among the most profitable of US grocers, ...
Summary: US supermarket group Winn-Dixie has filed for bankruptcy protection due to stiff competition from Wal-Mart, with 920 stores expected to remain open but likely to off-load some sites. The company has total debts of $1.87bn and owes $15.1m to Kraft Foods. Winn-Dixie's new CEO, Peter Lynch, aims to turn the company around through cost reductions and improved customer service.

Title: Why few targets are better than many
Article_Text: The economic targets set out at the Lisbon summit of European Union leaders in 2000 were meant to help Europe leapfrog its way past the United States to become the world's leading economy by 2010.  Bu...
Summary: A report by former Dutch prime minister Wim Kok assesses the European Union's progress towards meeting the Lisbon targets, which were set to help Europe become the world's leading economy by 2010. The report concludes that many targets will be missed and that the EU's competitive position is waning. Kok recommends narrowing down the targets to 14 key indicators and creating a league table to rank countries.

Title: Malaysia lifts Islamic bank limit
Article_Text: Malaysia's central bank is to relax restrictions on foreign ownership to encourage Islamic banking.  Banks in Malaysia will now be able to sell up to 49% of their Islamic banking units, while the limi...
Summary: Malaysia's central bank is relaxing restrictions on foreign ownership to encourage Islamic banking, allowing banks to sell up to 49% of their Islamic banking units. The move puts Malaysia ahead of a 2007 deadline to open up the sector. The country's economy expanded 7.1% in 2004, but growth slowed in the fourth quarter.

Title: Alfa Romeos 'to get GM engines'
Article_Text: Fiat is to stop making six-cylinder petrol engines for its sporty Alfa Romeo subsidiary, unions at the Italian carmaker have said.  The unions claim Fiat is to close the Fiat Powertrain plant at Arese...
Summary: Fiat is reportedly closing its Alfa Romeo engine plant in Arese, Italy, and will source six-cylinder engines from General Motors instead. The move is expected to result in the loss of 800 jobs. Fiat has yet to comment on the matter.

Title: Saab to build Cadillacs in Sweden
Article_Text: General Motors, the world's largest car maker, has confirmed that it will build a new medium-sized Cadillac BLS at its loss-making Saab factory in Sweden.  The car, unveiled at the Geneva motor show, ...
Summary: General Motors has announced plans to build a new medium-sized Cadillac BLS at its Saab factory in Sweden, aiming to compete in the European luxury car market. The move is intended to introduce scale to the loss-making factory and alleviate fears of its closure. However, it may not be welcomed by Opel workers in Germany.

Title: Shares hit by MS drug suspension
Article_Text: Shares in Elan and Biogen Idec plunged on Monday as the firms suspended sales of new multiple sclerosis drug Tysabri after a patient's death in the US.  On the New York Stock Exchange, shares in Irela...
Summary: Shares in Elan and Biogen Idec plummeted after the firms suspended sales of new multiple sclerosis drug Tysabri following a patient's death in the US. The companies took action after a suspected case of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) was reported. The firms plan to evaluate Tysabri-treated patients and consult with experts to better understand the possible risk of PML.

Title: Bank voted 8-1 for no rate change
Article_Text: The decision to keep interest rates on hold at 4.75% earlier this month was passed 8-1 by the Bank of England's rate-setting body, minutes have shown.  One member of the Bank's Monetary Policy Committ...
Summary: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee kept interest rates on hold at 4.75%, surprising some analysts who had expected a unanimous decision. Worries over growth rates and consumer spending were behind the decision. One MPC member, Paul Tucker, voted to raise rates to 5%.

Title: Crude oil prices back above $50
Article_Text: Cold weather across parts of the United States and much of Europe has pushed US crude oil prices above $50 a barrel for the first time in almost three months.  Freezing temperatures and heavy snowfall...
Summary: US crude oil prices have risen above $50 a barrel for the first time in almost three months due to cold weather and low stock levels, while Opec members say they have no reason to cut production.

Title: House prices show slight increase
Article_Text: Prices of homes in the UK rose a seasonally adjusted 0.5% in February, says the Nationwide building society.  The figure means the annual rate of increase in the UK is down to 10.2%, the lowest rate s...
Summary: UK home prices rose 0.5% seasonally in February, with the annual rate of increase down to 10.2% and the lowest since June 2001. The number of mortgage approvals fell to a near 10-year low in January. Nationwide economist Alex Bannister expects house prices to rise by 1% over the next six months, which could lead to interest rate increases.

Title: Golden rule boost for Chancellor
Article_Text: Chancellor Gordon Brown has been given a £2.1bn boost in his attempts to meet his golden economic rule, which allows him to borrow only for investment.  The extra leeway came after the Office for Nati...
Summary: Chancellor Gordon Brown has been given a £2.1bn boost in his attempts to meet his golden economic rule, which allows him to borrow only for investment. The boost came after the Office for National Statistics corrected its measurement of road expenditure data over the past five years. The correction would help Mr Brown meet his golden rule, but economists speculate that it might also allow for some vote-catching measures in the Budget.

Title: Macy's owner buys rival for $11bn
Article_Text: US retail giant Federated Department Stores is to buy rival May Department Stores for $11bn (£5.7bn).  The deal will bring together famous stores like Macy's, Bloomingdale's and Marshall Field's, crea...
Summary: US retail giant Federated Department Stores is acquiring rival May Department Stores for $11bn, creating the largest department store chain in the US. The deal will bring together famous stores like Macy's, Bloomingdale's and Marshall Field's. The combined firm will operate about 1,000 stores across the US.

Title: Industrial revival hope for Japan
Article_Text: Japanese industry is growing faster than expected, boosting hopes that the country's retreat back into recession is over.  Industrial output rose 2.1% - adjusted for the time of year - in January from...
Summary: Japan's industrial output rose 2.1% in January, boosting hopes for a recovery from recession, while retail sales picked up faster than at any time since 1997. Tokyo shares reached an eight-month high, and the yen strengthened against the dollar. Economic officials expressed cautiously optimistic views on the economy's prospects.

Title: Khodorkovsky ally denies charges
Article_Text: A close associate of former Yukos boss Mikhail Khodorkovsky has told a court that fraud charges levelled against him are "false".  Platon Lebedev has been on trial alongside Mr Khodorkovsky since June...
Summary: Platon Lebedev, a close associate of former Yukos boss Mikhail Khodorkovsky, claims fraud charges against him are false and politically motivated. Lebedev and Khodorkovsky face possible 10-year jail sentences if convicted. The charges are seen as part of a drive by Russian President Vladimir Putin to rein in the country's super-rich business leaders.

Title: Qatar and Shell in $6bn gas deal
Article_Text: Shell has signed a $6bn (£3.12bn) deal with the Middle Eastern sheikhdom of Qatar to supply liquid natural gas (LNG) to North America and Europe.  The UK-Dutch group will own 30% of the project, with ...
Summary: Shell has signed a $6bn deal with Qatar to supply LNG to North America and Europe, with 30% ownership by Shell and 70% by Qatar's state oil firm. ExxonMobil has also signed a $12.8bn deal, with France's Total expected to join soon. The agreements are part of Qatar's efforts to become a regional natural gas leader.

Title: India unveils anti-poverty budget
Article_Text: India is to boost spending on primary schools and health in a budget flagged as a boost for the ordinary citizen.  India's defence budget has also been raised 7.8% to 830bn rupees ($19bn). The priorit...
Summary: India's Finance Minister Palaniappan Chidambaram has presented a budget that prioritizes poverty reduction and social spending, while also increasing defense spending and making concessions to the Communist Party. The budget aims to reduce the deficit to 4.3% of GDP in the next fiscal year, falling short of the law's requirement. The government has also announced measures to expand the tax base and reduce corporate tax rates.

Title: GM pays $2bn to evade Fiat buyout
Article_Text: General Motors of the US is to pay Fiat 1.55bn euros ($2bn; £1.1bn) to get out of a deal which could have forced it to buy the Italian car maker outright.  Fiat had sold GM a stake in 2000, as part of...
Summary: General Motors will pay Fiat 1.55bn euros to exit a deal that could have forced it to buy the Italian car maker outright. Fiat will keep supplying diesel engines and use the money to reduce its debt. The deal allows Fiat to maintain its freedom to design its own future.

Title: Ex-Boeing director gets jail term
Article_Text: An ex-chief financial officer at Boeing has received a four-month jail sentence and a fine of $250,000 (£131,961) for illegally hiring a top Air Force aide.  Michael Sears admitted his guilt in breaki...
Summary: An ex-Boeing CFO received a four-month jail sentence and a fine for illegally hiring a top Air Force aide, Darleen Druyun, who was serving a nine-month sentence for favouring Boeing in awarding lucrative contracts. Boeing lost a $23bn government contract after a Pentagon inquiry into the case. The Pentagon is examining eight other contracts worth $3bn.

Title: Verizon 'seals takeover of MCI'
Article_Text: Verizon has won a takeover battle for US phone firm MCI with a bid worth $6.8bn (£3.6bn), reports say.  The two firms are expected to seal the deal on Monday morning, according to news agency reports,...
Summary: Verizon has won a takeover battle for US phone firm MCI with a bid worth $6.8bn, despite a higher bid from Qwest. The deal is expected to be sealed on Monday morning. MCI exited bankruptcy in April after admitting to illegal expenses and profits in 2002.

Title: US data sparks inflation worries
Article_Text: Wholesale prices in the US rose at the fastest rate in more than six years in January, according to government data.  New figures show the Labor Department producer price index (PPI) rose by 0.3% - in...
Summary: Wholesale prices in the US rose at the fastest rate in over six years in January, according to government data, with core producer prices surging by 0.8% and inflationary concerns increasing. The University of Michigan barometer of US retail consumer confidence showed a slight dip, indicating a potential fall in retail spending. The mixed data led to volatile early Wall Street trade.

Title: Yukos sues four firms for $20bn
Article_Text: Russian oil firm Yukos has sued four companies for their role in last year's forced state auction of its key oil production unit Yuganskneftegas.  Yukos is claiming more than $20bn (£11bn) in damages ...
Summary: Russian oil firm Yukos has sued four companies for their role in the forced state auction of its key oil production unit Yuganskneftegas, claiming over $20bn in damages. Yukos has also filed for bankruptcy in Houston and submitted a reorganisation plan. The four companies named in the lawsuit are Gazprom, Gazpromneft, Baikal, and Rosneft.

Title: Consumer spending lifts US growth
Article_Text: US economic growth accelerated in the third quarter, helped by strong consumer spending, official figures have shown.  The economy expanded at an annual rate of 3.7% in the July to September period, t...
Summary: US economic growth accelerated in the third quarter, driven by strong consumer spending, with an annual rate of 3.7% in the July to September period. This growth rate fell short of forecasters' expectations but still marked a significant increase from the previous quarter. Consumer spending accounts for about two thirds of all economic activity in the US.

Title: Crossrail link 'to get go-ahead'
Article_Text: The £10bn Crossrail transport plan, backed by business groups, is to get the go-ahead this month, according to The Mail on Sunday.  It says the UK Treasury has allocated £7.5bn ($13.99bn) for the proj...
Summary: The UK Treasury has allocated £7.5bn for the Crossrail project, and talks with business groups on raising the rest will begin shortly. The project, backed by business groups and the government, aims to introduce a fast cross-London rail link. The bill will go before the House of Commons on 23 February.

Title: Hariri killing hits Beirut shares
Article_Text: Shares in Solidere, the Lebanese company founded by assassinated former prime minister Rafik Hariri, fell 15% in renewed trading in Beirut.  The real estate firm, which dominates Lebanon's stock excha...
Summary: Shares in Solidere fell 15% in Beirut after a three-day market closure to mourn the death of former prime minister Rafik Hariri. The company's benchmark value dropped to $8.08, affecting the overall BLOM stock index. Hariri's assassination has sent shockwaves through Lebanon's business community.

Title: Small firms 'hit by rising costs'
Article_Text: Rising fuel and materials costs are hitting confidence among the UK's small manufacturers despite a rise in output, business lobby group the CBI says.  A CBI quarterly survey found output had risen by...
Summary: The CBI's quarterly survey found UK small manufacturers' output rose by the fastest rate in seven years, but increasing expenses hit confidence. Firms are scaling back investment and looking to the government for relief. Some managed to increase prices, but many saw orders fall.

Title: Buyers snap up Jet Airways' shares
Article_Text: Investors have snapped up shares in Jet Airways, India's biggest airline, following the launch of its much anticipated initial public offer (IPO).  The IPO for 17.3 million shares was fully sold withi...
Summary: Investors have snapped up shares in Jet Airways, India's biggest airline, following the launch of its initial public offer (IPO). The IPO was fully sold within 10 minutes of opening, with analysts expecting Jet to raise at least 16.4bn rupees. The company plans to use the cash to buy new planes and cut its debt.

Title: House prices suffer festive fall
Article_Text: UK house prices fell 0.7% in December, according to figures from the Office of the Deputy Prime Minister.  Nationally, house prices rose at an annual rate of 10.7% in December, less than the 13.7% ris...
Summary: UK house prices fell 0.7% in December, with the average price dropping from £180,126 to £178,906. This marks a slowdown in the market, with all major UK regions except Northern Ireland experiencing a fall in annual growth. The slowdown is attributed to a decrease in sales between October and December.

Title: Deutsche Boerse boosts dividend
Article_Text: Deutsche Boerse, the German stock exchange that is trying to buy its London rival, has said it will boost its 2004 dividend payment by 27%.  Analysts said that the move is aimed at winning over invest...
Summary: Deutsche Boerse is boosting its 2004 dividend payment by 27% in an effort to win over investors opposed to its bid for the London Stock Exchange. The company reported a profit of 120.7m euros and record revenue of 1.45bn euros for the year. A rival bid is also being made by Euronext.

Title: Newest EU members underpin growth
Article_Text: The European Union's newest members will bolster Europe's economic growth in 2005, according to a new report.  The eight central European states which joined the EU last year will see 4.6% growth, the...
Summary: The European Union's newest members are expected to boost economic growth in 2005, with central European states forecast to see 4.6% growth, while the Euro zone countries are expected to see 1.8% growth. The global economy is forecast to slow, with the US current account deficit being a major challenge for policy makers. The EU's average economic growth is forecast to be 2.2% in 2005.
Key_Entities: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe

Title: Brewers' profits lose their fizz
Article_Text: Heineken and Carlsberg, two of the world's largest brewers, have reported falling profits after beer sales in western Europe fell flat.  Dutch firm Heineken saw its annual profits drop 33% and warned ...
Summary: Heineken and Carlsberg, two of the world's largest brewers, have reported falling profits due to weak demand in western Europe and increased marketing costs. They plan to invest in marketing and cut costs to boost sales. Carlsberg is more optimistic about 2005, projecting a 15% rise in net profits.

Title: Yangtze Electric's profits double
Article_Text: Yangtze Electric Power, the operator of China's Three Gorges Dam, has said its profits more than doubled in 2004.  The firm has benefited from increased demand for electricity at a time when power sho...
Summary: Yangtze Electric Power's profits more than doubled in 2004, driven by increased demand for electricity in China. The company's net income jumped to 3bn yuan, while sales surged to 6.2bn yuan. The growth rate has slowed from 2003, and analysts forecast a decline in expansion this year.

Title: French consumer spending rising
Article_Text: French consumers increased their spending by 1.5% in January, a figure which bodes well for the country's economic growth, figures revealed.  The National Statistic Institute (INSEE) added that consum...
Summary: French consumers increased their spending by 1.5% in January, with household equipment sales driving the increase, while car sales fell 2.8% but still saw a year-on-year increase of 6.5%. French consumer prices fell 0.6% in January but rose 1.6% on an annual basis. Italian consumer confidence rose to its highest level since October 2004.

Title: GSK aims to stop Aids profiteers
Article_Text: One of the world's largest manufacturers of HIV/Aids drugs has launched an initiative to combat the smuggling of cheaper pills - supplied to poorer African countries - back into Europe for resale at f...
Summary: GlaxoSmithKline has launched an initiative to combat the smuggling of cheaper HIV/AIDS drugs from Africa back into Europe for resale at higher prices. The company is altering packaging and changing pill color to reduce diversion. Distribution of the new drugs has already begun.

Title: Optimism remains over UK housing
Article_Text: The UK property market remains robust despite the recent slowdown, according to mortgage lender Bradford & Bingley and housebuilder George Wimpey.  B&B said the buy-to-let market - in which the bank i...
Summary: The UK property market remains robust despite recent slowdowns, according to Bradford & Bingley and George Wimpey. The banks reported strong profits, with B&B's profits rising 6% to £280.2m and Wimpey's profits rising 19% to £450.7m. The banks attribute the growth to strong housing demand and low interest rates.

Title: Russia WTO talks 'make progress'
Article_Text: Talks on Russia's proposed membership of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) have been "making good progress" say those behind the negotiations.  But the chairman of the working party, Ambassador Stefa...
Summary: Talks on Russia's proposed membership of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) are making progress, but challenges remain, including limits on foreign ownership and energy price subsidies.

Title: Irish duo could block Man Utd bid
Article_Text: Irishmen JP McManus and John Magnier, who own a 29% stake in Manchester United, will reportedly reject any formal £800m offer for the club.  The Sunday Times and The Sunday Telegraph say they will opp...
Summary: Irish billionaires JP McManus and John Magnier are reportedly rejecting a £800m takeover bid for Manchester United from US tycoon Malcom Glazer. The bid's price of 300p a share is believed to undervalue the club's prospects. The owners of at least 75% of the club's shares are required to back the bid.

Title: Dollar drops on reserves concerns
Article_Text: The US dollar has dropped against major currencies on concerns that central banks may cut the amount of dollars they hold in their foreign reserves.  Comments by South Korea's central bank at the end ...
Summary: The US dollar has dropped against major currencies due to concerns that central banks may cut their dollar holdings, with South Korea's central bank sparking recent declines. Analysts predict other nations may follow suit, boosting their holdings of alternative currencies. The dollar has fallen against the euro and Japanese yen, with some countries increasing their euro holdings.

Title: India and Russia in energy talks
Article_Text: India and Russia are to work together in a series of energy deals, part of a pact which could see India invest up to $20bn in oil and gas projects.  On the agenda are oil and gas extraction as well as...
Summary: India and Russia are set to work together on energy deals worth up to $20bn, including oil and gas extraction and transportation projects led by Gazprom and ONGC. The two companies are expected to develop refining facilities and deliver oil, gas, and petrochemicals from Russia to India and other Asian countries. India is seeking fresh energy supplies due to growing domestic demand.

Title: Weak data buffets French economy
Article_Text: A batch of downbeat government data has cast doubt over the French economy's future prospects.  Official figures showed on Friday that unemployment was unchanged at 9.9% last month, while consumer con...
Summary: French government data showed unchanged unemployment and falling consumer confidence, with finance minister Nicolas Sarkozy warning of the impact of high oil prices on growth. Analysts say structural unemployment and high labor costs are major issues. The economy is expected to grow 2.4% this year, above the eurozone average.

Title: Business fears over sluggish EU economy
Article_Text: As European leaders gather in Rome on Friday to sign the new EU constitution, many companies will be focusing on matters much closer to home - namely how to stay in business.  Lille is a popular touri...
Summary: European companies are struggling with the impact of globalization and EU policies, with many facing pressure to cut costs and reduce workforce due to cheaper production in countries like China and India. The EU's labor market laws and generous unemployment system are also seen as contributing to the problem.
Key_Entities: Institute for the Study of Labour

Title: M&S cuts prices by average of 24%
Article_Text: Marks & Spencer has cut prices in London and the regions by an average of 24%, according to research from a City investment bank.  Dresdner Kleinwort Wasserstein said: "In spite of the snow in the UK,...
Summary: Marks & Spencer has cut prices in London and the regions by an average of 24% due to a tough trading environment, according to research from City investment bank Dresdner Kleinwort Wasserstein. The move may force competitors like Next to lower prices. M&S has brought in new clothing at new price points as part of its strategy to compete in the mid-market retail sector.

Title: US bank 'loses' customer details
Article_Text: The Bank of America has revealed it has lost computer tapes containing account details of more than one million customers who are US federal employees.  Several members of the US Senate are among thos...
Summary: The Bank of America has lost computer tapes containing account details of over 1.2 million US federal employees, including several senators, due to a shipment mishap. The bank is monitoring customer accounts and has notified those affected. The Secret Service is investigating the loss.

Title: Huge rush for Jet Airways shares
Article_Text: Indian airline Jet Airways' initial public offering was oversubscribed 16.2 times, bankers said on Friday.  Over 85% of the bids were at the higher end of the price range of 1,050-1,125 rupees ($24-$2...
Summary: Indian airline Jet Airways' initial public offering was oversubscribed 16.2 times, with 85% of bids at the higher end of the price range. The airline plans to raise up to $443m by selling 20% of its equity. Jet Airways controls 45% of the Indian domestic airline market.

Title: Bank payout to Pinochet victims
Article_Text: A US bank has said it will donate more than $8m to victims of former Chilean military ruler Augusto Pinochet's regime under a Madrid court settlement.  Riggs Bank will put money in a special fund to b...
Summary: A US bank, Riggs Bank, has agreed to donate over $8m to victims of former Chilean military ruler Augusto Pinochet's regime as part of a Madrid court settlement. The bank had been accused of illegally concealing Pinochet's assets. Pinochet is facing charges relating to human rights violations and other crimes.

Title: Qwest may spark MCI bidding war
Article_Text: US phone company Qwest has said it will table a new offer for MCI after losing out to larger rival Verizon, setting the scene for a possible bidding war.  MCI accepted a $6.75bn (£3.6bn) buyout from t...
Summary: US phone company Qwest has rejected a $6.75bn buyout offer from Verizon, but plans to submit a new offer after examining Verizon's bid. MCI accepted the Verizon offer, while Qwest's offer was worth $8bn. The takeover would give the buyer access to a global telecommunications network and a large number of business-based subscribers.

Title: Fiat chief takes steering wheel
Article_Text: The chief executive of the Fiat conglomerate has taken day-to-day control of its struggling car business in an effort to turn it around.  Sergio Marchionne has replaced Herbert Demel as chief executiv...
Summary: Sergio Marchionne has taken control of Fiat Auto's car business to turn it around, replacing Herbert Demel as CEO. The business is expected to make an 800m euro loss in 2004 and has underperformed the market in Europe. Fiat is undergoing a restructuring, including integrating Maserati within its operations.

Title: Consumers drive French economy
Article_Text: France's economic growth accelerated in the last three months of 2004, driven by consumer spending, a report shows.  Gross domestic product (GDP) rose by 0.8% in the fourth quarter compared with the p...
Summary: France's economic growth accelerated in the fourth quarter of 2004, driven by consumer spending and business investment, with annual growth reaching 2.3%.

Title: US regulator to rule on pain drug
Article_Text: US food and drug regulators will decide on Friday whether to recommend the sale of painkillers that have been linked to a high risk of heart attack and stroke.  The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) ...
Summary: US food and drug regulators will decide on Friday whether to recommend the sale of painkillers linked to a high risk of heart attack and stroke. The FDA advisory panel will give its verdict after hearing evidence for three days. The decision will be based on whether the benefits to patients justify the increased risks.

Title: Yukos bankruptcy 'not US matter'
Article_Text: Russian authorities do not have to abide by any US court decisions taken with regard to troubled oil giant Yukos, a Houston court has been told.  Legal expert William Butler said there was no treaty b...
Summary: A US court has ruled that Russian authorities do not have to abide by its decisions in the Yukos case, as there is no treaty between the US and Russia to recognize each other's legal rulings. Yukos filed for bankruptcy in the US to halt the sale of its main oil-producing unit, Yugansk, but the US court's jurisdiction has been challenged by Deutsche Bank and Gazpromneft. The sale of Yugansk was completed by a previously unknown group, which was later bought by state-controlled oil company Rosneft.

Title: Borussia Dortmund near bust
Article_Text: German football club and former European champion Borussia Dortmund has warned it will go bankrupt if rescue talks with creditors fail.  The company's shares tumbled after it said it has "entered a li...
Summary: Borussia Dortmund, Germany's only stock-market listed football club, has warned it will go bankrupt if rescue talks with creditors fail. The club has posted record losses and missed rent payments on its stadium. Creditors are pushing for greater control and a capital injection of 35m euros.

Title: 'Post-Christmas lull' in lending
Article_Text: UK mortgage lending showed a "post-Christmas lull" in January, indicating a slowing housing market, lenders have said.  Both the Council of Mortgage Lenders (CML) and Building Society Association (BSA...
Summary: UK mortgage lending declined sharply in January, with gross mortgage lending down 18% year-on-year and mortgage approvals down 21% compared to January 2004. The decline is attributed to a post-Christmas lull in the housing market. Lenders attribute the slowdown to a weaker pattern of lending seen in the last months of 2004.

Title: UK 'risks breaking golden rule'
Article_Text: The UK government will have to raise taxes or rein in spending if it wants to avoid breaking its "golden rule", a report suggests.  The rule states that the government can borrow cash only to invest, ...
Summary: The UK government may need to raise taxes or cut spending to avoid breaking the golden rule, a report suggests. The National Institute of Economic and Social Research (NIESR) claims that taxes need to rise by about £10bn to put state finances in order. The report also forecasts a strong global economy, with growth expected to continue in the US, Japan, and the euro zone.
Key_Entities: National Institute of Economic and Social Research

Title: Worldcom director ends evidence
Article_Text: The former chief financial officer at US telecoms firm WorldCom has finished giving evidence at the trial of his ex-boss Bernie Ebbers.  Scott Sullivan admitted to jurors he was willing to commit frau...
Summary: The former CFO of WorldCom, Scott Sullivan, has testified that he was willing to commit fraud to meet Wall Street earnings projections. Scott Sullivan has already pleaded guilty to fraud and will be sentenced following the trial of his ex-boss Bernie Ebbers. Ebbers is on trial for fraud and conspiracy in relation to WorldCom's collapse in 2002.

Title: Ukraine steel sell-off 'illegal'
Article_Text: The controversial sell-off of a Ukrainian steel mill to a relative of the former president was illegal, a court has ruled.  The mill, Krivorizhstal, was sold in June 2004 for $800m (£424m) - well belo...
Summary: A Ukrainian court has ruled that the sell-off of a steel mill to a relative of the former president was illegal, and the mill's sale price was significantly lower than other offers. President Viktor Yushchenko plans to review many of Ukraine's recent privatisations, including the sale of the mill. The sale price was $800m, which is lower than the suggested fair valuation of $3bn.

Title: Cairn shares up on new oil find
Article_Text: Shares in Cairn Energy have jumped 6% after the firm said an Indian oilfield was larger than previously thought.  Cairn said drilling to the north-west of its development site in Rajasthan had produce...
Summary: Shares in Cairn Energy have jumped 6% after the firm said an Indian oilfield was larger than previously thought, with drilling producing strong results and a 25-year production timeline. The company's share price rose 300% last year after several oil finds, but was hit in December following a disappointing drilling update. Cairn's shares are now in danger of being relegated from the FTSE 100.

Title: Georgia plans hidden asset pardon
Article_Text: Georgia is offering a one-off 'tax amnesty' to people who hid their earnings under the regime of former president Eduard Shevardnadze.  The country's new president, Mikhail Saakashvili, has said that ...
Summary: Georgia is offering a one-off tax amnesty to people who hid their earnings under the regime of former president Eduard Shevardnadze, with the goal of legitimizing previously hidden economic activity and boosting the country's economy.

Title: Cuba winds back economic clock
Article_Text: Fidel Castro's decision to ban all cash transactions in US dollars in Cuba has once more turned the spotlight on Cuba's ailing economy.  All conversions between the US dollar and Cuba's "convertible" ...
Summary: Cuba is introducing a 10% tax on all conversions between the US dollar and Cuba's peso, affecting Cuban citizens and foreign visitors, in an effort to raise revenue for the cash-strapped economy.
Key_Entities: UN Economic Commission for Latin America

Title: Novartis hits acquisition trail
Article_Text: Swiss drugmaker Novartis has announced 5.65bn euros ($7.4bn; £3.9bn) of purchases to make its Sandoz unit the world's biggest generic drug producer.  Novartis, which last month forecast record sales f...
Summary: Novartis has announced a 5.65bn euros purchase to make its Sandoz unit the world's biggest generic drug producer, acquiring Hexal and Eon Labs. The deal will see cost savings of about $200m a year and create jobs. Novartis' shares rose 1% after the announcement.

Title: MCI shareholder sues to stop bid
Article_Text: A shareholder in US phone firm MCI has taken legal action to halt a $6.75bn (£3.6bn) buyout by telecoms giant Verizon, hoping to get a better deal.  The lawsuit was filed on Friday after Qwest Communi...
Summary: A shareholder in US phone firm MCI has filed a lawsuit to halt a $6.75bn buyout by Verizon, alleging that the directors breached their fiduciary duties by accepting a lower offer. MCI's directors have backed Verizon, despite it offering less money. The lawsuit argues that Verizon's offer undervalues the company's future growth prospects.

Title: 'Standoff' on Deutsche's LSE bid
Article_Text: Deutsche Boerse investors unhappy with its London Stock Exchange bid will have no chance to throw out the exchange's management until May, Reuters says.  The Sunday Times reported that hedge funds TCI...
Summary: Deutsche Boerse investors unhappy with its London Stock Exchange bid will have to wait until May to demand the removal of the exchange's management, according to Reuters. The investors want Deutsche to return cash to shareholders rather than bid. Deutsche Boerse has opposed the LSE bid, saying it would destroy shareholder value.

Title: Bush to outline 'toughest' budget
Article_Text: President Bush is to send his toughest budget proposals to date to the US Congress, seeking large cuts in domestic spending to lower the deficit.  About 150 federal programs could be cut or axed altog...
Summary: President Bush is sending a $2.5 trillion budget proposal to the US Congress, aiming to cut domestic spending and lower the deficit. The proposal includes large cuts in 150 federal programs, while defence spending will rise. The budget excludes the cost of continuing military operations in Iraq.

Title: Orange colour clash set for court
Article_Text: A row over the colour orange could hit the courts after mobile phone giant Orange launched action against a new mobile venture from Easyjet's founder.  Orange said it was starting proceedings against ...
Summary: Mobile phone giant Orange is taking action against Easymobile, a new low-cost mobile service from Easyjet's founder Stelios Haji-Ioannou, alleging trademark infringement and passing off due to the use of the colour orange.

Title: Standard Life cuts policy bonuses
Article_Text: Standard Life, Europe's largest mutual life insurer, has cut bonuses for with-profit policyholders.  Annual bonus rates on its with-profits life policies were cut from 2.5% to 2%, while bonuses on pen...
Summary: Standard Life, Europe's largest mutual life insurer, has cut bonuses for with-profit policyholders due to poor share returns and low interest rates. The insurer has made cuts to bonus rates for the sixth time in three years. With-profits policies are designed to smooth out stock market volatility.

Title: EMI shares hit by profit warning
Article_Text: Shares in music giant EMI have sunk by more than 16% after the firm issued a profit warning following disappointing sales and delays to two album releases.  EMI said music sales for the year to March ...
Summary: Shares in music giant EMI have sunk by more than 16% after the firm issued a profit warning due to disappointing sales and delays to two album releases. EMI expects profits to be 15% lower than analysts had expected. The company blamed poor sales since Christmas and delays to the releases of new albums by Coldplay and Gorillaz.

Title: China's Shanda buys stake in Sina
Article_Text: Chinese online game operator Shanda Interactive Entertainment has bought a 20% stake in Sina, the country's biggest internet portal firm.  The move may be a precursor to a full takeover, with analysts...
Summary: Chinese online game operator Shanda Interactive Entertainment has bought a 20% stake in Sina, the country's biggest internet portal firm, sparking speculation of a potential full takeover. The move may be influenced by a better-known international firm showing interest in Sina. A merger could create a firm offering online role-playing games, news, entertainment, and wireless messaging.

Title: Mixed reaction to Man Utd offer
Article_Text: Shares in Manchester United were up over 5% by noon on Monday following a new offer from Malcolm Glazer.  The board of Man Utd is expected to meet early this week to discuss the latest proposal from t...
Summary: Shares in Manchester United rose over 5% after a new offer from Malcolm Glazer, who values the club at $1.5bn. The board is expected to meet to discuss the proposal, which includes a £200m reduction in debt. The club's largest shareholders, JP McManus and John Magnier, are required to support the bid.

Title: Gold falls on IMF sale concerns
Article_Text: The price of gold has fallen after the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said it will look at ways of using its gold reserves to provide debt relief.  By revaluing its holdings, the IMF may be able to...
Summary: The IMF plans to revalue its gold reserves to sell billions of dollars of gold and use the cash to cancel debts owed by the world's poorest nations. The plan was put forward by G7 finance ministers, who also backed plans to write off up to 100% of debts owed by some of the world's poorest countries. The IMF values its gold reserves at between $40 and $50 an ounce, a price that is about a tenth of the metal's current market value.

Title: Electronics firms eye plasma deal
Article_Text: Consumer electronics giants Hitachi and Matshushita Electric are joining forces to share and develop technology for flat screen televisions.  The tie-up comes as the world's top producers are having t...
Summary: Hitachi and Matsushita Electric are joining forces to share and develop technology for flat screen televisions, aiming to expand the plasma display TV market globally. The deal will enable the companies to develop new technology and improve their competitiveness. The plasma panel market has seen rapid consolidation in recent months.

Title: MG Rover China tie-up 'delayed'
Article_Text: MG Rover's proposed tie-up with China's top carmaker has been delayed due to concerns by Chinese regulators, according to the Financial Times.  The paper said Chinese officials had been irritated by R...
Summary: MG Rover's proposed tie-up with Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp has been delayed due to concerns from Chinese regulators, who are worried about job losses and the need for cost-cutting measures. The deal was seen as crucial to saving Rover's Longbridge plant in the West Midlands. The approval process is now awaiting the Shanghai city government and the National Development and Reform Commission.

Title: US bank boss hails 'genius' Smith
Article_Text: US Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan has given a speech at a Scottish church in honour of the pioneering economist, Adam Smith.  He delivered the 14th Adam Smith Lecture in Kirkcaldy, Fife. The ...
Summary: US Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan delivered the 14th Adam Smith Lecture at a Scottish church in Kirkcaldy, Fife, in honour of Adam Smith. The lecture celebrated Smith's work on capitalism and economics. Greenspan praised Smith's genius and impact on the modern world.
Key_Entities: Fife College of Further and Higher Education

Title: Economy 'strong' in election year
Article_Text: UK businesses are set to prosper during the next few months - but this could trigger more interest rate rises, according to a report.  Optimism is at its highest since 1997 and business will reap the ...
Summary: UK businesses are optimistic about the next few months, with a report from BDO Stoy Hayward predicting continued growth due to increased public spending and merger and acquisition activity. However, the Bank of England may raise interest rates later in the year, potentially slowing growth. The general election in May is also expected to impact business optimism.

Title: SEC to rethink post-Enron rules
Article_Text: The US stock market watchdog's chairman has said he is willing to soften tough new US corporate governance rules to ease the burden on foreign firms.  In a speech at the London School of Economics, Wi...
Summary: The US stock market watchdog's chairman, William Donaldson, has proposed softening new corporate governance rules to ease the burden on foreign firms, which have protested that US laws make Wall Street listings too costly.

Title: Nissan names successor to Ghosn
Article_Text: Nissan has named a lifetime employee to run its operations after Carlos Ghosn, its highly successful boss, takes charge at Renault.  As chief operating officer, Toshiyuki Shiga will run Nissan on a da...
Summary: Nissan has named Toshiyuki Shiga as its new chief operating officer, succeeding Carlos Ghosn, who will become chairman and chief executive of Renault. Ghosn transformed Nissan into a profitable business, and Shiga will lead global sales and marketing. Ghosn will split his time between Nissan and Renault.

Title: Ukraine trims privatisation check
Article_Text: Ukraine is to review "dozens" of state asset sales as the country's new administration tackles corruption.  The figure announced by President Viktor Yushchenko is less than the 3,000 cases mentioned l...
Summary: Ukraine is reviewing dozens of state asset sales as part of its efforts to tackle corruption, with President Viktor Yushchenko announcing the review will cover many of the biggest deals. The move comes as Ukraine seeks closer ties with the European Union and the US has been urged to support Ukraine's entry into the World Trade Organisation. President Yushchenko is set to meet with US President George W Bush and other NATO leaders in Brussels.

Title: Absa and Barclays talks continue
Article_Text: South Africa biggest retail bank Absa has said it is still in talks with UK bank Barclays over the sale of majority stake in the group.  In November, Absa said it was close to striking a deal with Bar...
Summary: Absa is in talks with Barclays over the sale of a majority stake, with earnings growth forecasted at 20-25% in the current financial year. Barclays is waiting for approval from South Africa's banking and competition authorities before making a formal offer. Absa's earnings forecast was better than expected, but headline earnings growth will be trimmed due to share options and staff incentives.

Title: Rescue hope for Borussia Dortmund
Article_Text: Shares in struggling German football club Borussia Dortmund slipped on Monday despite the club agreeing a rescue plan with creditors on Friday.  The club, which has posted record losses and racked up ...
Summary: Shares in Borussia Dortmund slipped 7% after the club agreed a rescue plan with creditors, despite a previous boost from the news. The club needs almost 30m euros to pay its bills until the end of June. Borussia Dortmund is facing financial difficulties and has been beaten by Bayern Munich.

Title: Standard Life concern at LSE bid
Article_Text: Standard Life is the latest shareholder in Deutsche Boerse to express concern at the German stock market operator's plans to buy the London Stock Exchange.  It said Deutsche Boerse had to show why its...
Summary: Standard Life, a shareholder of Deutsche Boerse, has expressed concerns over the German stock market operator's planned £1.35bn ($2.5bn) offer for the London Stock Exchange, citing the need for Deutsche Boerse to demonstrate the value of the acquisition to shareholders. Fellow shareholders have also expressed doubts, with some requesting a shareholder vote on the issue. Deutsche Boerse's management is expected to make an improved offer.

Title: BP surges ahead on high oil price
Article_Text: Oil giant BP has announced a 26% rise in annual profits to $16.2bn (£8.7bn) on the back of record oil prices.  Last week, rival Shell reported an annual profit of $17.5bn - a record profit for a UK-li...
Summary: Oil giant BP has announced a 26% rise in annual profits to $16.2bn, driven by record oil prices, and plans to increase its fourth-quarter dividend by 26% and continue share buybacks. The company's performance was below expectations, but its share price rose 4p in morning trading. BP attributes its profits to its investment in oil exploration, which has led to new discoveries in Egypt, the Gulf of Mexico, and Angola.

Title: Oil companies get Russian setback
Article_Text: International oil and mining companies have reacted cautiously to Russia's decision to bar foreign firms from natural resource tenders in 2005.  US oil giant Exxon said it did not plan to take part in...
Summary: International oil and mining companies have reacted cautiously to Russia's decision to bar foreign firms from natural resource tenders, with some expressing concern over the impact on the investment climate. The decision aims to protect national interests and allow Russian companies to develop strategic resources. Foreign firms will be permitted to bid only if they are at least 51% Russian-owned.

Title: Gaming firm to sell UK dog tracks
Article_Text: Six UK greyhound tracks have been put up for sale by gaming group Wembley as part of a move which will lead to the break-up of the group.  Wembley announced the planned sale as it revealed it was to o...
Summary: Gaming group Wembley is selling its US gaming division to BLB Investors for $339m, subject to conditions. The sale will leave Wembley with its UK business, including six greyhound tracks. Analysts value the tracks at £40m-£50m.

Title: Man Utd to open books to Glazer
Article_Text: Manchester United's board has agreed to give US tycoon Malcolm Glazer access to its books.  Earlier this month, Mr Glazer presented the board with detailed proposals on an offer to buy the football cl...
Summary: Manchester United's board has agreed to allow US tycoon Malcolm Glazer to access the club's books as part of a limited due diligence process, despite opposing his plans to buy the club. The club values the offer at £800m ($1.5bn) and has expressed concerns over Glazer's business plan assumptions. The club's biggest shareholders, including Irish horse racing millionaires JP McManus and John Magnier, will need to support a formal offer.

Title: Sales 'fail to boost High Street'
Article_Text: The January sales have failed to help the UK High Street recover from a poor Christmas season, a survey has found.  Stores received a boost from bargain hunters but trading then reverted to December l...
Summary: January sales in the UK failed to help the High Street recover from a poor Christmas season, with sales only rising by 0.5% on a like-for-like basis. Consumers remain cautious over buying big-ticket items. Higher interest rates and uncertainty over the housing market continue to affect the retail sector.

Title: McDonald's to sponsor MTV show
Article_Text: McDonald's, the world's largest restaurant chain, is to sponsor a programme on music channel MTV as part of its latest youth market promotion.  The show Advance Warning highlights new talent and MTV r...
Summary: McDonald's is sponsoring a music program on MTV as part of its youth market promotion, aiming to reach 400 million homes in 162 countries. The move comes amid growing concerns about obesity in Europe and the US. McDonald's has been taking steps to improve its junk food reputation.

Title: Call to save manufacturing jobs
Article_Text: The Trades Union Congress (TUC) is calling on the government to stem job losses in manufacturing firms by reviewing the help it gives companies.  The TUC said in its submission before the Budget that ...
Summary: The Trades Union Congress is calling on the government to review its support for manufacturing firms to prevent job losses, citing 105,000 jobs lost in the sector over the last year.

Title: Tsunami 'to hit Sri Lanka banks'
Article_Text: Sri Lanka's banks face hard times following December's tsunami disaster, officials have warned.  The Sri Lanka Banks Association said the waves which killed more than 30,000 people also washed away hu...
Summary: Sri Lanka's banks are facing financial difficulties following the December tsunami disaster, with 13.6% of loans made to clients in the disaster zone written off or damaged. The private banking sector has 25bn rupees of loans outstanding in the disaster zone. State-owned lenders, such as the People's Bank, are also expected to be hit hard.

Title: Shares rise on new Man Utd offer
Article_Text: Shares in Manchester United closed up 4.75% on Monday following a new offer from US tycoon Malcolm Glazer.  The board of the football club is expected to meet early this week to discuss the latest pro...
Summary: Shares in Manchester United closed up 4.75% on Monday following a new offer from US tycoon Malcolm Glazer, who values the club at £800m ($1.5bn). The club's board is expected to meet to discuss the proposal, which has been rejected previously. Glazer's latest move is being led by his two sons, Avi and Joel.

Title: Yukos drops banks from court bid
Article_Text: Russian oil company Yukos has dropped the threat of legal action against five banks it had accused of involvement in the sale of its key Yugansk unit.  State-owned Rosneft bought the unit for $9.3bn (...
Summary: Russian oil company Yukos has dropped the threat of legal action against five banks it had accused of involvement in the sale of its key Yugansk unit. Yukos claims the sale was illegal and is pursuing damages in a US court. The company has an outstanding complaint against Deutsche Bank, which it alleges to be the leader of a consortium that was behind a bid for Yugansk by state gas monopoly Gazprom.

Title: Venezuela reviews foreign deals
Article_Text: Venezuela is to review all foreign investment in its mining industries in an effort to strengthen its indigenous industrial output.  President Hugo Chavez has ordered all existing contracts with forei...
Summary: Venezuela is reviewing foreign investment in its mining industries to strengthen its indigenous industrial output, with President Hugo Chavez ordering an examination of existing contracts with foreign firms. The review excludes the oil sector and aims to transfer technology and training capabilities to projects with foreign partners. The government seeks to develop its own industrial infrastructure to create new jobs and reduce reliance on foreign partners.

Title: Lloyd's of London head chides FSA
Article_Text: The head of Lloyd's of London, the insurance market, has criticised Britain's financial watchdog, the Financial Services Authority (FSA).  In a speech on Monday, Mr Prettejohn urged the FSA to force b...
Summary: The head of Lloyd's of London, Mr Prettejohn, has criticized Britain's financial watchdog, the FSA, for not forcing brokers to disclose their commissions. He wants the FSA to make disclosure mandatory. The FSA has sidestepped calls to require brokers to disclose commissions to their clients.

Title: Bat spit drug firm goes to market
Article_Text: A German firm whose main product is derived from the saliva of the vampire bat is looking to raise more than 70m euros ($91m; £49m) on the stock market.  The firm, Paion, said that it hoped to sell 5 ...
Summary: Paion, a German firm, plans to raise over 70m euros by selling 5 million shares on the stock market, with the main product desmoteplase based on a protein from vampire bat saliva.

Title: Vodafone appoints new Japan boss
Article_Text: Vodafone has drafted in its UK chief executive William Morrow to take charge of its troubled Japanese operation.  Mr Morrow will succeed Shiro Tsuda as president of Vodafone KK, Japan's number three m...
Summary: Vodafone has appointed William Morrow as president of its Japanese operation, Vodafone KK, in an effort to turn around the struggling business. The company has lost customers in recent months, including a net loss of over 58,000 in January. Morrow will succeed Shiro Tsuda, who will become chairman.

Title: Pension hitch for long-living men
Article_Text: Male life expectancy is much higher than originally estimated, leading pension researchers have said.  The Pensions Policy Institute (PPI) said life expectancy for unskilled and professional men has b...
Summary: Pension researchers say male life expectancy is higher than estimated, with a gap of 8 years between manual and professional workers. Life expectancy at 65 is 5 years apart. The PPI's estimate excludes pre-65 deaths and accounts for life expectancy improvements. This may lead to more pressure on state pension spending.

Title: Card fraudsters 'targeting web'
Article_Text: New safeguards on credit and debit card payments in shops has led fraudsters to focus on internet and phone payments, an anti-fraud agency has said.  Anti-fraud consultancy Retail Decisions says 'card...
Summary: New safeguards on credit and debit card payments in shops have led to a shift in fraud tactics from in-store to online and phone payments, according to anti-fraud agency Retail Decisions. The introduction of chip and pin cards has tightened security, but fraudsters have adapted to the new system by targeting internet and phone payments. Card-not-present fraud has risen by 22% in the UK since the start of 2005.

Title: Britannia members' £42m windfall
Article_Text: More than 800,000 Britannia Building Society members are to receive a profit share worth on average £52 each.  Members of the UK's second largest building society will share £42m, with 100,000 receivi...
Summary: More than 800,000 Britannia Building Society members are to receive a profit share worth on average £52 each, with 100,000 receiving a windfall of more than £100. The payouts are bigger than last year due to stricter eligibility rules. Britannia has paid out more than £370m through its profit share scheme since its introduction in 1997.

Title: Firms pump billions into pensions
Article_Text: Employers have spent billions of pounds propping up their final salary pensions over the past year, research suggests.  A survey of 280 schemes by Incomes Data Services' (IDS) said employer contributi...
Summary: Employer contributions to final salary pensions have increased by 49.7% to £8.2bn, with some firms forced to top up funds due to rising deficits. Many companies are struggling to maintain these schemes due to rising costs and increased liabilities. The trend is expected to lead to reduced benefits for existing scheme members.

Title: UK homes hit £3.3 trillion total
Article_Text: The value of the UK's housing stock reached the £3.3 trillion mark in 2004 - triple the value 10 years earlier, a report indicates.  Research from Halifax, the country's biggest mortgage lender, sugge...
Summary: The UK's housing stock value reached £3.3 trillion in 2004, a 262% increase in Northern Ireland and a 112% increase in Scotland, according to a report by Halifax. The value of private housing stock continues to rise steadily, with London and the South East holding over a third of the UK's private housing assets. The average price of a British property is £163,748, according to Halifax's monthly figures.

Title: Economy 'strong' in election year
Article_Text: UK businesses are set to prosper during the next few months - but this could trigger more interest rate rises, according to a report.  Optimism is at its highest since 1997 and business will reap the ...
Summary: UK businesses are optimistic about the next few months, with a report from BDO Stoy Hayward predicting continued growth due to increased public spending and merger and acquisition activity. However, the Bank of England may raise interest rates later in the year, potentially slowing growth. The general election in May is also expected to impact business optimism.

Title: G7 backs Africa debt relief plan
Article_Text: G7 finance ministers have backed plans to write off up to 100% of the debts of some of the world's poorest countries.  UK chancellor Gordon Brown said the London meeting of the world's seven richest n...
Summary: G7 finance ministers have backed plans to write off up to 100% of the debts of some of the world's poorest countries, with 37 countries potentially benefiting from the move. The UK's International Finance Facility proposal to boost aid to developing countries has not been agreed upon by the US, but other countries have expressed support for the plan. The G7 meeting also discussed other global issues, including the impact of rising economies in China and India.

Title: Q&A: Malcolm Glazer and Man Utd
Article_Text: The battle for control of Manchester United has taken another turn after the club confirmed it had received a fresh takeover approach from US business tycoon Malcolm Glazer.  No formal offer has been ...
Summary: Manchester United has received a fresh takeover approach from US business tycoon Malcolm Glazer, who is offering 300p per share, valuing the club at about £800m ($1.5bn). The approach is being led by Glazer's two sons, Avi and Joel, and is reportedly being considered by the club's board. However, the club's largest shareholders, John Magnier and JP McManus, are holding their stake as an investment and will need to be convinced to support the bid.

Title: Making your office work for you
Article_Text: Our mission to brighten up your working lives continues - and this time, we're taking a long hard look at your offices.  Over the next few months, our panel of experts will be listening to your gripes...
Summary: An expert panel is advising on how to create an efficient and comfortable workspace, particularly for freelancers and remote workers. They suggest considering the work personality, setting boundaries, and bringing the outside world into the space. The panel also provides guidance on interior design, electrical and plumbing requirements, and technology setup.

Title: Market unfazed by Aurora setback
Article_Text: As the Aurora limped back to its dock on 20 January, a blizzard of photos and interviews seemed to add up to an unambiguous tale of woe.  The ship had another slice of bad luck to add to its history o...
Summary: P&O Cruises, part of Carnival Corporation, faced a crisis after the Aurora ship experienced health scares and technical trouble, but the impact on profits and stock prices was minimal, with investors seemingly unaware of the issue.

Title: The 'ticking budget' facing the US
Article_Text: The budget proposals laid out by the administration of US President George W Bush are highly controversial. The Washington-based Economic Policy Institute, which tends to be critical of the President,...
Summary: The Bush administration's budget proposals are highly controversial and may lead to large cuts in small programs, forcing the federal government to make good on its debts to the Social Security Trust Fund. Rising federal debt and increased borrowing will put upward pressure on interest rates, affecting consumers and businesses. The public outcry will force Congress to act, but the chosen remedy of reducing domestic spending is deemed the least feasible.
Key_Entities: Aid to state and local governments

Title: Ebbers 'aware' of WorldCom fraud
Article_Text: Former WorldCom boss Bernie Ebbers was directly involved in the $11bn financial fraud at the firm, his closest associate has told a US court.  Giving evidence in the criminal trial of Mr Ebbers, ex-fi...
Summary: Bernie Ebbers, former WorldCom boss, is accused of orchestrating a $11bn financial fraud, with his closest associate, Scott Sullivan, implicating him in the scandal. Ebbers denies the charges, claiming he was unaware of the fraud. Sullivan, who pleaded guilty to fraud, testified that Ebbers was involved in hiding the true state of the company's finances.

Title: Renault boss hails 'great year'
Article_Text: Strong sales outside western Europe helped Renault boost its profits by more than 40% in 2004 although the firm warned of lower margins this year.  France's second largest carmaker enjoyed a healthy 4...
Summary: Renault's profits rose 43% in 2004 to 2.4bn euros, driven by strong sales outside western Europe and the good performance of its Megane range. The firm expects lower margins in 2005, but plans to grow global sales. Renault will launch new models in 2005.

Title: Survey confirms property slowdown
Article_Text: Government figures have confirmed a widely reported slowdown of the UK's housing market in late 2004.  House prices were 11.8% higher on the year in the last quarter of 2004, down from 16.3% in the Ju...
Summary: The UK's housing market slowed down in late 2004, with house prices 11.8% higher in the last quarter compared to the previous quarter, and the volume of sales dropping by nearly a quarter from the same period in 2003. The average house price in England and Wales decreased, with the biggest annual gains made in Wales. The market is expected to be influenced by the Bank of England's interest rate decision.

Title: Bush budget seeks deep cutbacks
Article_Text: President Bush has presented his 2006 budget, cutting domestic spending in a bid to lower a record deficit projected to peak at $427bn (£230bn) this year.  The $2.58 trillion (£1.38 trillion) budget s...
Summary: President Bush has presented his 2006 budget, cutting domestic spending to lower a record deficit, while foreign aid and military spending are set to rise. The budget does not include the cost of running military operations in Iraq and Afghanistan, and a key spending line is missing, the cost of funding the administration's proposed radical overhaul of Social Security.

Title: Profits stall at China's Lenovo
Article_Text: Profits at Chinese computer firm Lenovo have stood still amid slowing demand at home and stiffening competition.  The firm is in the international spotlight after last year signing a deal to buy the P...
Summary: Lenovo's profits have remained steady despite slowing demand in China and increased competition. The company's sales were down 3.7% in the three months to December. A deal to buy IBM's PC division is expected to mark the end of an era, but investors have been less than impressed due to the unit's unprofitability.

Title: MCI shares climb on takeover bid
Article_Text: Shares in US phone company MCI have risen on speculation that it is in takeover talks.  The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday that Qwest has bid $6.3bn (£3.4bn) for MCI. Other firms have also e...
Summary: Shares in US phone company MCI have risen on speculation that it is in takeover talks with Qwest, which has bid $6.3bn for MCI. Other firms may now table rival bids, analysts said. A merger between MCI and Qwest would give Qwest access to MCI's global network and business-based subscribers.

Title: BT offers equal access to rivals
Article_Text: BT has moved to pre-empt a possible break-up of its business by offering to cut wholesale broadband prices and open its network to rivals.  The move comes after telecom regulator Ofcom said in Novembe...
Summary: BT has proposed changes to its business model in response to a UK telecom regulator's review, aiming to promote greater competition in the UK telecom sector. The company plans to cut wholesale broadband prices and open its network to rivals, in exchange for lighter regulation. BT aims to invest £10bn in the next five years to create a 21st Century network.

Title: Jobs growth still slow in the US
Article_Text: The US created fewer jobs than expected in January, but a fall in jobseekers pushed the unemployment rate to its lowest level in three years.  According to Labor Department figures, US firms added onl...
Summary: The US created fewer jobs than expected in January, but the unemployment rate fell to its lowest level in three years. The job gains were below market expectations, but still pushed the unemployment rate down to 5.2%. The administration's first term jobs record ended in positive territory.

Title: News Corp eyes video games market
Article_Text: News Corp, the media company controlled by Australian billionaire Rupert Murdoch, is eyeing a move into the video games market.  According to the Financial Times, chief operating officer Peter Chernin...
Summary: News Corp, controlled by Rupert Murdoch, is considering a move into the video games market, with Activision being a potential target. The company's chief operating officer, Peter Chernin, stated that video games are a 'big business' and that News Corp wants to get into it. However, Chernin noted that finding a suitable target is challenging due to the high price tags of companies like Electronic Arts.

Title: Call to overhaul UK state pension
Article_Text: The UK pension system has been branded inadequate and too complex by a leading retirement think-tank.  The Pensions Policy Institute (PPI) said replacing the state pension with a "citizen's pension" w...
Summary: A leading retirement think-tank has called for a 'citizen's pension' to tackle inequality and complexity in the UK pension system, replacing state pension calculations with residency length.

Title: Singapore growth at 8.1% in 2004
Article_Text: Singapore's economy grew by 8.1% in 2004, its best performance since 2000, figures from the trade ministry show.  The advance, the second-fastest in Asia after China, was led by growth of 13.1% in the...
Summary: Singapore's economy grew 8.1% in 2004, its best performance since 2000, driven by a 13.1% growth in the manufacturing sector. However, a slower-than-expected fourth quarter points to more modest growth in 2005 due to global technology demand and potential disruptions from the tsunami disaster. Economic growth is expected to halve to 3-5% this year.

Title: Turkey knocks six zeros off lira
Article_Text: Turkey is to relaunch its currency on Saturday, knocking six zeros off the lira in the hope of boosting trade and powering its growing economy.  The change will see the end of such dizzyingly-high den...
Summary: Turkey is relaunching its currency, the lira, by removing six zeros, aiming to boost trade and stabilize its economy. The new currency will be launched on January 1, replacing denominations such as five million lira and the 20m note. The move is seen as a promise of growing economic stability as Turkey pursues EU membership.

Title: S Korea spending boost to economy
Article_Text: South Korea will boost state spending next year in an effort to create jobs and kick start its sputtering economy.  It has earmarked 100 trillion won ($96bn) for the first six months of 2005, 60% of i...
Summary: South Korea plans to boost state spending to create jobs and stimulate its economy, earmarking 100 trillion won for the first six months of 2005. The government aims to create 400,000 jobs and focus on infrastructure and home building. However, some experts are skeptical about the effectiveness of the plan.

Title: Latin America sees strong growth
Article_Text: Latin America's economy grew by 5.5% in 2004, its best performance since 1980, while exports registered their best performance in two decades.  The United Nations' Economic Commission for Latin Americ...
Summary: Latin America's economy grew by 5.5% in 2004, its best performance since 1980, driven by strong exports and regional blocs. The region's exports reached a 20-year high, with China and the US contributing to the growth. However, doubts about the US recovery and Chinese economy pose risks for 2005.
Key_Entities: Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean

Title: Asia shares defy post-quake gloom
Article_Text: Indonesian, Indian and Hong Kong stock markets reached record highs.  Investors seemed to feel that some of the worst-affected areas were so under-developed that the tragedy would have little impact o...
Summary: Indonesian, Indian and Hong Kong stock markets reached record highs, with investors downplaying the economic impact of the tsunami on Asia's listed firms. India's Bombay Stock Exchange and Indonesia's Jakarta stock exchange benefited from expectations of strong corporate earnings in 2005. However, some economists warned that the disaster could lead to losses in tourism revenue and economic growth in affected countries.

Title: Booming markets shed few tears
Article_Text: The market, former British government minister Michael Heseltine once said, has no morality.  And indeed, stock exchange traders around Asia have wasted little time regretting the victims of this week...
Summary: Stock markets in Asia have hit all-time highs despite the devastating floods, with many companies unaffected by the disaster. Insurance costs are estimated in the tens of billions of dollars, but the impact on corporate bottom lines is expected to be minimal. The global capital market is vast and resilient, with most businesses recovering from disasters.

Title: Asian quake hits European shares
Article_Text: Shares in Europe's leading reinsurers and travel firms have fallen as the scale of the damage wrought by tsunamis across south Asia has become apparent.  More than 23,000 people have been killed follo...
Summary: Shares in European reinsurers and travel firms fell as the scale of the damage from tsunamis in south Asia became apparent, with investors worrying about rebuilding costs. The disaster had little impact on US and Asian stock markets. Currencies weakened, with the Thai baht and Indonesian rupiah losing value.

Title: Split-caps pay £194m compensation
Article_Text: Investors who lost money following the split-capital investment trust scandal are to receive £194m compensation, the UK's financial watchdog has announced.  Eighteen investment firms involved in the s...
Summary: Investors who lost money in the split-capital investment trust scandal are to receive £194m compensation from 18 investment firms. The compensation package will be overseen by an independent company. Further details on how investors can claim their share will be announced in the new year.

Title: French suitor holds LSE meeting
Article_Text: European stock market Euronext has met with the London Stock Exchange (LSE) amid speculation that it may be ready to launch a cash bid.  Euronext chief Jean-Francois Theodore held talks with LSE boss ...
Summary: Euronext and the London Stock Exchange met amid speculation of a potential cash bid, with Deutsche Boerse also making a move. The German exchange has offered £1.3bn, while Euronext is rumored to have £1.4bn in place. A deal would create the biggest stock market operator in Europe and the second biggest in the world.

Title: Troubled Marsh under SEC scrutiny
Article_Text: The US stock market regulator is investigating troubled insurance broker Marsh & McLennan's shareholder transactions, the firm has said.  The Securities and Exchange Commission has asked for informati...
Summary: The US stock market regulator is investigating Marsh & McLennan's shareholder transactions, and the company is cooperating with the investigation. The inquiry is also being led by New York's attorney-general, Eliot Spitzer, who is investigating whether insurers rigged the market. The investigation includes dealings in the Trident Funds and may result in significant fines and penalties.

Title: Could Yukos be a blessing in disguise?
Article_Text: Other things being equal, the notion of entrepreneurs languishing in jail while their companies are sold off for a song ought to be bad for business.  But in the looking-glass world of modern Russia, ...
Summary: A new report from the Centre for Economic Policy Research argues that increased tax enforcement in Russia has benefited all firms, including those targeted by tax police, by increasing transparency and efficiency. The report attributes the growth of the Russian stock market to this increased enforcement, particularly in the oil industry.

Title: Nasdaq planning $100m share sale
Article_Text: The owner of the technology-dominated Nasdaq stock index plans to sell shares to the public and list itself on the market it operates.  According to a registration document filed with the Securities a...
Summary: Nasdaq plans to sell shares to the public and list itself on the market it operates, raising $100m, and will not make a profit from the sale.

Title: Giving financial gifts to children
Article_Text: Your child or grandchild may want the latest toy this Christmas, but how about giving them a present that will help their financial future?  Gifts of the financial variety might have a longer lasting ...
Summary: The UK government is introducing a Child Trust Fund to encourage saving among children, with vouchers worth £250 or £500 for low-income families. Parents can top up the fund with up to £1,200 a year, and interest earned is tax-free for children but subject to income tax for parents. Alternative gift options include deposit accounts, Premium Bonds, and investing in the stock market through unit trusts or Exchange Traded Funds.

Title: Air China in $1bn London listing
Article_Text: China's national airline is to make its overseas stock market debut with a dual listing in London and Hong Kong, the London Stock Exchange (LSE) has said.  Air China plans to raise $1bn (£514m) from t...
Summary: China's national airline, Air China, is set to make its overseas stock market debut with a dual listing in London and Hong Kong, raising $1bn. The listing is part of the modernisation of China's airline sector to cope with soaring demand for air travel. The London Stock Exchange has been actively courting Chinese companies to list in London.

Title: Oil prices reach three-month low
Article_Text: Oil prices have fallen heavily for a second day, closing at three-month lows after news that US crude stocks have improved ahead of winter.  London Brent crude closed at $40.15 on Thursday - a drop of...
Summary: US crude stocks have improved ahead of winter, triggering a 5.1% drop in London Brent crude to $40.15 per barrel, its lowest close since mid-September.
