The Energy Information Administration reported a 3.5% increase in US crude stocks, calming worries about winter shortages. The price drop is attributed to mild early-winter weather and stronger fuel inventories, but analysts warn that a cold snap in North America or supply problems could lead to a rebound in prices.

Title: Arsenal 'may seek full share listing'
Article_Text: Arsenal vice-chairman David Dein has said the club may consider seeking a full listing for its shares on the London Stock Exchange.  Speaking at the Soccerex football business forum in Dubai, he said ...
Summary: Arsenal vice-chairman David Dein discussed the club's financial options, including a potential full listing on the London Stock Exchange, after moving to its new stadium. The club is seeking to increase matchday earnings and balance media exposure with attendances. Dein warned of potential saturation in TV coverage of the Premiership.

Title: Markets signal Brazilian recovery
Article_Text: The Brazilian stock market has risen to a record high as investors display growing confidence in the durability of the country's economic recovery.  The main Bovespa index on the Sao Paolo Stock Excha...
Summary: The Brazilian stock market reached a record high, driven by growing confidence in the country's economic recovery, which is expected to grow by 4.5% in 2004. The market's buoyancy reflects optimism about the Brazilian economy, which has seen a decline in unemployment and inflation. Analysts predict the stock market will rise above 25,000 points.

Title: Markets fall on weak dollar fears
Article_Text: Rising oil prices and the sinking dollar hit shares on Monday after a finance ministers' meeting and stern words from Fed chief Alan Greenspan.  The London FTSE fell 0.8% while Tokyo's Nikkei 225 drop...
Summary: Rising oil prices and a sinking dollar led to a decline in shares on Monday, with the London FTSE and Tokyo's Nikkei 225 falling due to concerns over the US deficit and potential funding cuts from Asian states. The euro reached an all-time high against the dollar, while oil prices rose due to concerns over cold weather and potential output cuts from Opec. The US government is using the dollar's decline as a short-term fix to make exports more affordable, but the debt is expected to increase in the long term.

Title: Google shares fall as staff sell
Article_Text: Shares in Google have fallen 6.7% after employees and early investors in the web search took advantage of the first chance to sell their holdings.  Restrictions were imposed ahead of its flotation in ...
Summary: Shares in Google have fallen 6.7% after employees and early investors sold their holdings, but analysts expect demand for stock to hold due to the company's good performance and growth potential.

Title: Five million Germans out of work
Article_Text: Germany's unemployment figure rose above the psychologically important level of five million last month.  On Wednesday, the German Federal Labour Agency said the jobless total had reached 5.037 millio...
Summary: Germany's unemployment figure rose to 5.037 million in January, with a jobless rate of 12.1%, the highest level since the 1930s. The increase is partly due to changes in statistics compilation. The government's controversial 'Hartz IV' reforms are also cited as a factor. The opposition criticized the government's reforms, saying they do not go far enough.

Title: India power shares jump on debut
Article_Text: Shares in India's largest power producer, National Thermal Power Corp (NTPC) have risen 13% on their stock market debut.  The government's partial sell-off of NTPC is part of a controversial programme...
Summary: Shares in India's largest power producer, National Thermal Power Corp (NTPC), have risen 13% on their stock market debut, raising 54 billion rupees ($1.2 billion) from a 865 million share offer. The government's partial sell-off is part of a programme to privatise state-run firms, with analysts predicting it will encourage the government to reduce stakes in more power companies. NTPC, the largest utility company in India, plans to use the funds to meet the growing energy needs of the country's economy.

Title: Turkey turns on the economic charm
Article_Text: Three years after a gruelling economic crisis, Turkey has dressed its economy to impress.  As part of a charm offensive - ahead of 17 December, when the European Union will decide whether to start ent...
Summary: Turkey is preparing to join the European Union, with its economic leaders promoting recent achievements such as growing economy, rising education levels, and booming tourism industry. The country aims to attract $15bn of foreign investment and contribute to the EU budget. However, critics argue that Turkey's massive debt and high debt-to-GDP ratio pose significant economic challenges.

Title: SBC plans post-takeover job cuts
Article_Text: US phone company SBC Communications said it expects to cut around 12,800 jobs following its $16bn (£8.5bn) takeover of former parent AT&T.  SBC said 5,125 positions would go as a result of network eff...
Summary: US phone company SBC Communications expects to cut around 12,800 jobs following its $16bn takeover of AT&T. The takeover will be financed with $15bn of shares and a $1bn special dividend. Estimated cost savings of at least $2bn from 2008 were a main driver for the merger.

Title: German bidder in talks with LSE
Article_Text: Deutsche Boerse bosses have held "constructive, professional and friendly" talks with the London Stock Exchange (LSE), its chief has said.  Werner Seifert met LSE chief executive Clara Furse amid rumo...
Summary: Deutsche Boerse has held talks with the London Stock Exchange, potentially raising its bid to £1.5bn, amid a bid battle with Euronext. The LSE has left the door open for talks, while Euronext has also begun discussions. A deal would create the biggest stock market operator in Europe and the second biggest in the world.

Title: Amex shares up on spin-off news
Article_Text: Shares in American Express surged more than 8% on Tuesday after it said it was to spin off its less profitable financial advisory subsidiary.  The US credit card to travel services giant said off-load...
Summary: Shares in American Express surged more than 8% on Tuesday after the company announced plans to spin off its less profitable financial advisory subsidiary, American Express Financial Advisors (AEFA). AEFA has struggled with poor profits and losses over the years. The spin-off is expected to boost American Express's profitability.

Title: Axa Sun Life cuts bonus payments
Article_Text: Life insurer Axa Sun Life has lowered annual bonus payouts for up to 50,000 with-profits investors.  Regular annual bonus rates on former Axa Equity & Law with-profits policies are to be cut from 2% t...
Summary: Axa Sun Life has lowered annual bonus payouts for up to 50,000 with-profits investors due to poor stock market performance, cutting rates from 2% to 1% for 2004.

Title: Chinese dam firm 'defies Beijing'
Article_Text: The China Three Gorges Project Corp is refusing to obey a government order to stop construction of one of its giant dams, the Chinese state press has said.  The builder of the Three Gorges Dam is cont...
Summary: The China Three Gorges Project Corp is refusing to stop construction of the Xiluodu dam, one of 30 large-scale projects halted due to environmental concerns. The company may face a fine of up to 200,000 yuan. China's State Environmental Protection Agency has ordered the shutdown of 30 projects without proper environmental impact assessments.

Title: Stock market eyes Japan recovery
Article_Text: Japanese shares have ended the year at their highest level since 13 July amidst hopes of an economic recovery during 2005.  The Nikkei index of leading shares gained 7.6% during the year to close at 1...
Summary: Japanese shares ended the year at their highest level since July 13, 2005, with the Nikkei index gaining 7.6% to close at 11,488.76 points. This optimism contrasts with pessimism in the Japanese business community, where business confidence has weakened due to slower economic growth and rising oil prices. Traders expect the global economy to benefit Japan despite its recent recession concerns.

Title: Iraqi voters turn to economic issues
Article_Text: Beyond the desperate security situation in Iraq lies an economy in tatters.  A vicious cycle of unemployment, poor social services and poverty has been made worse by a lack of investment. So there is ...
Summary: Iraq's economy is in a dire state due to unemployment, poor social services, and poverty, with many Iraqis hoping an elected government will address these issues. The country's oil revenues have exceeded $22bn since 2003, but serious problems remain, including a growing divide between the rich and the poor. Foreign firms are investing in the country's finance and reconstruction sectors, but this has raised concerns among some Iraqis.

Title: EU 'too slow' on economic reforms
Article_Text: Most EU countries have failed to put in place policies aimed at making Europe the world's most competitive economy by the end of the decade, a report says.  The study, undertaken by the European Commi...
Summary: A report by the European Commission says most EU countries have failed to meet their economic targets, including the Lisbon Agenda, which aimed to make Europe the world's most competitive economy by 2010.

Title: China continues breakneck growth
Article_Text: China's economy has expanded by a breakneck 9.5% during 2004, faster than predicted and well above 2003's 9.1%.  The news may mean more limits on investment and lending as Beijing tries to take the ec...
Summary: China's economy expanded by 9.5% in 2004, faster than predicted, but with slowing industrial growth and rising consumer prices, which could lead to higher interest rates and inflation.

Title: Japan's ageing workforce: built to last
Article_Text: In his twenties he battled tuberculosis for eight years, then went on to run his own clothing business before marrying in his late thirties. And the 101-year-old Torao Toshitsune has eaten raw fish pr...
Summary: Japan is facing a demographic crisis with a low birth rate and an aging population, which could lead to financial strain and economic stagnation. The country's public sector debt is already high, and the cost of running its welfare state is expected to double by 2010. To address this, some experts suggest further welfare reform, immigration, or a shift towards financial services.

Title: GE sees 'excellent' world economy
Article_Text: US behemoth General Electric has posted an 18% jump in quarterly sales, and in profits, and declared itself "in great shape".  "We are benefiting from our growth initiatives and an excellent global ec...
Summary: General Electric has posted an 18% jump in quarterly sales and profits, with CEO Jeff Immelt attributing the growth to initiatives and a strong global economy. The company forecasts sustained growth of 10-15% for this year and next. GE's shares rose initially but ended the day lower.

Title: UK economy facing 'major risks'
Article_Text: The UK manufacturing sector will continue to face "serious challenges" over the next two years, the British Chamber of Commerce (BCC) has said.  The group's quarterly survey of companies found exports...
Summary: The UK manufacturing sector faces serious challenges, with exports picking up but overall growth slowing due to concerns over exchange rates and persistent inability to sustain recovery. Domestic sales growth fell, employment in manufacturing decreased, and job expectations were at their lowest level for a year. The outlook for the service sector is uncertain despite an increase in exports and orders.

Title: Bank holds interest rate at 4.75%
Article_Text: The Bank of England has left interest rates on hold again at 4.75%, in a widely-predicted move.  Rates went up five times from November 2003 - as the bank sought to cool the housing market and consume...
Summary: The Bank of England has left interest rates on hold at 4.75%, despite a slowdown in manufacturing and consumer spending, as well as disappointing retail sales over Christmas. Analysts predict a further slowdown in the housing market, which could worsen economic conditions. The Bank is concerned about rising personal debt.

Title: Tobacco giants hail court ruling
Article_Text: US tobacco companies have welcomed an appeal court's decision to reject the government's $280bn (£155bn) claim for alleged deceit about smoking dangers.  Tobacco stocks rose sharply on Wall Street aft...
Summary: An appeal court rejected the government's $280bn claim against US tobacco companies, citing federal anti-racketeering laws. Tobacco stocks rose sharply after the 2-1 decision. The government had accused tobacco firms of deceit over smoking dangers, but the companies denied conspiracy and said they had already met many of the government's demands in a 1998 settlement.

Title: Steady job growth continues in US
Article_Text: The US created fewer jobs than expected in December, but analysts said that the dip in hiring was not enough to derail the world's biggest economy.  According to Labor Department figures, 157,000 new ...
Summary: The US economy added 157,000 new jobs in December, bringing the total to 2.2 million, the best showing in five years. The unemployment rate remained at 5.4%. Analysts say the conditions are set for steady growth in 2005, despite some concerns about job creation.

Title: Glazer makes new Man Utd approach
Article_Text: Malcolm Glazer has made a fresh approach to buy Manchester United, which could lead to a bid valuing the Premiership club at £800m.  The US tycoon, who has been wooing the club for the last 12 months,...
Summary: Malcolm Glazer has made a fresh approach to buy Manchester United, which could lead to a bid valuing the Premiership club at £800m. The US tycoon has approached the United board with detailed proposals, which are expected to contain substantially less debt. The club's board has confirmed the proposal, but talks will not resume unless Glazer comes up with definitive proposals.

Title: Wall Street cheers Bush victory
Article_Text: The US stock market has closed higher in response to George W Bush's victory in the presidential elections.  The benchmark Dow Jones share index closed more than 1% higher at 10,137, while the Nasdaq ...
Summary: US stocks closed higher on November 3, 2004, following George W. Bush's victory in the presidential election, with the Dow Jones index rising 1% to 10,137. Investors believed Bush's policies were more business-friendly than John Kerry's, and relief that a clear winner emerged from a tight poll contributed to the market's rally. The Dow had lost 5% of its value in the weeks following the 2000 election, which was marked by uncertainty over the White House occupant.

Title: Business confidence dips in Japan
Article_Text: Business confidence among Japanese manufacturers has weakened for the first time since March 2003, the quarterly Tankan survey has found.  Slower economic growth, rising oil prices, a stronger yen and...
Summary: Business confidence among Japanese manufacturers has weakened for the first time since March 2003, due to slower economic growth, rising oil prices, and a stronger yen. The economy minister, Heizo Takenaka, expects the recovery to continue, but with slower growth. Japanese firms have increased capital investment expectations.

Title: Millions 'to lose textile jobs'
Article_Text: Millions of the world's poorest textile trade workers will lose their jobs under new trade rules to be introduced in the new year, a charity has warned.  The World Trade Organisation (WTO) is to end i...
Summary: The World Trade Organisation is ending its Multi-Fibre Agreement, which will lead to job losses for millions of textile trade workers, particularly in Bangladesh. The WTO claims that funding is available to help countries transition to a fully liberalised market. Christian Aid warns that many workers could end up in worse jobs, including the sex trade.

Title: Dutch bank to lay off 2,850 staff
Article_Text: ABN Amro, the Netherlands' largest bank, is to cut 2,850 jobs as a result of falling profits.  The cuts - amounting to 3% of the bank's workforce - will result in a one-off charge of 790m euros ($1.1b...
Summary: ABN Amro is cutting 2,850 jobs due to falling profits, with 1,100 in investment banking, 1,200 in IT, and 550 in human resources. The bank will incur a one-off charge of 790m euros. This move is part of a restructuring to improve efficiency and reduce administrative costs.

Title: Fannie Mae 'should restate books'
Article_Text: US mortgage company Fannie Mae should restate its earnings, a move that is likely to put a billion-dollar dent in its accounts, watchdogs have said.  The Securities & Exchange Commission accused Fanni...
Summary: US mortgage company Fannie Mae is likely to restate its earnings due to SEC accusations of non-compliance with accounting standards. The move may impact its accounts by a billion dollars. The SEC's comments may increase pressure on Congress to strengthen supervision of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.
Key_Entities: Office of Federal Housing Enterprise Oversight

Title: US to rule on Yukos refuge call
Article_Text: Yukos has said a US bankruptcy court will decide whether to block Russia's impending auction of its main production arm on Thursday.  The Russian oil firm has filed for bankruptcy protection in the US...
Summary: Yukos has filed for bankruptcy protection in the US to halt the forced sale of its main production arm, Yuganskneftegas, to pay a $27bn back tax bill. The Russian government is due to auction off the firm on December 19. Yukos claims the sale is illegal and will cause the company to suffer immediate and irreparable harm.

Title: J&J agrees $25bn Guidant deal
Article_Text: Pharmaceutical giant Johnson & Johnson has agreed to buy medical technology firm Guidant for $25.4bn (£13bn).  Guidant is a key producer of equipment that combats heart problems such as implant defibr...
Summary: Johnson & Johnson has agreed to buy medical technology firm Guidant for $25.4bn, aiming to offset a slowing drug business and capitalize on increasing demand for defibrillators. The deal is expected to be completed after the firm pays $76 for each Guidant share. US antitrust regulators may require the firms to shed overlapping stent operations.

Title: Libya takes $1bn in unfrozen funds
Article_Text: Libya has withdrawn $1bn in assets from the US, assets which had previously been frozen for almost 20 years, the Libyan central bank has said.  The move came after the US lifted a trade ban to reward ...
Summary: Libya has withdrawn $1bn in assets from the US after the US lifted a trade ban, which had been in place for almost 20 years. The assets were previously frozen due to Libya's alleged involvement in terrorist acts. The US ban was lifted in April after Libya agreed to give up weapons of mass destruction and compensate Lockerbie victims.

Title: Cactus diet deal for Phytopharm
Article_Text: A slimming aid made from a southern African cactus is set to be developed by UK firm Phytopharm and Unilever.  Anglo-Dutch food giant Unilever will help the pharmaceutical firm develop the snacks cont...
Summary: UK firm Phytopharm and Unilever are developing a slimming aid made from a southern African cactus, with potential sales of $600m a year. Phytopharm will receive an initial fee and royalties from Unilever. The deal is seen as a way to restore market faith in Phytopharm's pipeline.

Title: Brazil plays down Varig rescue
Article_Text: The Brazilian government has played down claims that it could step in to save the country's biggest airline.  Brazil's airport authority chief Carlos Wilson had claimed the government was on the brink...
Summary: The Brazilian government has downplayed claims of stepping in to save Varig, the country's largest airline, amid a debt burden of 6.5 billion reais. Vice President Jose Alencar said the government is still looking for a solution, while Airport Authority Chief Carlos Wilson claimed President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva had decided to intervene. Varig operates in 18 countries and has been affected by Brazil's economic downturn.

Title: Bombardier chief to leave company
Article_Text: Shares in train and plane-making giant Bombardier have fallen to a 10-year low following the departure of its chief executive and two members of the board.  Paul Tellier, who was also Bombardier's pre...
Summary: Shares in Bombardier have fallen to a 10-year low following the departure of its CEO and two board members amid an ongoing restructuring. Laurent Beaudoin will take on the role of CEO under a newly created management structure. The company's restructuring plans, drawn up by former CEO Paul Tellier, will continue to be implemented.

Title: Brazil approves bankruptcy reform
Article_Text: A major reform of Brazil's bankruptcy laws has been approved by the country's Congress, in a move which it is hoped will cut the cost of borrowing.  The bill, proposed in 1993, has finally been approv...
Summary: Brazil's Congress has approved a major reform of the country's bankruptcy laws, which will give priority to creditors and limit payments to workers. The new legislation aims to reduce the cost of borrowing. The law also makes it more difficult for a company to declare bankruptcy and provides protection for firms during the recovery process.

Title: Retail sales show festive fervour
Article_Text: UK retail sales were better than expected in November as Christmas shoppers began their seasonal flock to the High Street, figures show.  The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said retail sales ros...
Summary: UK retail sales rose 0.6% on the month and 6.1% on the year in November, defying analyst expectations. The unexpected rise in sales may be due to retailers' aggressive tactics, such as one-day discount sales. The data also supported the view that sterling is due for a rally.

Title: Cairn shares slump on oil setback
Article_Text: Shares in Cairn Energy, a UK oil firm, have closed down 18% after a disappointing drilling update and a warning over possible tax demands.  The company said tests had shown no significant finds in one...
Summary: Shares in Cairn Energy have fallen 18% after a disappointing drilling update and a warning over possible tax demands from the Indian government. The company had previously announced significant oil finds in India, but estimates have been revised downward. Cairn Energy's CEO, Bill Gammell, disputes the government's position on tax payments.

Title: French boss to leave EADS
Article_Text: The French co-head of European defence and aerospace group EADS Philippe Camus is to leave his post.  Mr Camus said in a statement that he has accepted the invitation to return full-time to the Lagard...
Summary: Philippe Camus, French co-head of EADS, is leaving his post to return to the Lagardere group, and Noel Forgeard will replace him, bringing an end to the power struggle. The departure of Camus and the support of Forgeard by the Lagardere group should stabilize the company. The A380 project is running over budget, but Forgeard denies the current overrun.

Title: AstraZeneca hit by drug failure
Article_Text: Shares in Anglo-Swedish drug have closed down 8% in UK trade after the failure of its Iressa drug in a major clinical trial.  The lung cancer drug did not significantly prolong survival in patients wi...
Summary: Shares in AstraZeneca have fallen 8% in UK trade after the failure of its Iressa drug in a major clinical trial, which did not significantly prolong survival in patients with lung cancer. The company's anti-coagulant pill Exanta was also rejected by the US in October. Meanwhile, its cholesterol drug Crestor is facing mounting safety concerns. AstraZeneca has appointed a new executive director to the board to address these issues.

Title: Strong quarterly growth for Nike
Article_Text: Nike has reported its best second-quarter earnings, helped by strong demand for its athletic shoes and Converse sneakers.  The global sports giant said it posted a profit of $261.9m (£135.6m), for the...
Summary: Nike has reported its best second-quarter earnings, driven by strong demand for its athletic shoes and Converse sneakers. The company's profit and revenues increased significantly, with profits reaching an all-time high. Nike attributes the growth to solid performance across its global portfolio and favourable exchange rates.

Title: Stormy year for property insurers
Article_Text: A string of storms, typhoons and earthquakes has made 2004 the most expensive year on record for property insurers, according to Swiss Re.  The world's second biggest insurer said disasters around the...
Summary: 2004 was the most expensive year on record for property insurers, with global property claims reaching $42bn, according to Swiss Re. The rise in claims was attributed to tightly packed populations in disaster-prone areas. The largest claims came from the US and Japan, with a total cost of $105bn.

Title: Parmalat sues 45 banks over crash
Article_Text: Parmalat has sued 45 banks as it tries to reclaim money paid to banks before the scandal-hit Italian dairy company went bust last year.  The firm collapsed with debts of about 14bn euros ($19bn; £10bn...
Summary: Parmalat has sued 45 banks to reclaim money paid to them before the company went bust, claiming they were aware of financial troubles but continued to work with the company for commissions. The company's new boss, Enrico Bondi, has taken legal action against several lenders. Parmalat is also preparing further lawsuits. The company is seeking to recover money paid to financial institutions under Italian law.

Title: Irish company hit by Iraqi report
Article_Text: Shares in Irish oil company Petrel Resources have lost more than 50% of their value on a report that the firm has failed to win a contract in Iraq.  Reuters news agency reported that Iraq's Oil Minist...
Summary: Shares in Petrel Resources have lost over 50% of their value after Iraq's Oil Ministry awarded contracts to Canadian and Turkish companies, IOG and Everasia, respectively. The contracts are valued at $500m and aim to develop two oil fields. Petrel Resources has denied receiving information from Iraqi authorities to confirm or deny the report.

Title: Yukos unit fetches $9bn at auction
Article_Text: A little-known Russian company has bought the main production unit of oil giant Yukos at auction in Moscow.  Baikal Finance Group outbid favourite Gazprom, the state-controlled gas monopoly, to buy Yu...
Summary: A Russian company, Baikal Finance Group, has bought the main production unit of oil giant Yukos at an auction in Moscow for 260.75 billion roubles ($9.37 billion). Yukos claims the auction was illegal and has vowed to take legal action against the winner, while Baikal has paid a deposit of nearly $1.7 billion to the Russian Federal Property Fund. The sale comes despite a US court's restraining order on the sale, which would have allowed Yukos' current management to retain control of the business.

Title: S&N extends Indian beer venture
Article_Text: The UK's biggest brewer, Scottish and Newcastle (S&N), is to buy 37.5% of India's United Breweries in a deal worth 4.66bn rupees ($106m:£54.6m).  S&N will buy a 17.5% equity stake in United, maker of ...
Summary: UK brewer Scottish and Newcastle is buying 37.5% of India's United Breweries in a deal worth 4.66bn rupees, with Vijay Mallya also holding a similar stake. The deal is a natural development of their joint venture, which includes a joint venture business and a UK investment in the Indian brewer. The deal will see S&N invest 2.47bn rupees in United.

Title: Euronext 'poised to make LSE bid'
Article_Text: Pan-European group Euronext is poised to launch a bid for the London Stock Exchange, UK media reports say.  Last week, the LSE rejected a takeover proposal from German rival Deutsche Boerse - the 530 ...
Summary: Euronext is reportedly working on a bid for the London Stock Exchange, which was previously rejected by the LSE. The LSE believes the bid undervalues the business, but is open to further talks. Euronext has a presence in London and has appointed additional advisors to support the bid.

Title: Christmas shoppers flock to tills
Article_Text: Shops all over the UK reported strong sales on the last Saturday before Christmas with some claiming record-breaking numbers of festive shoppers.  A spokesman for Manchester's Trafford Centre said it ...
Summary: Shops across the UK reported strong sales on the last Saturday before Christmas, with some claiming record-breaking numbers of festive shoppers. Sales were up 5% at Manchester's Trafford Centre and 2% up on the same time last year at Bluewater in Kent. The Regent Street Association expects a busy Christmas period with sales exceeding £200m.

Title: Mystery surrounds new Yukos owner
Article_Text: The fate of Russia's Yuganskneftegas - the oil firm sold to a little-known buyer on Sunday - is the subject of frantic speculation in Moscow.  Baikal Finance Group emerged as the auction winner, agree...
Summary: Russia's Yuganskneftegas oil firm was sold to Baikal Finance Group for 260.75bn roubles, sparking speculation about Gazprom's involvement. The sale has destroyed Yukos, once the owner of Yuganskneftegas, and its founder Mikhail Khodorkovsky has threatened legal action. Gazprom has denied being behind the purchase.

Title: Euronext joins bid battle for LSE
Article_Text: Pan-European stock market Euronext has approached the London Stock Exchange (LSE) about a possible takeover bid.  "The approach is at an early stage and therefore does not require a response at this p...
Summary: Euronext has approached the London Stock Exchange (LSE) about a possible takeover bid, following a rejected £1.3bn offer from Deutsche Boerse. The LSE's shares surged after the announcement, and experts expect a bidding war for Europe's biggest stock market. A deal with Euronext could offer more cost savings than a deal with Deutsche Boerse.

Title: Iraq and Afghanistan in WTO talks
Article_Text: The World Trade Organisation (WTO) is to hold membership talks with both Iraq and Afghanistan.  But Iran's bid to join the trade body has been refused after the US blocked its application for the 21st...
Summary: The World Trade Organisation (WTO) will hold membership talks with Iraq and Afghanistan, while Iran's bid has been refused for the 21st time due to US opposition. Membership benefits include equal treatment in markets and association with globalisation. The US blocked Iran's application, but several nations criticised the approach.

Title: Diageo to buy US wine firm
Article_Text: Diageo, the world's biggest spirits company, has agreed to buy Californian wine company Chalone for $260m (£134m) in an all-cash deal.  Although Diageo's best-known brands include Smirnoff vodka and G...
Summary: Diageo, the world's biggest spirits company, has agreed to buy Californian wine company Chalone for $260m in an all-cash deal. The deal is expected to be approved by US regulators in the first quarter of 2005. Chalone will be integrated into Diageo's existing US wine business.

Title: Tokyo says deflation 'controlled'
Article_Text: The Japanese government has forecast that the country's economic growth will slow to 1.6% in the next fiscal year starting in April 2005.  While it predicts this fall from the current 2.1% level, it s...
Summary: The Japanese government has forecast a slowdown in economic growth to 1.6% in the next fiscal year, while predicting a 2% growth rate in 2006/07. The economy is expected to see a 0.1% rise in the consumer price index, the first gain since 2000/01. The government aims to overcome deflation.

Title: No seasonal lift for house market
Article_Text: A swathe of figures have provided further evidence of a slowdown in the UK property market.  The Council of Mortgage Lenders (CML), British Bankers Association (BBA) and Building Societies Association...
Summary: The UK property market is slowing down, with mortgage lending falling by 4% in November and the number of new home buyers decreasing. The average asking price of a home fell by over £600, and estate agents are expecting a third more properties on their books in 2005. Mortgage lenders and economists predict that property prices will either fall or stagnate in 2005.

Title: Yukos seeks court action on sale
Article_Text: Yukos will return to a US court on Wednesday to seek sanctions against Baikal Finance Group, the little-known firm which has bought its main asset.  Yukos has said it will sue Baikal and others involv...
Summary: Yukos will return to a US court on Wednesday to seek sanctions against Baikal Finance Group, the firm that bought Yuganskneftegas for $20bn, in damages for the alleged illegal auction. The Russian government forced the sale of Yukos' most lucrative asset as part of its action to enforce a $27bn back tax bill, which Yukos' US lawyers claim is an attempt to destroy the company due to its founder Mikhail Khodorkovsky's political ambitions. The future ownership of Yuganskneftegas remains unclear, with speculation that Baikal may be a front for other interests, including Surgutneftegas and Gazprom.

Title: Indy buys into India paper
Article_Text: Irish publishing group Independent News & Media is buying up a 26% stake in Indian newspaper company Jagran in a deal worth 25m euros ($34.1m).  Jagran publishes India's top-selling daily newspaper, t...
Summary: Irish publishing group Independent News & Media is acquiring a 26% stake in Indian newspaper company Jagran for 25m euros. The deal comes as the company reported strong revenue growth across its major markets. Independent News & Media's chief executive, Sir Anthony O'Reilly, expressed confidence in the company's earnings for 2005.

Title: Senior Fannie Mae bosses resign
Article_Text: The two most senior executives at US mortgage giant Fannie Mae have resigned after accounting irregularities were uncovered at the company.  Chief executive Franklin Raines, a former senior official i...
Summary: The two most senior executives at Fannie Mae, Chief Executive Franklin Raines and Chief Financial Officer Tim Howard, have resigned after accounting irregularities were uncovered. The company may have to restate its earnings by up to $9bn. Fannie Mae is the second largest financial institution in the US and supplies funds to the $8 trillion mortgage market.
Key_Entities: Office of Federal Housing Enterprise Oversight

Title: Cannabis hopes for drug firm
Article_Text: A prescription cannabis drug made by UK biotech firm GW Pharmaceuticals is set to be approved in Canada.  The drug is used to treat the central nervous system and alleviate the symptoms of multiple sc...
Summary: GW Pharmaceuticals' prescription cannabis drug Sativex is set to be approved in Canada for treating multiple sclerosis, with Canadian authorities considering the drug for approval after UK regulators expressed interest in more evidence. The drug could be legally available to MS sufferers in Canada within the next few months. Final approval is expected to be a formality.

Title: Bush to get 'tough' on deficit
Article_Text: US president George W Bush has pledged to introduce a "tough" federal budget next February in a bid to halve the country's deficit in five years.  The US budget and its trade deficit are both deep in ...
Summary: US President George W. Bush has pledged to introduce a "tough" federal budget in February to halve the country's deficit in five years, with strict discipline on non-defence spending. The federal budget deficit reached a record $412bn in the 12 months to September 30, and Mr. Bush aims to address this with a budget that prioritizes military spending, homeland protection, and other government priorities. The goal is to send a signal to financial markets and address long-term deficit issues.

Title: House prices drop as sales slow
Article_Text: House prices fell further in November and property sale times lengthened as rate rises took their toll, the Royal Institute of Chartered Surveyors found.  A total of 48% of chartered surveyor estate a...
Summary: House prices fell further in November, with 48% of chartered surveyors reporting lower prices, and the number of sales dropped 32% to an average of 22 per surveyor. The Bank of England's decision not to increase interest rates further and the healthy economy are contributing to the slowdown. The market is expected to pick up in the second half of 2005, with a 3% rise in prices over the coming 12 months.

Title: Fresh hope after Argentine crisis
Article_Text: Three years after Argentina was hit by a deadly economic crisis, there is fresh hope.  The country's economy is set to grow about 8% this year after seeing 9% growth last year, a sharp turnaround from...
Summary: Argentina's economy is expected to grow 8% this year, a sharp turnaround from 2002's 11% decline, with the unemployment rate set to drop below 13% by the end of the year. The country has made a remarkable recovery from a devastating recession, with the International Monetary Fund acknowledging the strong performance of the economy.

Title: Disney settles disclosure charges
Article_Text: Walt Disney has settled charges from US federal regulators that it failed to disclose how family members of directors were employed by the company.  The media giant was not fined by the Securities and...
Summary: Walt Disney has settled charges with US federal regulators for failing to disclose relationships between directors and family members, without being fined. The company agreed to refrain from future violations. Disney employed adult children of directors without informing investors. The SEC found several undisclosed payments and relationships.

Title: Putin backs state grab for Yukos
Article_Text: Russia's president has defended the purchase of Yukos' key production unit by state-owned oil firm Rosneft, saying it followed free market principles.  Vladimir Putin said it was quite within the righ...
Summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin defended the purchase of Yukos' key production unit by state-owned oil firm Rosneft, stating it followed free market principles. The deal, which amounts to the renationalization of a major chunk of Russia's oil industry, was made possible by a forced auction and allows Rosneft to control about 16% of Russia's total crude oil output. The move comes after more than a year of wrangling and follows a period of "cowboy capitalism" in Russia, where the state is now safeguarding its interests using market methods.

Title: Troubled Marsh under SEC scrutiny
Article_Text: The US stock market regulator is investigating troubled insurance broker Marsh & McLennan's shareholder transactions, the firm has said.  The Securities and Exchange Commission has asked for informati...
Summary: The US stock market regulator is investigating Marsh & McLennan's shareholder transactions, and the company is cooperating with the investigation. The inquiry is also being led by New York's attorney-general, Eliot Spitzer, who is investigating whether insurers rigged the market. The investigation includes dealings in the Trident Funds and may result in significant fines and penalties.

Title: US firm pulls out of Iraq
Article_Text: A US company has pulled out of a major contract to rebuild Iraq's transport system after attacks on reconstruction efforts, Pentagon officials have said.  Contrack International, of Arlington, Virgini...
Summary: A US company, Contrack International, has withdrawn from a $325m contract to rebuild Iraq's transport system due to security concerns, and the Pentagon has taken over its management. The withdrawal is thought to be the largest cancellation to date. The Pentagon says security concerns are a major reason for the slow pace of reconstruction in Iraq.

Title: Boeing secures giant Japan order
Article_Text: Boeing is to supply Japan Airlines with up to 50 of its forthcoming 7E7 planes in a deal that could be worth as much as $6bn (£3.1bn) for the US giant.  Japan Airlines has made a firm order for 30 of ...
Summary: Boeing is set to supply Japan Airlines with up to 50 of its 7E7 planes in a deal worth up to $6bn, with Japan Airlines ordering 30 at $120m each. Airbus has also announced a pre-sale of its A350 rival, with Air Europe ordering 10 at $180m each. Both aircraft are designed to be fuel-efficient in the 200- to 300-seat sector.

Title: Banker loses sexism claim
Article_Text: A former executive at the London offices of Merrill Lynch has lost her £7.5m ($14.6m) sex discrimination case against the US investment bank.  An employment tribunal dismissed Stephanie Villalba's all...
Summary: A former Merrill Lynch executive, Stephanie Villalba, lost her £7.5m sex discrimination case but won her claim of unfair dismissal after being sacked in 2003. The tribunal found her unfairly dismissed due to her removal from a senior post, but the extent of damages will be assessed in the New Year. The decision was seen as a test case for the bank's procedures.

Title: Building giant in asbestos payout
Article_Text: Australian building products group James Hardie has agreed to pay $1.1bn (£568m) to victims of asbestos-related diseases.  The landmark deal could see thousands of people suffering from lung diseases ...
Summary: Australian building products group James Hardie has agreed to pay $1.1bn to victims of asbestos-related diseases, following a state inquiry that found the company misled the public about its asbestos-related liabilities. The deal is subject to shareholder approval. James Hardie was once Australia's biggest supplier of asbestos building materials.

Title: Police detain Chinese milk bosses
Article_Text: Chinese police have detained three top executives at milk firm Yili, with reports suggesting that they are being investigated for embezzlement.  Yili - full name Inner Mongolia Yili Industrial - confi...
Summary: Chinese police have detained three top executives at milk firm Yili, who are being investigated for embezzlement. Yili, China's third-largest milk producer, is holding an emergency meeting to debate the issue. The company's shares were suspended after falling 10% on Monday.

Title: India's Deccan seals $1.8bn deal
Article_Text: Air Deccan has ordered 30 Airbus A320 planes in a $1.8bn (£931m) deal as India's first low-cost airline expands in the fast-growing domestic market.  Air Deccan was set up last year and wants to lure ...
Summary: Air Deccan has ordered 30 Airbus A320 planes in a $1.8bn deal to expand in India's growing domestic market. The airline aims to lure travellers away from the railway network and pricier rivals. India's booming economy has boosted personal spending power and helped swell the middle classes.

Title: Venezuela and China sign oil deal
Article_Text: Venezuelan president Hugo Chavez has offered China wide-ranging access to the country's oil reserves.  The offer, made as part of a trade deal between the two countries, will allow China to operate oi...
Summary: Venezuela has offered China wide-ranging access to its oil reserves as part of a trade deal, allowing China to operate oil fields and invest in new refineries. Venezuela aims to diversify its sales to reduce dependence on the US, while China seeks to lessen its reliance on Middle Eastern oil imports. The deal includes plans for China to supply 120,000 barrels of fuel oil per month.

Title: Jarvis sells Tube stake to Spain
Article_Text: Shares in engineering group Jarvis have soared more than 16% on news that it is offloading its stake in London underground consortium Tube Lines.  The sale of the 33% stake to Spain's Ferrovial for £1...
Summary: Shares in Jarvis have soared 16% after the company sold its 33% stake in Tube Lines to Ferrovial for £146m, providing a lifeline to its debts. The sale will allow Jarvis to extend its credit facilities until March 2006. The company plans to focus on UK rail renewal, roads, and plant hire work.

Title: Honda wins China copyright ruling
Article_Text: Japan's Honda has won a copyright case in Beijing, further evidence that China is taking a tougher line on protecting intellectual property rights.  A court ruled that Chongqing Lifan Industry Group m...
Summary: A court in Beijing ruled that Chongqing Lifan Industry Group must stop selling Honda brand motorbikes and pay 1.47m yuan in compensation. China is taking a tougher line on protecting intellectual property rights, with analysts saying internationally recognized regulation is key to its economic development plans. Foreign companies have won cases in China, boosting optimism that attitudes are changing.

Title: Air Jamaica back in state control
Article_Text: The Jamaican government is regaining control of Air Jamaica in an bid to help the ailing company out of its financial difficulties.  The firm has failed to make money since the state sold a majority s...
Summary: The Jamaican government is regaining control of Air Jamaica to help the company recover from financial difficulties, which include high fuel costs and the impact of the 9/11 attacks. The company will be restructured with the aim of finding a new buyer. Air Jamaica transports a significant portion of the island's passengers.

Title: Battered dollar hits another low
Article_Text: The dollar has fallen to a new record low against the euro after data fuelled fresh concerns about the US economy.  The greenback hit $1.3516 in thin New York trade, before rallying to $1.3509. The do...
Summary: The US dollar has fallen to a new record low against the euro due to concerns about the US economy, with data showing a 12% decline in new home sales and a 0.2% growth in consumer spending. France's finance minister, Herve Gaymard, has called for coordinated management of currency controls. The US government supports a strong dollar but is allowing market forces to determine its strength.

Title: Quake's economic costs emerging
Article_Text: Asian governments and international agencies are reeling at the potential economic devastation left by the Asian tsunami and floods.  World Bank president James Wolfensohn has said his agency is "only...
Summary: Asian governments and international agencies are reeling at the potential economic devastation left by the Asian tsunami and floods. The tragedy has left at least 25,000 people dead, with Sri Lanka, Thailand, India and Indonesia worst hit. Economists believe several of the 10 countries hit by the giant waves could see a slowdown in growth.

Title: Disaster claims 'less than $10bn'
Article_Text: Insurers have sought to calm fears that they face huge losses after an earthquake and giant waves killed at least 38,000 people in southern Asia.  Munich Re and Swiss Re, the world's two biggest reins...
Summary: Insurers have sought to calm fears about huge losses after a devastating earthquake and tsunami in southern Asia, with total claims expected to be less than $10bn. Rebuilding costs are likely to be cheaper than in developed countries, and many of those affected will not have insurance. Insurers have not yet assessed the full economic impact of the damage.
Key_Entities: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

Title: India-Pakistan peace boosts trade
Article_Text: Calmer relations between India and Pakistan are paying economic dividends, with new figures showing bilateral trade up threefold in the summer.  The value of trade in April-July rose to $186.3m (£97m)...
Summary: Bilateral trade between India and Pakistan has increased threefold, with trade valued at $186.3m in April-July 2003, compared to $64.4m in the same period in 2003. The Indian Government expects trade to continue growing, with the South Asian Free Trade Area Agreement set to start in 2006. India's overall exports are expected to reach $60bn, while Pakistan's are set to hit $12bn.
Key_Entities: South Asian Free Trade Area Agreement

Title: US to probe airline travel chaos
Article_Text: The US government is to investigate two airlines- US Airways and Delta Air Lines' Comair subsidiary - after travel chaos over the Christmas weekend.  Staff calling in sick at US Airways and computer f...
Summary: The US government is investigating US Airways and Delta Air Lines' Comair subsidiary after travel chaos over the Christmas weekend, leaving 30,000 passengers stranded and 10,000 pieces of baggage undelivered.

Title: S Korean lender faces liquidation
Article_Text: Creditors of South Korea's top credit card firm have said they will put the company into liquidation if its ex-parent firm fails to back a bail-out.  LG Card's creditors have given LG group until Wedn...
Summary: LG Card's creditors are threatening to put the company into liquidation if the LG Group fails to back a $1.1bn rescue package, which would give control to the creditors. The firm avoided bankruptcy in 2004 with a $4.5bn bail-out. LG Card owes $12.05bn and is at risk of being delisted from the Korea Stock Exchange due to high debt levels.

Title: Dollar hits new low versus euro
Article_Text: The US dollar has continued its record-breaking slide and has tumbled to a new low against the euro.  Investors are betting that the European Central Bank (ECB) will not do anything to weaken the euro...
Summary: The US dollar has fallen to a new low against the euro, with investors predicting further decline due to the US trade deficit and the European Central Bank's inaction.

Title: Mild winter drives US oil down 6%
Article_Text: US oil prices have fallen by 6%, driven down by forecasts of a mild winter in the densely populated northeast.  Light crude oil futures fell $2.86 to $41.32 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchang...
Summary: US oil prices have fallen by 6% due to forecasts of a mild winter in the northeast, while still being 30% more expensive than in 2004 due to growing demand and refinery bottlenecks.

Title: Share boost for feud-hit Reliance
Article_Text: The board of Indian conglomerate Reliance has agreed a share buy-back, to counter the effects of a power struggle in the controlling family.  The buy-back is a victory for chairman Mukesh Ambani, whos...
Summary: The Reliance board has agreed to a share buy-back to counter a power struggle in the controlling family, with chairman Mukesh Ambani's plan approved despite opposition from his brother Anil.

Title: Giant waves damage S Asia economy
Article_Text: Governments, aid agencies, insurers and travel firms are among those counting the cost of the massive earthquake and waves that hammered southern Asia.  The worst-hit areas are Sri Lanka, India, Indon...
Summary: The massive earthquake and tsunami in southern Asia have caused widespread destruction and loss of life, with at least 23,000 people killed. The World Bank estimates that $5 billion in aid is needed, while the International Monetary Fund has promised rapid action to help governments cope. The tourism industry, which provides jobs for 19 million people, has been severely impacted.
