Title: Asia shares defy post-quake gloom
Article_Text: Thailand has become the first of the 10 southern Asian nations battered by giant waves at the weekend to cut its economic forecast.  Thailand's economy is now expected to grow by 5.7% in 2005, rather ...
Summary: Thailand has cut its economic forecast due to the impact of giant waves from tsunamis, while other southern Asian nations seem to be less concerned about the economic impact. Investors in large firms have reached record highs, but individuals who have lost their livelihoods are not seeing the same optimism.

Title: Israeli economy picking up pace
Article_Text: Israel's economy is forecast to grow by 4.2% in 2004 as it continues to emerge from a three-year recession.  The main driver of the faster-than-expected expansion has been exports, with tourism seeing...
Summary: Israel's economy is forecast to grow by 4.2% in 2004, driven by exports and tourism, despite a strike by public sector workers earlier this year. The economy has benefited from a quieter period in Palestinian-Israeli violence and global demand for technology products. Growth figures come despite a slight slowdown in the second half of the year.

Title: S Korea spending boost to economy
Article_Text: South Korea will boost state spending next year in an effort to create jobs and kick start its sputtering economy.  It has earmarked 100 trillion won ($96bn) for the first six months of 2005, 60% of i...
Summary: South Korea plans to boost state spending to create jobs and stimulate its economy, earmarking 100 trillion won for the first six months of 2005. The government aims to create 400,000 jobs and focus on infrastructure and home building. However, some experts are skeptical about the effectiveness of the plan.

Title: Soros group warns of Kazakh close
Article_Text: The Open Society Institute (OSI), financed by billionaire George Soros, has accused Kazakhstan officials of trying to close down its local office.  A demand for unpaid taxes and fines of $600,000 (£42...
Summary: The Open Society Institute has accused Kazakhstan officials of trying to close down its local office due to a demand for unpaid taxes and fines, claiming it is a politically motivated move. The OSI has paid the money and denies any role in the alleged toppling of Georgia's former president. The organization has withdrawn from several countries in the region.

Title: Deutsche attacks Yukos case
Article_Text: German investment bank Deutsche Bank has challenged the right of Yukos to claim bankruptcy protection in the US.  In a court filing on Tuesday, it said the Russian oil giant has few Texas ties beyond ...
Summary: Deutsche Bank has challenged Yukos' claim to US bankruptcy protection, alleging the Russian oil giant artificially manufactured a legal case to stop the sale of its main asset. The US bankruptcy court judge in Texas granted Yukos an injunction, but the deal ultimately went to Gazprom. Yukos intends to seek $20bn in damages from the buyer of Yuganskneftegas.

Title: GM in crunch talks on Fiat future
Article_Text: Fiat will meet car giant General Motors (GM) on Tuesday in an attempt to reach agreement over the future of the Italian firm's loss-making auto group.  Fiat claims that GM is legally obliged to buy th...
Summary: Fiat and General Motors are set to meet to discuss the future of Fiat's loss-making auto group, with Fiat claiming a legal obligation to sell the unit to GM. GM disputes this, citing a contract that has expired. The meeting comes as both companies seek to cut costs in the car industry.

Title: Record year for Chilean copper
Article_Text: Chile's copper industry has registered record earnings of $14.2bn in 2004, the governmental Chilean Copper Commission (Cochilco) has reported.  Strong demand from China's fast-growing economy and high...
Summary: Chile's copper industry has reported record earnings of $14.2bn in 2004, driven by strong demand from China's growing economy and high prices. The industry expects to see $10bn in investment over the next three years. Chile is now analyzing ways to maintain high copper prices without killing demand or leading customers to seek substitutes.

Title: US consumer confidence up
Article_Text: Consumers' confidence in the state of the US economy is at its highest for five months and they are optimistic about 2005, an influential survey says.  The feel-good factor among US consumers rose in ...
Summary: US consumers' confidence in the economy is at its highest in five months, with optimism about job creation and economic growth rising in December. Retailers have reported strong sales, and Wal-Mart expects its December sales to be better than forecast. Consumer confidence figures are seen as a key economic indicator.

Title: Cash gives way to flexible friend
Article_Text: Spending on credit and debit cards has overtaken cash spending in the UK for the first time.  The moment that plastic finally toppled cash happened at 10.38am on Wednesday, according to the Associatio...
Summary: Spending on credit and debit cards has overtaken cash spending in the UK for the first time, according to the Association for Payment Clearing Services (Apacs). The historic transaction took place at 10:38am on Wednesday, with school teacher Helen Carroll making the purchase at Tesco's Cromwell Road branch. This marks a significant shift in payment patterns, with £269bn expected to be spent on plastic cards in 2004.

Title: Go-ahead for Balkan oil pipeline
Article_Text: Albania, Bulgaria and Macedonia has given the go ahead for the construction of a $1.2bn oil pipeline that will pass through the Balkan peninsula.  The project aims to allow alternative ports for the s...
Summary: Albania, Bulgaria, and Macedonia have approved a $1.2bn oil pipeline project that will transport 750,000 daily barrels of oil, bypassing Turkish ports. The pipeline will be built by the US-registered Albanian Macedonian Bulgarian Oil Corporation and is expected to be completed in three or four years. The project has the support of the European Union and several major oil companies.

Title: Durex maker SSL awaits firm bid
Article_Text: UK condom maker SSL International has refused to comment on reports it may be subject to a takeover early in 2005.  A Financial Times report said business intelligence firm GPW was understood to be st...
Summary: UK condom maker SSL International has seen its shares rise after reports of a potential takeover, with GPW starting due diligence work on the company. SSL International has sold off several businesses in the past year, including its surgical gloves and antiseptics businesses. The company's shares rose over 6% after the news.

Title: Nasdaq planning $100m-share sale
Article_Text: The owner of the technology-dominated Nasdaq stock index plans to sell shares to the public and list itself on the market it operates.  According to a registration document filed with the Securities a...
Summary: Nasdaq plans to sell shares to the public and list itself on the market it operates, raising $100m, and will not make a profit from the sale.

Title: WMC says Xstrata bid is too low
Article_Text: Australian mining firm WMC Resources has said it is worth up to 30% more than a hostile 7.4bn Australian dollar ($5.8bn; £3bn) bid by rival Xstrata.  There is now pressure on Swiss-based Xstrata to in...
Summary: Australian mining firm WMC Resources has valued itself at up to 30% more than a hostile takeover bid by Xstrata, putting pressure on the rival company to increase its offer.

Title: Takeover offer for Sunderland FC
Article_Text: Bob Murray, chairman of Sunderland FC, has launched a £1.5m ($2.8m) bid for the club after buying broadcaster BSkyB's stake in the business.  Mr Murray is already Sunderland's leading shareholder, hol...
Summary: Bob Murray, chairman of Sunderland FC, has launched a £1.5m bid to take full control of the Championship side after buying BSkyB's stake in the business. He now holds a 42.3% stake and plans to make an offer for the remaining shares at the same price paid for the BSkyB holding. The move aims to simplify the club's financial affairs and reduce uncertainty.

Title: Warning over US pensions deficit
Article_Text: Taxpayers may have to bail out the US agency that protects workers' pension funds, leading economists have warned.  With the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (PBGC) some £23bn (£12m) in deficit, t...
Summary: The Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (PBGC) is facing a £23bn deficit, leading economists to warn that taxpayers may have to bail it out. The Financial Economists Roundtable (FER) is calling for Congress to change the PBGC's funding rules to prevent this. The FER blames a 2004 law for the current situation.

Title: Beer giant swallows Russian firm
Article_Text: Brewing giant Inbev has agreed to buy Alfa-Eco's stake in Sun Interbrew, Russia's second-largest brewer, for up to 259.7m euros ($353.3m; £183.75m).  Alfa-Eco, the venture capital arm of Russian congl...
Summary: Inbev has agreed to buy Alfa-Eco's stake in Sun Interbrew, Russia's second-largest brewer, for up to 259.7m euros. The deal gives Inbev near-total control over the Russian brewer. Inbev will own 97.3% of the voting shares and 98.8% of the non-voting shares.

Title: US manufacturing expands
Article_Text: US industrial production increased in December, according to the latest survey from the Institute for Supply Management (ISM).  Its index of national manufacturing activity rose to 58.6 last month fro...
Summary: US industrial production increased in December, with the Institute for Supply Management's manufacturing index rising to 58.6 from 57.8 in November. The result was better than expected and marked the 19th consecutive expansion. The growth was driven by a significant rise in new orders.

Title: Singapore growth at 8.1% in 2004
Article_Text: Singapore's economy grew by 8.1% in 2004, its best performance since 2000, figures from the trade ministry show.  The advance, the second-fastest in Asia after China, was led by growth of 13.1% in the...
Summary: Singapore's economy grew 8.1% in 2004, its best performance since 2000, driven by a 13.1% growth in the manufacturing sector. However, a slower-than-expected fourth quarter points to more modest growth in 2005 due to global technology demand and potential disruptions from the tsunami disaster. Economic growth is expected to halve to 3-5% this year.

Title: Madagascar completes currency switch
Article_Text: Madagascar has completed the replacement of its Malagasy franc with a new currency, the ariary.  From Monday, all prices and contracts will have to be quoted in the ariary, which was trading at 1,893 ...
Summary: Madagascar has replaced its Malagasy franc with the ariary, which began trading on Monday at 1,893 to the US dollar. The old currency is no longer legal tender but will remain exchangeable at banks until 2009. The move aims to distance the country from its colonial past and establish its own currency.

Title: Quiksilver moves for Rossignol
Article_Text: Shares of Skis Rossignol, the world's largest ski-maker, have jumped as much as 15% on speculation that it will be bought by US surfwear firm Quiksilver.  The owners of Rossignol, the Boix-Vives famil...
Summary: Shares of Rossignol have jumped 15% on speculation of a potential takeover by Quiksilver, with analysts expecting other sporting goods companies to take a closer look.

Title: Dollar hovers around record lows
Article_Text: The US dollar hovered close to record lows against the euro on Friday as concern grows about the size of the US budget deficit.  Analysts predict that the dollar will remain weak in 2005 as investors ...
Summary: The US dollar hovered near record lows against the euro due to concerns about the US budget deficit and the state of the US economy. Analysts predict the dollar will remain weak in 2005. The dollar's weakness was triggered by disappointing business figures from Chicago.

Title: S Korean credit card firm rescued
Article_Text: South Korea's largest credit card firm has averted liquidation following a one trillion won ($960m; £499m) bail-out.  LG Card had been threatened with collapse because of its huge debts but the firm's...
Summary: South Korea's largest credit card firm, LG Card, has received a $960m bail-out to avoid liquidation, following a consortium of creditors and LG Group stepping in to rescue it. The firm's creditors had threatened to delist the company unless a deal was reached on its future funding. The agreement will see 12 trillion won of debt converted into equity.

Title: Dollar slides ahead of New Year
Article_Text: The US dollar has hit a new record low against the euro and analysts predict that more declines are likely in 2005.  Disappointing economic reports dented the currency, which had been rallying after E...
Summary: The US dollar has hit a new record low against the euro, and analysts predict further declines in 2005 due to disappointing economic reports and concerns about US trade and budget deficits. The dollar slid to a record $1.3666 versus the euro on Thursday, before bouncing back to $1.3636. Investors are concerned about the state of the US economy and the strength of the euro.

Title: VW considers opening Indian plant
Article_Text: Volkswagen is considering building a car factory in India, but said it had yet to make a final decision.  The German giant said it was studying the possibility of opening an assembly plant in the coun...
Summary: Volkswagen is considering building a car factory in India, but has not made a final decision. The company is studying the possibility of opening an assembly plant in the country, with plans to set up a facility in Visakhapatnam. Several foreign carmakers already have production facilities in India.

Title: Ukraine strikes Turkmen gas deal
Article_Text: Ukraine has agreed to pay 30% more for natural gas supplied by Turkmenistan.  The deal was sealed three days after Turkmenistan cut off gas supplies in a price dispute that threatened the Ukrainian ec...
Summary: Ukraine has agreed to pay 30% more for natural gas supplied by Turkmenistan, following a price dispute that threatened the Ukrainian economy. The deal was sealed after Turkmenistan cut off gas supplies. The new price is $58 per 1,000 cubic metres, $14 higher than the 2004 contract.

Title: Reliance unit loses Anil Ambani
Article_Text: Anil Ambani, the younger of the two brothers in charge of India's largest private company, has resigned from running its petrochemicals subsidiary.  The move is likely to be seen as the latest twist i...
Summary: Anil Ambani has resigned as director and vice-chairman of Indian Petrochemicals Corporation (IPC), a subsidiary of Reliance Industries, amid a feud with his brother Mukesh. The move comes after a series of ownership issues and speculation about the brothers' political ambitions and business investments. The shares of IPC and Reliance Energy, headed by Anil, have reacted to the news.

Title: India opens skies to competition
Article_Text: India will allow domestic commercial airlines to fly long haul international routes, a move it hopes will stoke competition and drive down prices.  However, only state controlled carriers will be able...
Summary: India will allow domestic airlines to fly long-haul international routes, with state-controlled carriers initially restricted to Gulf routes. The move aims to boost competition and reduce prices. Air travel in India has seen significant growth, but infrastructure development lags behind.

Title: Oil rebounds from weather effect
Article_Text: Oil prices recovered in Asian trade on Tuesday, after falling in New York on milder winter weather across the US.  With winter temperatures staying relatively high in the northern US, a barrel of ligh...
Summary: Oil prices recovered in Asian trade after falling in New York due to milder winter weather, with prices expected to fall further if temperatures continue to rise. Crude prices have rebounded in Asia, rising to $42.30 a barrel for February delivery. The price of crude oil remains almost 30% higher than year-ago levels despite a decline of over $12 a barrel from record highs.

Title: Ban on forced retirement under 65
Article_Text: Employers will no longer be able to force workers to retire before 65, unless they can justify it.  The government has announced that firms will be barred from 2006 from imposing arbitrary retirement ...
Summary: The UK government has announced that firms will no longer be able to force workers to retire before 65, unless they can justify it, under new European age discrimination rules.

Title: Fed warns of more US rate rises
Article_Text: The US looks set for a continued boost to interest rates in 2005, according to the Federal Reserve.  Minutes of the December meeting which pushed rates up to 2.25% showed that policy-makers at the Fed...
Summary: The US Federal Reserve is expected to continue raising interest rates in 2005, with the key rate having risen 1.25 percentage points since 2001. The release of the December meeting minutes showed policymakers are worried about accelerating inflation. The dollar has gained ground against the euro and sterling, but the respite may be short-lived.

Title: Weak end-of-year sales hit Next
Article_Text: Next has said its annual profit will be £5m lower than previously expected because its end-of-year clearance sale has proved disappointing.  "Clearance rates in our end-of-season sale have been below ...
Summary: Next's annual profit will be £5m lower than expected due to a disappointing end-of-year clearance sale, but overall sales across its retail and mail order divisions were up 12.4%.

Title: Tate & Lyle boss bags top award
Article_Text: Tate & Lyle's chief executive has been named European Businessman of the Year by a leading business magazine.  Iain Ferguson was awarded the title by US publication Forbes for returning one of the UK'...
Summary: Iain Ferguson, Tate & Lyle's chief executive, has been named European Businessman of the Year by Forbes for returning the company to the UK's top 100 companies. Tate's shares have increased 55% this year, driven by firming sugar prices and sales of artificial sweeteners. The company had been absent from the FTSE 100 for seven years.

Title: Krispy Kreme shares hit
Article_Text: Shares in Krispy Kreme Doughnuts have taken a dunking on Wall Street after the firm revealed it would have to restate its 2004 financial reports.  The company warned the move would cut its profits by ...
Summary: Krispy Kreme Doughnuts has announced it will restate its 2004 financial reports due to accounting errors, which will cut its profits by $3.8m to $4.9m. The company warned it might need to further restate results for 2004 and 2005. Shares in Krispy Kreme sank 14.87% after the announcement.

Title: Germany nears 1990 jobless level
Article_Text: German unemployment rose for the 11th consecutive month in December - making the year's average jobless total the highest since reunification.  The seasonally adjusted jobless total rose a higher than...
Summary: German unemployment rose for the 11th consecutive month in December, reaching a 10.8% average jobless rate, the highest since reunification. The increase was attributed to bad weather and a sluggish economy. The Hartz IV reforms are expected to further increase unemployment in the coming months.

Title: Venezuela identifies 'idle' farms
Article_Text: Venezuelan authorities have identified more than 500 farms, including 56 large estates, as idle as it continues with its controversial land reform policy.  Under a 2001 land law, the government can ta...
Summary: Venezuelan authorities have identified over 500 idle farms, including 56 large estates, under the country's land reform policy, which critics claim ignores property rights. The government says the policy aims to address inequality, while land owners claim mistakes have been made in classifying lands. A conflict has arisen with the El Charcote cattle ranch, where pro-Chavez squatters have taken over 80% of the property.

Title: Egypt to sell off state-owned bank
Article_Text: The Egyptian government is reportedly planning to privatise one of the country's big public banks.  An Investment Ministry official has told the Reuters news agency that the Bank of Alexandria will be...
Summary: The Egyptian government plans to privatise the Bank of Alexandria, one of the country's big public banks, with the sale expected to take place in 2005. The move is part of the government's efforts to reduce the size of the public sector. Analysts say the public-sector banks have suited the government's monetary, credit and exchange policies.

Title: Wal-Mart to pay $14m in gun suit
Article_Text: The world's largest retailer, Wal-Mart, has agreed to pay a total of $14.5m (£7.74m) to settle a lawsuit over gun sales violations in California.  The lawsuit alleged Wal-Mart committed thousands of g...
Summary: Wal-Mart has agreed to pay $14.5m to settle a lawsuit over gun sales violations in California, including $5m in fines and $4m for state compliance checks. The company suspended firearms sales in 2003, but the settlement aims to ensure compliance with state laws in the future. Wal-Mart has not decided whether to resume sales.

Title: Yukos heading back to US courts
Article_Text: Russian oil and gas company Yukos is due in a US court on Thursday as it continues to fight for its survival.  The firm is in the process of being broken up by Russian authorities in order to pay a $2...
Summary: Russian oil and gas company Yukos is fighting for its survival in a US court, claiming its assets were sold at less than market value. The company has filed for bankruptcy and is seeking $20bn in damages. The US court will hear motions from various parties, including Deutsche Bank and Gazprom.

Title: Deutsche Boerse set to 'woo' LSE
Article_Text: Bosses of Deutsche Boerse and the London Stock Exchange are to meet amid talk that a takeover bid for the LSE will be raised to £1.5bn ($2.9bn).  Last month, the German exchange tabled a 530 pence-per...
Summary: Deutsche Boerse and the London Stock Exchange are set to meet amid a potential £1.5bn takeover bid for the LSE. Euronext has also expressed interest in bidding for the LSE, with a reported £1.4bn offer. The LSE rejected Deutsche Boerse's initial £1.3bn offer, but left the door open for talks. A deal would create the biggest stock market operator in Europe and the second biggest in the world.

Title: Laura Ashley chief stepping down
Article_Text: Laura Ashley is parting company with its chief executive Ainum Mohd-Saaid.  The clothing and home furnishing retailer said Ms Mohd-Saaid had resigned for personal reasons. Her departure will come into...
Summary: Laura Ashley is parting ways with its chief executive Ainum Mohd-Saaid, who is leaving for personal reasons. She will be replaced by Lillian Tan, who has experience managing a large retail group in Malaysia. The company has been struggling with poor sales and has reported losses in recent months.

Title: US Airways staff agree to pay cut
Article_Text: A union representing 5,200 flight attendants at bankrupt US Airways have agreed to a new contract that cuts pay by nearly 10%.  The deal will help the carrier, trying to survive by cutting costs by ne...
Summary: A US Airways flight attendant union has agreed to a new contract that cuts pay by nearly 10% to help the carrier cut costs by nearly $1bn a year. More than two thirds of its staff have accepted wage cuts. The airline is trying to survive after filing for bankruptcy for the second time in two years.

Title: Delta cuts fares in survival plan
Article_Text: Delta Air Lines is cutting domestic fares by as much as 50% as part of a plan to ensure its financial survival.  Other US carriers, including United, have sought bankruptcy protection, amid high fuel ...
Summary: Delta Air Lines is cutting domestic fares by up to 50% as part of its restructuring plan to ensure financial survival. The airline has also eliminated a Saturday-night stay requirement on discount fares and will offer further reductions to customers booking in advance and online. Delta's move has prompted speculation that other firms will be forced to match their fares.

Title: Profits jump at China's top bank
Article_Text: Industrial and Commercial Bank (ICBC), China's biggest lender, has seen an 18% jump in profits during 2004.  The increase in earnings has allowed the firm to write off bad loans and pave the way for a...
Summary: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) has seen an 18% jump in profits in 2004, allowing it to write off bad loans and potentially receive a state bailout and stock-market listing. China is cleaning up its banking system, which is weighed down by unpaid loans. The bank's profits were 74.7 billion yuan in 2004.
Key_Entities: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China

Title: Green reports shun supply chain
Article_Text: Nearly 20% more UK top 250 firms produced non-financial reports on social and environment issues than last year.  But of the 145 companies reporting, 76% didn't examine their supply chains, says the a...
Summary: Nearly 20% more UK top 250 firms produced non-financial reports on social and environment issues than last year, but 76% didn't examine their supply chains, according to the annual Directions survey. The UK government will soon require all quoted companies to report their social and environmental risks. The quality of reports has improved, but most reports are not independently verified.

Title: Tsunami to cost Sri Lanka $1.3bn
Article_Text: Sri Lanka faces a $1.3bn (£691m) bill in 2005 for reconstruction after the tsunami which killed more than 30,000 of its people, its central bank says.  This estimate is preliminary, bank governor Suni...
Summary: Sri Lanka is facing a $1.3 billion bill for reconstruction after the 2004 tsunami, with the central bank estimating the cost could rise in 2006. The country is seeking $320 million from the International Monetary Fund to help pay for relief. The bank has set aside $50 million to lend to those who lost property.

Title: Indian oil firm eyes Yukos assets
Article_Text: India's biggest oil exploration firm, Oil & Natural Gas Corp (ONGC), says it is in talks to buy the former assets of troubled Russian crude producer Yukos.  "We are in touch with the concerned Russian...
Summary: India's Oil & Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) is in talks to buy the former assets of Russian crude producer Yukos, which is being broken up by Russian authorities to pay a massive tax bill. ONGC chairman Subir Raha discussed the plans with Indian oil minister Mani Shankar Aiyar during a trip to Moscow. The move aims to reduce India's dependence on Gulf states for oil imports and secure future supplies.

Title: Monsanto fined $1.5m for bribery
Article_Text: The US agrochemical giant Monsanto has agreed to pay a $1.5m (£799,000) fine for bribing an Indonesian official.  Monsanto admitted one of its employees paid the senior official two years ago in a bid...
Summary: Monsanto has agreed to pay a $1.5m fine for bribing an Indonesian official to avoid environmental impact studies on its cotton. The company accepted full responsibility for the improper activities and has agreed to close monitoring of its business practices. Monsanto also paid bribes to other high-ranking officials between 1997 and 2002.

Title: Marsh executive in guilty plea
Article_Text: An executive at US insurance firm Marsh & McLennan has pleaded guilty to criminal charges in connection with an ongoing fraud and bid-rigging probe.  New York Attorney General Elliot Spitzer said seni...
Summary: An executive at US insurance firm Marsh & McLennan has pleaded guilty to criminal charges in connection with a fraud and bid-rigging probe. The offence carries a sentence of 16 months to four years in state prison. The company has agreed to cooperate in the case.

Title: US interest rate rise expected
Article_Text: US interest rates are expected to rise for the fifth time since June following the US Federal Reserve's latest rate-setting meeting later on Tuesday.  Borrowing costs are tipped to rise by a quarter o...
Summary: US interest rates are expected to rise for the fifth time since June, with borrowing costs tipped to rise by a quarter of a percentage point to 2.25%. The move comes as the US economy shows signs of robustness and sustainability, but also raises concerns about inflation. The Federal Reserve will implement the rate hike in a measured way to combat price growth.

Title: WorldCom bosses' $54m payout
Article_Text: Ten former directors at WorldCom have agreed to pay $54m (£28.85m), including $18m from their own pockets, to settle a class action lawsuit, reports say.  James Wareham, a lawyer representing one of t...
Summary: Ten former WorldCom directors have agreed to pay $54m to settle a class action lawsuit, with $18m coming from their own pockets. The remaining $36m will be paid by their insurers. A formal agreement is expected to be signed on Thursday. The settlement is seen as a significant development in corporate governance, with experts praising the directors' willingness to take responsibility for their actions.

Title: Continental 'may run out of cash'
Article_Text: Shares in Continental Airlines have tumbled after the firm warned it could run out of cash.  In a filing to US regulators the airline warned of "inadequate liquidity" if it fails to reduce wage costs ...
Summary: Continental Airlines has warned of potential cash shortages and significant losses if it fails to reduce wage costs by $500m by the end of February. The airline expects to lose hundreds of millions of dollars in 2005 if it does not make cuts. Continental has nearly $984m in debt and pension payments to pay off this year.

Title: House prices rebound says Halifax
Article_Text: UK house prices increased by 1.1% in December, the first monthly rise since September, the Halifax has said.  The UK's biggest mortgage lender said prices rose 15.1% over the whole of 2004, but by onl...
Summary: UK house prices increased by 1.1% in December, marking the first monthly rise since September, according to the Halifax. The average house price in the UK is now £162,086. Despite this, the housing market is still experiencing a slowdown due to interest rate rises.

Title: Mixed Christmas for US retailers
Article_Text: US retailers posted mixed results for December - with luxury retailers faring well while many others were forced to slash prices to lift sales.  Upscale department store Nordstrom said same store sale...
Summary: US retailers posted mixed results for December, with luxury retailers performing well and others cutting prices to boost sales. Some retailers, like Wal-Mart, saw sales rise after cutting prices, while others, like Pier 1 Imports and Best Buy, missed sales targets. Online stores, however, saw a surge in sales during the holiday season.

Title: India's Deccan gets more planes
Article_Text: Air Deccan has signed a deal to acquire 36 planes from Avions de Transport Regional (ATR).  The value of the deal has not been revealed, because of a confidentiality clause in the agreement. But Air D...
Summary: Air Deccan has signed a deal to acquire 36 planes from Avions de Transport Regional (ATR) for an undisclosed price. The deal includes 15 new ATR 72-500 planes and 15 leased planes, with deliveries starting in 2005 and continuing over a five-year period. The acquisition is part of Air Deccan's efforts to connect regional Indian cities.

Title: South African car demand surges
Article_Text: Car manufacturers with plants in South Africa, including BMW, General Motors, Toyota and Volkswagen, have seen a surge in demand during 2004.  New vehicle sales jumped 22% to 449,603 from a year earli...
Summary: Car manufacturers in South Africa saw a surge in demand in 2004, with new vehicle sales jumping 22% to 449,603, according to the National Association of Automobile Manufacturers of South Africa. Strong economic growth and low interest rates are expected to drive demand. Analysts predict sales will top 500,000 in 2005.
Key_Entities: National Association of Automobile Manufacturers of South Africa

Title: UK bank seals South Korean deal
Article_Text: UK-based bank Standard Chartered said it would spend $3.3bn (£1.8bn) to buy one of South Korea's main retail banks.  Standard Chartered said acquiring Korea First Bank (KFB) fulfilled a strategic obje...
Summary: UK-based bank Standard Chartered plans to spend $3.3bn to acquire Korea First Bank, a South Korean retail bank, to expand its presence in Asia's third-largest economy. The deal is expected to be completed by April 2005 and will contribute to the bank's earnings in 2006. Standard Chartered's shares fell 3% after the announcement.

Title: DaimlerChrysler's 2004 sales rise
Article_Text: US-German carmaker DaimlerChrysler has sold 2.1% more cars in 2004 than in the previous year, as solid Chrysler sales offset a weak showing for Mercedes.  Sales totalled 3.9 million units worldwide du...
Summary: DaimlerChrysler sold 2.1% more cars in 2004 than in the previous year, with Chrysler sales offsetting a weak Mercedes showing. The company sold 3.9 million units worldwide, with Smart brand sales jumping 21.1% to 136,000. Mercedes-Benz sales fell 3.1% to 1.06 million.

Title: Tsunami cost hits Jakarta shares
Article_Text: The stock market in Jakarta has seen its biggest slide in a month, after the country doubled the likely cost of rebuilding from the Asian tsunami.  The fall came as Indonesia said it expected debt rep...
Summary: The Jakarta Stock Exchange fell 2.1% after Indonesia doubled the likely cost of rebuilding from the Asian tsunami, with debt repayments expected to be frozen to help pay for the recovery. The country's economy minister, Aburizal Bakrie, announced the move, which could be defrayed by temporary debt relief. The Paris Club group of creditor countries has agreed to a moratorium on repayments for tsunami-hit countries.

Title: Iran budget seeks state sell-offs
Article_Text: Iran's president, Mohammad Khatami, has unveiled a budget designed to expand public spending by 30% but loosen the Islamic republic's dependence on oil.  The budget for the fiscal year starting on 21 ...
Summary: Iran's president, Mohammad Khatami, has unveiled a budget that aims to expand public spending by 30% and reduce the country's dependence on oil. The budget includes plans to sell off 20% of the state's corporate holdings, but faces opposition from parliament. Khatami's second term is ending, and his plans may be blocked by hard-line religious conservatives.

Title: EC calls truce in deficit battle
Article_Text: The European Commission (EC) has called a truce in its battle with France and Germany over breaching deficit limits.  The move came after France and Germany vowed to run their budget deficits below th...
Summary: The European Commission has called a truce in its battle with France and Germany over breaching deficit limits, with the two countries vowing to run their budget deficits below the EU cap in 2005. The commission warned that it would act if their fiscal situations deteriorated, but announced that it would erase France and Germany from its list of deficit rule breakers. The EU expects the two countries to correct their excessive deficits by 2005.

Title: Enron bosses in $168m payout
Article_Text: Eighteen former Enron directors have agreed a $168m (£89m) settlement deal in a shareholder lawsuit over the collapse of the energy firm.  Leading plaintiff, the University of California, announced th...
Summary: Eighteen former Enron directors have agreed a $168m settlement deal in a shareholder lawsuit over the collapse of the energy firm. The settlement will be put to the courts for approval next week. The deal does not include former Enron chief executives Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling, or Andrew Fastow, who has pleaded guilty to taking part in an illegal conspiracy.

Title: UK house prices dip in November
Article_Text: UK house prices dipped slightly in November, the Office of the Deputy Prime Minister (ODPM) has said.  The average house price fell marginally to £180,226, from £180,444 in October. Recent evidence ha...
Summary: UK house prices dipped slightly in November, with the average house price falling to £180,226, according to the Office of the Deputy Prime Minister. Annual house price inflation remains strong at 13.8%, but economists forecast a drop in prices in 2005. The housing market is slowing down, with mortgage lending and approvals data showing a decline.

Title: Steady job growth continues in US
Article_Text: The US created fewer jobs than expected in December, but analysts said that the dip in hiring was not enough to derail the world's biggest economy.  According to Labor Department figures, 157,000 new ...
Summary: The US economy added 157,000 new jobs in December, bringing the total to 2.2 million, the best showing in five years. The unemployment rate remained at 5.4%. Analysts say the conditions are set for steady growth in 2005, despite some concerns about job creation.

Title: Barclays shares up on merger talk
Article_Text: Shares in UK banking group Barclays have risen on Monday following a weekend press report that it had held merger talks with US bank Wells Fargo.  A tie-up between Barclays and California-based Wells ...
Summary: Shares in Barclays rose on Monday following a weekend report of merger talks with Wells Fargo, creating the world's fourth biggest bank valued at $180bn. Barclays declined to comment on the report. The two banks reportedly held talks in 2004. Barclays shares were up 1.3% at 605 pence by late morning.

Title: US firm 'bids for Lacroix label'
Article_Text: A US firm has said it is in final negotiations with luxury goods group LVMH to buy the loss-making Christian Lacroix haute-couture house.  Paris-based LVMH has been selling non-core businesses and foc...
Summary: A US firm, Falic Group, is in final negotiations to buy Christian Lacroix haute-couture house from LVMH. LVMH is selling non-core businesses to focus on profitable labels. Falic Group aims to increase brand exposure and business volume.

Title: $1m payoff for former Shell boss
Article_Text: Shell is to pay $1m (£522,000) to the ex-finance chief who stepped down from her post in April 2004 after the firm over-stated its reserves.  Judy Boynton finally left the firm on 31 December, having ...
Summary: Shell is paying $1m to its ex-finance chief Judy Boynton, who left the firm in December after it was revealed that the company had over-stated its reserves. The payment is in line with her contract and includes long-term share options. The scandal led to the resignation of several top executives.

Title: India and Iran in gas export deal
Article_Text: India has signed a $40bn (£21bn) deal to import millions of tonnes of liquefied natural gas from Iran.  Firms led by the Oil & Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) will also assist in the development of Ira...
Summary: India has signed a $40bn deal to import liquefied natural gas from Iran, with the Oil & Natural Gas Corporation to assist in the development of Iranian oil fields. The deal is part of a series of agreements between Middle East producers and Asia's biggest energy consumers. India's oil production has stagnated, prompting the country to look abroad for future supplies.

Title: LSE 'sets date for takeover deal'
Article_Text: The London Stock Exchange (LSE) is planning to announce a preferred takeover by the end of the month, newspaper reports claim.  The Sunday Telegraph said the LSE's plan was further evidence it wants t...
Summary: The London Stock Exchange is planning to announce a preferred takeover by the end of the month, with Paris-based Euronext and Deutsche Boerse holding talks over a possible offer. Euronext has made an all-cash bid of £1.4bn, while Deutsche Boerse has offered £1.3bn, which was rejected. The LSE is expected to hold further talks with the two parties later this week.

Title: News Corp makes $5.4bn Fox offer
Article_Text: News Corporation is seeking to buy out minority investors in Fox Entertainment Group, its broadcasting subsidiary, for about $5.4bn (£3.7bn).  The media giant, run by Rupert Murdoch, owns 82% of the s...
Summary: News Corporation is seeking to buy out minority investors in Fox Entertainment Group for $5.4bn, following its decision to register its business in the US. The move will simplify the company's stock market listing and attract more investment. Fox Entertainment Group generated $12bn in revenues last year.

Title: Israel looks to US for bank chief
Article_Text: Israel has asked a US banker and former International Monetary Fund director to run its central bank.  Stanley Fischer, vice chairman of banking giant Citigroup, has agreed to take the Bank of Israel ...
Summary: Israel has asked Stanley Fischer, a US banker and former International Monetary Fund director, to run its central bank. Fischer has agreed to take the job subject to approval from parliament and cabinet. He will have to become an Israeli citizen to take the job.

Title: EU-US seeking deal on air dispute
Article_Text: The EU and US have agreed to begin talks on ending subsidies given to aircraft makers, EU Trade Commissioner Peter Mandelson has announced.  Both sides hope to reach a negotiated deal over state aid r...
Summary: The EU and US have agreed to begin talks on ending subsidies given to aircraft makers, with the goal of avoiding a dispute at the World Trade Organisation (WTO). The US and EU had previously filed complaints against each other over state aid to Airbus and Boeing. The talks aim to resolve the dispute and limit subsidies to development and production of large civil aircraft.

Title: Nortel in $300m profit revision
Article_Text: Telecoms equipment maker Nortel Networks has sharply revised downwards its profits for the 2003 fiscal year.  In a long-awaited filing, Nortel said it had made $434m (£231m), compared to the previousl...
Summary: Nortel Networks has revised downwards its profits for the 2003 fiscal year to $434m, compared to the previously reported $732m, with revenue being about 4% higher than first thought. The company's shares have lost nearly 50% of their value since last year. Nortel has also issued new figures for the 2001-2002 period, which had previously understated losses.

Title: Minister hits out at Yukos sale
Article_Text: Russia's renationalisation of its energy industry needs to be reversed, a senior government figure has warned.  Economy minister German Gref told the Kommersant newspaper that direct state involvement...
Summary: Russia's economy minister, German Gref, has warned that the country's renationalisation of its energy industry needs to be reversed, citing the unjustified direct state involvement in oil. The sale of Yukos to cover back taxes has been widely criticized.

Title: Chinese exports rise 25% in 2004
Article_Text: Exports from China leapt during 2004 over the previous year as the country continued to show breakneck growth.  The spurt put China's trade surplus - a sore point with some of its trading partners - a...
Summary: China's exports surged in 2004, driven by rapid growth, and put the country's trade surplus at a six-year high. The growth was attributed to a tightening of controls on tax evasion and a rapid expansion. China's tax revenues rose 25.7% to 2.572 trillion yuan.
Key_Entities: US-China Economic and Security Review Commission

Title: Karachi stocks hit historic high
Article_Text: The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) has recorded its largest single day gain, surging 3.5% to a new high.  The index rose 225.79 points in four hours of furious trading, with many investors optimistic th...
Summary: The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) recorded its largest single day gain, surging 3.5% to a new high, with energy and telecommunication stocks performing well. The KSE index closed at 6709.93, an overall gain of nearly 400 points in the first two trading days of the week. Analysts attribute the market's performance to solid economic growth, improved credit ratings, and reduced political tensions.

Title: US trade gap ballooned in October
Article_Text: The US trade deficit widened by more than expected in October, hitting record levels after higher oil prices raised import costs, figures have shown  The trade shortfall was $55.5bn (£29bn), up 9% fro...
Summary: The US trade deficit widened by $55.5bn in October, reaching record levels due to higher oil prices and a weaker dollar. Imports rose 3.4% while exports increased only 0.6%. The 10-month deficit is now $500.5bn. Analysts express concerns about funding trade and budget deficits.

Title: US prepares for hybrid onslaught
Article_Text: Sales of hybrid cars in the US are set to double in 2005, research suggests.  Research group JD Power estimates sales will hit 200,000 in 2005, despite higher prices and customer scepticism. Carmakers...
Summary: Sales of hybrid cars in the US are expected to double in 2005, driven by increasing demand and government regulations, despite higher prices and customer skepticism. Carmakers are expanding their hybrid offerings, with several launching new models in the coming year. The price premium for hybrids remains a concern.

Title: Mitsubishi in Peugeot link talks
Article_Text: Trouble-hit Mitsubishi Motors is in talks with French carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen about a possible alliance.  On Tuesday Mitsubishi, the only major Japanese car firm in the red, confirmed earlier rep...
Summary: Mitsubishi Motors is in talks with PSA Peugeot Citroen about a possible alliance, amid a recall scandal and declining sales. The company has been hit by a 41% sales drop in the past year. Mitsubishi is due to unveil a recovery plan later in January.

Title: BA to suspend two Saudi services
Article_Text: British Airways is to halt its flights from London Heathrow to Jeddah and Riyadh in Saudi Arabia from 27 March.  The airline said the decision was a commercial one due to reduced passenger demand for ...
Summary: British Airways will suspend flights from London Heathrow to Jeddah and Riyadh in Saudi Arabia from 27 March due to reduced passenger demand, citing unprofitable routes.

Title: Cairn Energy in Indian gas find
Article_Text: Shares in Cairn Energy rose 3.8% to 1,088 pence on Tuesday after the UK firm announced a fresh gas discovery in northern India.  The firm, which last year made a number of other new finds in the Rajas...
Summary: Shares in Cairn Energy rose 3.8% after the firm announced a fresh gas discovery in northern India, with the potential for large gas volumes. The discovery is part of a string of finds in the Rajasthan area, which has elevated the company to the FTSE 100 index. Additional evaluation is needed before the extent of the discovery can be determined.

Title: Asia quake increases poverty risk
Article_Text: Nearly two million people across Asia could be thrown into poverty because of the Indian Ocean tsunami, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) has said.  In its first overview of the disaster, the ADB said ...
Summary: The Asian Development Bank warns that nearly two million people in Asia could be thrown into poverty due to the Indian Ocean tsunami, despite major cities and factories escaping damage. The Paris Club has offered to freeze debts owed by tsunami-hit countries, but only Sri Lanka, Indonesia, and the Seychelles have indicated they will take it up. Donor nations have promised $717m in disaster relief over six months.

Title: Fosters buys stake in winemaker
Article_Text: Australian brewer Fosters has bought a large stake in Australian winemaker Southcorp, sparking rumours of a possible takeover.  Fosters bought 18.8% of Southcorp, the global winemaker behind the Penfo...
Summary: Australian brewer Fosters has acquired a 18.8% stake in winemaker Southcorp for 4.17 Australian dollars per share, sparking rumors of a possible takeover. The deal values Southcorp at A$3.1bn. Fosters is currently in discussions with Southcorp, and the companies have asked for trading to be suspended.

Title: ECB holds rates amid growth fears
Article_Text: The European Central Bank has left its key interest rate unchanged at 2% for the 19th month in succession.  Borrowing costs have remained on hold amid concerns about the strength of economic growth in...
Summary: The European Central Bank has left its key interest rate unchanged at 2% for the 19th month in succession, amid concerns about the strength of economic growth in the eurozone. Labour markets and consumer demand remain sluggish, while firms are eyeing cost cutting measures. High oil prices have put upward pressure on the inflation rate.

Title: China bans new tobacco factories
Article_Text: The world's biggest tobacco consumer, China, has said it will not allow any new tobacco factories to be built.  China already has more than enough cigarette-making capacity, according to a spokesman f...
Summary: China has banned the construction of new tobacco factories, citing an excess of existing capacity, and will retain its monopoly on cigarette distribution. The move affects a planned joint venture factory by British American Tobacco. China's tobacco market is experiencing steady growth, with pre-tax profits reaching $25.4bn last year.

Title: UK interest rates held at 4.75%
Article_Text: The Bank of England has left interest rates on hold again at 4.75%, in a widely-predicted move.  Rates went up five times from November 2003 - as the bank sought to cool the housing market and consume...
Summary: The Bank of England has left interest rates on hold at 4.75%, despite a slowdown in manufacturing and consumer spending, as well as disappointing retail sales over Christmas. Analysts predict a further slowdown in the housing market, which could worsen economic conditions. The Bank is concerned about rising personal debt.

Title: German economy rebounds
Article_Text: Germany's economy, the biggest among the 12 countries sharing the euro, grew at its fastest rate in four years during 2004, driven by strong exports.  Gross domestic product (GDP) rose by 1.7% last ye...
Summary: Germany's economy grew at its fastest rate in four years in 2004, driven by strong exports, with GDP rising by 1.7% last year. However, concerns remain over the strength of the euro, weak domestic demand, and a sluggish labour market. The European Central Bank left its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 2%.

Title: US trade deficit widens sharply
Article_Text: The gap between US exports and imports has widened to more than $60bn (£31.7bn), an all-time record.  Figures from the Commerce Department for November showed exports down 2.3% to $95.6bn, while impor...
Summary: The US trade deficit has widened to an all-time record $60bn, with exports down 2.3% and imports up 1.3% in November. The dollar has fallen against the euro and pound, with economists attributing the decline to the large budget deficit and current account deficit. The White House has tacitly indicated it would be happy to see the dollar continue to fall.

Title: Trade gap narrows as exports rise
Article_Text: The UK's trade gap narrowed in November, helped by a 7.5% rise in exports outside the European Union.  According to the Office for National Statistics, the difference between what the UK exported and ...
Summary: The UK's trade gap narrowed in November due to a 7.5% rise in exports outside the European Union, with exports rising 3.2% to a new record of £24.8bn. Total imports rose to a new record of £27.9bn, but the deficit for goods alone was £4.6bn, down from October's £5bn. The UK's surplus on trade-in-services remained steady at £1.5bn.

Title: Lesotho textile workers lose jobs
Article_Text: Six foreign-owned textile factories have closed in Lesotho, leaving 6,650 garment workers jobless, union officers told the AP news agency.  Factory Workers Union secretary general Billy Macaefa blamed...
Summary: Six foreign-owned textile factories in Lesotho have closed, leaving 6,650 garment workers jobless, due to the end of worldwide textile quotas. The closures were likely due to the strong South African rand against the US dollar, making exports to the US and EU unprofitable. The factories' owners, from Taiwan, China, Mauritius, and Malaysia, left without informing or paying their employees.

Title: Kraft cuts snack ads for children
Article_Text: Kraft plans to cut back on advertising of products like Oreo cookies and sugary Kool-Aid drinks as part of an effort to promote healthy eating.  The largest US food maker will also add a label to its ...
Summary: Kraft plans to reduce advertising of unhealthy products and add labels to its healthier brands to promote healthy eating, following a similar initiative by PepsiCo. The move aims to address rising obesity levels in US children. Kraft will continue to advertise its products in media seen by parents and family audiences.

Title: Khodorkovsky quits Yukos shares
Article_Text: Jailed tycoon Mikhail Khodorkovsky has transferred his controlling stake in oil giant Yukos to a business partner.  Mr Khodorkovsky handed over his entire 59.5% stake in holding company Group Menatep ...
Summary: Mikhail Khodorkovsky has transferred his controlling stake in oil giant Yukos to business partner Leonid Nevzlin, following the forced sale of Yukos' core oil production unit to pay a giant tax bill. The sale was made to recover government tax claims against Yukos totalling over $27bn. Khodorkovsky is currently on trial for fraud and tax evasion.

Title: Executive trio leave Aer Lingus
Article_Text: Three senior executives of Ireland's state-owned airline, Aer Lingus, are set to leave early on 28 January after accusations of a conflict of interest.  The trio are chief executive Willie Walsh, chie...
Summary: Three senior executives of Aer Lingus are leaving early, amid accusations of a conflict of interest, and have denied plans to launch a private airline in competition with Aer Lingus.

Title: US in EU tariff chaos trade row
Article_Text: The US has asked the World Trade Organisation to investigate European Union customs tariffs, which it says are inconsistent and hamper trade.  The EU's own institutions have noted the uneven way EU cu...
Summary: The US has asked the World Trade Organisation to investigate European Union customs tariffs, which it claims are inconsistent and hinder trade. The EU's customs rules are unevenly applied, with small and mid-sized US firms being the worst-hit. The US filed the complaint after talks failed to find a solution.

Title: News Corp eyes video games market
Article_Text: News Corp, the media company controlled by Australian billionaire Rupert Murdoch, is eyeing a move into the video games market.  According to the Financial Times, chief operating officer Peter Chernin...
Summary: News Corp is considering a move into the video games market, with chief operating officer Peter Chernin stating that the company is 'kicking the tires' of several video games companies, including Activision.

Title: US Ahold suppliers face charges
Article_Text: US prosecutors have charged nine food suppliers with helping Dutch retailer Ahold inflate earnings by more than $800m (£428m).  The charges have been brought against individuals as well as companies, ...
Summary: US prosecutors have charged nine food suppliers with helping Dutch retailer Ahold inflate earnings by more than $800m. Ahold has admitted to accounting irregularities and the suppliers are accused of signing false documents. The charges are part of a larger scandal that damaged investor confidence in Europe.

Title: Wal-Mart fights back at accusers
Article_Text: Two big US names have launched advertising campaigns to "set the record straight" about their products and corporate behaviour.  The world's biggest retailer Wal-Mart took out more than 100 full page ...
Summary: Wal-Mart and Eli Lilly are launching advertising campaigns to address criticism about their corporate behavior and products. Wal-Mart is trying to counter criticism over its pay deals, benefits package, and promotion strategy, while Eli Lilly is responding to a British Medical Journal article that claimed its anti-depressant drug Prozac was linked to suicide and violent behavior.

Title: US retail sales surge in December
Article_Text: US retail sales ended the year on a high note with solid gains in December, boosted by strong car sales.  Seasonally adjusted sales rose 1.2% in the month, compared to 0.1% a month earlier, boosted by...
Summary: US retail sales ended the year on a high note with a 1.2% increase in December, driven by strong car sales, and a 8% annual gain, the best performance since 1999. Sales for the year broke through the $4 trillion mark. However, analysts expect the strong figures to have limited impact on the Federal Reserve's interest rate policy.

Title: Winemaker rejects Foster's offer
Article_Text: Australian winemaker Southcorp has rejected a takeover offer worth 3.1bn Australian dollars ($2.3bn; £1.8bn) from brewing giant Foster's Group.  Southcorp, whose brands include Penfolds, Rosemount and...
Summary: Australian winemaker Southcorp has rejected a takeover offer worth 3.1bn Australian dollars from brewing giant Foster's Group, citing the offer as inadequate. The two companies held talks after Foster's bought an 18.8% stake in Southcorp. A merger would create a global player with worldwide annual sales of 39m cases and revenues of A$2.6bn.

Title: McDonald's boss Bell dies aged 44
Article_Text: Charlie Bell, the straight-talking former head of fast-food giant McDonald's, has died of cancer aged 44.  Mr Bell was diagnosed with colorectal cancer in May last year, a month after taking over the ...
Summary: Charlie Bell, the former head of McDonald's, has died of cancer at 44. He took over the top job in May last year and resigned in November to fight the illness. Bell is credited with helping revive McDonald's sales.

Title: US industrial output growth eases
Article_Text: US industrial production continued to rise in November, albeit at a slower pace than the previous month.  The US Federal Reserve said output from factories, mines and utilities rose 0.3% - in line wit...
Summary: US industrial production rose 0.3% in November, with mining output driving the increase, while factory output rose 0.3% and utility output dropped 1.4%. The growth is consistent with an economy growing at 3.5 to 4.0%. Industrial output has grown 4.2% in the past year.

Title: LSE doubts boost bidders' shares
Article_Text: Shares in Deutsche Boerse have risen more than 3% after a shareholder fund voiced opposition to the firm's planned takeover of the London Stock Exchange.  TCI, which claims to represent owners of 5% o...
Summary: Shares in Deutsche Boerse have risen after a shareholder fund voiced opposition to the firm's planned takeover of the London Stock Exchange, citing a high offer price. The opposition has sparked speculation that the proposed takeover could fail. Deutsche Boerse has stated that it is committed to the deal and will not be swayed by TCI's concerns.

Title: Qantas considers offshore option
Article_Text: Australian airline Qantas could transfer as many as 7,000 jobs out of its home country as it seeks to save costs, according to newspaper reports.  Chief executive Geoff Dixon was quoted by The Austral...
Summary: Australian airline Qantas is considering transferring up to 7,000 jobs overseas to reduce costs, despite making a record profit last year. The airline's chief executive, Geoff Dixon, said it needs to source products and staff from overseas to remain competitive. Qantas has committed to creating jobs in Australia, but unions have criticized the move as unnecessary.

Title: Gazprom 'in $36m back-tax claim'
Article_Text: The nuclear unit of Russian energy giant Gazprom is reportedly facing a 1bn rouble ($35.7m; £19.1m) back-tax claim for the 2001-2003 period.  Vedomosti newspaper reported that Russian authorities made...
Summary: Russian authorities have made a 1bn rouble back-tax claim against Gazprom for the 2001-2003 period, mostly linked to export activity. Gazprom is set to merge with Rosneft, a move that could help the government regain state influence over the energy sector. The claim is seen as a tool to boost state control over strategically important sectors.

Title: Germany calls for EU reform
Article_Text: German Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder has called for radical reform of the EU's stability pact to grant countries more flexibility over their budget deficits.  Mr Schroeder said existing fiscal rules sh...
Summary: German Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder is calling for radical reform of the EU's stability pact to grant countries more flexibility over their budget deficits, proposing exemptions for countries meeting certain criteria.

Title: Parmalat founder offers apology
Article_Text: The founder and former boss of Parmalat has apologised to investors who lost money as a result of the Italian dairy firm's collapse.  Calisto Tanzi said he would co-operate fully with prosecutors inve...
Summary: Calisto Tanzi, the founder of Parmalat, has apologized to investors who lost money due to the Italian dairy firm's collapse. Prosecutors are investigating the background of the scandal, which led to the bankruptcy of Parmalat in 2003. The firm's collapse resulted in over 130,000 people losing money.

Title: 'Golden economic period' to end
Article_Text: Ten years of "golden" economic performance may come to an end in 2005 with growth slowing markedly, City consultancy Deloitte has warned.  The UK economy could suffer a backlash from the slowdown in t...
Summary: Deloitte has warned that the UK economy may experience a slowdown in 2005, with growth expected to be 2% and interest rates falling to 4% by the end of the year. The slowdown is attributed to a decline in the housing market, which could lead to a fall in consumer spending and a rise in unemployment. The UK economy has enjoyed a decade of growth, but Deloitte believes this growth has been achieved at the expense of creating economic imbalances.

Title: Jobs go at Oracle after takeover
Article_Text: Oracle has announced it is cutting about 5,000 jobs following the completion of its $10.3bn takeover of its smaller rival Peoplesoft last week.  The company said it would retain more than 90% of Peopl...
Summary: Oracle is cutting about 5,000 jobs following its $10.3bn takeover of Peoplesoft, retaining over 90% of Peoplesoft product development staff. The cuts affect about 9% of the combined companies' 55,000 staff. Oracle's CEO Larry Ellison said the move will allow the company to deliver on its commitments to Peoplesoft customers.

Title: Beijingers fume over parking fees
Article_Text: Choking traffic jams in Beijing are prompting officials to look at reorganising car parking charges.  Car ownership has risen fast in recent years, and there are now two and a half million cars on the...
Summary: Beijing is considering reorganizing car parking charges due to high traffic congestion caused by drivers circling for cheaper outdoor options. Officials aim to close the price gap between indoor and outdoor parking bays. The city's car ownership has risen rapidly, with 2.5 million cars on the roads.
Key_Entities: Beijing Municipal Commission for Development and Reform

Title: GM issues 2005 profits warning
Article_Text: General Motors has warned that it expects earnings this year be lower than in 2004.  The world's biggest car maker is grappling with losses in its European business, and weak US sales. GM said higher ...
Summary: General Motors has warned that it expects lower earnings this year due to losses in its European business and weak US sales. The company expects to meet its 2004 earnings targets despite a tough competitive environment. GM plans to deliver a shareholder payout of $6.0-$6.5 per share this year.

Title: US economy still growing says Fed
Article_Text: Most areas of the US saw their economy continue to expand in December and early January, the US Federal Reserve said in its latest Beige Book report.  Of the 12 US regions it identifies for the study,...
Summary: The US economy continued to expand in December and early January, with 11 of 12 regions showing stronger economic growth, according to the Beige Book report. Consumer spending and employment improved, while wage pressures remained modest. Residential and commercial real estate activity remained strong.

Title: Wall Street cool to eBay's profit
Article_Text: Shares in online auction house eBay fell 9.8% in after-hours trade on Wednesday, after its quarterly profits failed to meet market expectations.  Despite seeing net profits rise by 44% to $205.4m (£11...
Summary: eBay's quarterly profits fell short of market expectations, despite a 44% increase in net profits to $205.4m. The company's stock price dropped 9.8% after-hours, and analysts attributed this to Wall Street's high expectations. eBay president Meg Whitman expressed confidence in the company's future.

Title: WorldCom trial starts in New York
Article_Text: The trial of Bernie Ebbers, former chief executive of bankrupt US phone company WorldCom, has started in New York with the selection of the jury.  Mr Ebbers, 63, is accused of being the mastermind beh...
Summary: The trial of Bernie Ebbers, former WorldCom CEO, has started in New York, with charges including securities fraud and conspiracy. Ebbers is accused of masterminding an $11bn accounting fraud that led to WorldCom's collapse in 2002. The trial is expected to last two months.

Title: High fuel costs hit US airlines
Article_Text: Two of the largest airlines in the US - American and Southwest - have blamed record fuel prices for their disappointing quarterly results.  American Airlines' parent AMR reported a loss of $387m (£206...
Summary: Two major US airlines, American and Southwest, reported disappointing quarterly results due to high fuel prices. American Airlines lost $387m, while Southwest Airlines saw a 15% decline in profits. Both airlines expect high fuel prices to continue affecting revenues in 2005.

Title: European losses hit GM's profits
Article_Text: General Motors (GM) saw its net profits fall 37% in the last quarter of 2004, as it continued to be hit by losses at its European operations.  The US giant earned $630m (£481.5m) in the October-to-Dec...
Summary: General Motors saw its net profits fall 37% in the last quarter of 2004 due to losses at its European operations. The company earned $630m in the October-to-December period, down from $1bn in the fourth quarter of 2003. GM's revenues rose 4.7% to $51.2bn.

Title: EU to probe Alitalia 'state aid'
Article_Text: The European Commission has officially launched an in-depth investigation into whether Italian airline Alitalia is receiving illegal state aid.  Commission officials are to look at Rome's provision of...
Summary: The European Commission has launched an investigation into Italian airline Alitalia to determine if it is receiving illegal state aid from the Italian government. The investigation will look at a 400m euro loan provided to Alitalia as part of its restructuring plan. The Commission aims to verify that the plan does not contain state aid.

Title: IMF agrees fresh Turkey funding
Article_Text: Turkey has agreed a draft proposal with the International Monetary Fund to borrow $10bn (£5.19bn), extending its ongoing financial support until 2007.  Turkey's current $18.6bn loan agreement with the...
Summary: Turkey has agreed a draft proposal with the International Monetary Fund to borrow $10bn, extending its financial support until 2007. The new deal would see Turkey receive added support between 2005 and 2007, in return for keeping inflation under control and introducing market reforms. Turkey's economy has steadily recovered from a severe crisis in 2001.

Title: Saudi investor picks up the Savoy
Article_Text: London's famous Savoy hotel has been sold to a group combining Saudi billionaire investor Prince Alwaleed bin Talal and a unit of HBOS bank.  Financial details of the deal, which includes the nearby S...
Summary: The Savoy hotel in London has been sold to a group combining Prince Alwaleed bin Talal and a unit of HBOS bank. The deal includes the nearby Simpson's in the Strand restaurant. Renovations are planned by Fairmont Hotels & Resorts.

Title: Tsunami slows Sri Lanka's growth
Article_Text: Sri Lanka's president has launched a reconstruction drive worth $3.5bn (£1.8bn) by appealing for peace and national unity.  President Kumaratunga said it was now important to find a peaceful solution ...
Summary: Sri Lanka's President Kumaratunga has launched a $3.5 billion reconstruction drive, appealing for peace and national unity in the wake of the devastating tsunami. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimates that the tsunami will cut one percentage point from Sri Lanka's economic growth this year, with physical damage equivalent to 6.5% of the economy. The International Labour Organisation (ILO) reports that at least one million people have lost their livelihoods in Sri Lanka and Indonesia, with the IMF warning of potential economic strain and strain on foreign exchange reserves.

Title: China suspends 26 power projects
Article_Text: China has ordered a halt to construction work on 26 big power stations, including two at the Three Gorges Dam, on environmental grounds.  The move is a surprising one because China is struggling to in...
Summary: China has ordered a halt to construction work on 26 big power stations due to environmental concerns, citing lack of proper environmental assessments. The move is a surprise given China's energy shortage. The halt affects projects including the Three Gorges Dam and a controversial dam on the Yangtze River.

Title: Two Nigerian banks set to merge
Article_Text: Nigerian banks United Bank of Africa and Standard Trust Bank have agreed plans to merge and create the biggest bank in West Africa.  The deal is also in line with a 2004 directive from the Nigerian ce...
Summary: Nigerian banks United Bank of Africa and Standard Trust Bank have agreed to merge, creating the biggest bank in West Africa, in line with a 2004 directive from the Nigerian central bank. The merger was announced without revealing financial details. United Bank is the third biggest in Nigeria, while Standard Trust is smaller but more profitable.

Title: Virgin Blue shares plummet 20%
Article_Text: Shares in Australian budget airline Virgin Blue plunged 20% after it warned of a steep fall in full year profits.  Virgin Blue said profits after tax for the year to March would be between 10% to 15% ...
Summary: Shares in Australian budget airline Virgin Blue fell 20% after the company warned of lower full-year profits due to sluggish demand and rising fuel costs. Virgin Blue's chief executive, Brett Godfrey, attributed the decline to competition from rival Jetstar. The airline has been struggling since its launch four years ago.

Title: Watchdog probes Vivendi bond sale
Article_Text: French stock market regulator AMF has filed complaints against media giant Vivendi Universal, its boss and another top executive.  It believes the prospectus for a bond issue was unclear and that exec...
Summary: The French stock market regulator AMF has filed complaints against Vivendi Universal, its CEO Jean-Rene Fourtou, COO Jean-Bernard Levy, and Deutsche Bank, alleging unclear prospectus and potential privileged information. Vivendi has denied the charges, while AMF is investigating claims of insider trading. The watchdog is also looking into whether the executives knew about Vivendi's consideration to buy British Telecom's shares in Cegetel.

Title: Saudi NCCI's shares soar
Article_Text: Shares in Saudi Arabia's National Company for Cooperative Insurance (NCCI) soared on their first day of trading in Riyadh.  They were trading 84% above the offer price on Monday, changing hands at 372...
Summary: Shares in Saudi Arabia's National Company for Cooperative Insurance (NCCI) soared on their first day of trading in Riyadh, with demand 12 times higher than the offer price. The listing aims to boost demand in the insurance sector and introduce a fully functioning insurance industry. NCCI is being developed as the industry's flagship firm.

Title: JP Morgan admits US slavery links
Article_Text: Thousands of slaves were accepted as collateral for loans by two banks that later became part of JP Morgan Chase.  The admission is part of an apology sent to JP Morgan staff after the bank researched...
Summary: JP Morgan Chase has apologized for its historical links to slavery, admitting that two of its predecessor banks, Citizens Bank and Canal Bank, accepted slaves as collateral for loans between 1831 and 1865. The bank has set up a $5m scholarship programme for students in Louisiana. JP Morgan has acknowledged that its history is intertwined with the institution of slavery.

Title: Egypt and Israel seal trade deal
Article_Text: In a sign of a thaw in relations between Egypt and Israel, the two countries have signed a trade protocol with the US, allowing Egyptian goods made in partnership with Israeli firms free access to Ame...
Summary: Egypt and Israel have signed a trade protocol with the US, allowing Egyptian goods made in partnership with Israeli firms free access to American markets. The protocol establishes 'qualified industrial zones' in Egypt, with products from these zones enjoying duty-free access to the US if 35% of their components are the product of Israeli-Egyptian cooperation. The agreement is seen as a significant economic development between the two countries.

Title: Ford gains from finance not cars
Article_Text: Ford, the US car company, reported higher fourth quarter and full-year profits on Thursday boosted by a buoyant period for its car loans unit.  Net income for 2004 was $3.5bn (£1.87bn) - up nearly $3b...
Summary: Ford reported higher profits in the fourth quarter and full year due to a strong performance from its car loans unit, but its auto unit made a loss. The company's net income rose to $3.5bn, while turnover increased to $170.8bn. Ford is working to revitalize its product portfolio with new models unveiled at the International Motor Show.

Title: Wipro beats forecasts once again
Article_Text: Wipro, India's third-biggest software firm, has reported a 60% rise in profit, topping market expectations.  Net income in the last quarter was 4.3bn rupees ($98m; £52m), against 2.7bn a year earlier....
Summary: Wipro, India's third-biggest software firm, has reported a 60% rise in profit, beating market expectations. The company's net income in the last quarter was 4.3bn rupees, with sales rising 34% to 20.9bn rupees. Wipro attributed the growth to strong demand and increased prices.

Title: Christmas sales worst since 1981
Article_Text: UK retail sales fell in December, failing to meet expectations and making it by some counts the worst Christmas since 1981.  Retail sales dropped by 1% on the month in December, after a 0.6% rise in N...
Summary: UK retail sales fell 1% in December, the worst Christmas since 1981, with clothing retailers and non-specialist stores being the worst hit. However, some retailers reported strong festive sales, and analysts note that the figures may not accurately reflect Christmas trading until Easter. The Bank of England is unlikely to be affected by the poor figures.

Title: Businesses fail to plan for HIV

Summary: A new report by the World Economic Forum, Harvard, and the UN AIDS agency found that companies are only taking action on HIV/AIDS when the disease affects a significant portion of the population, with 71% having no policies in place. However, one company, Anglo-American, has implemented a successful plan to address the issue in its workforce.

Summary: EuroDisney plans to sell 253m euros of new shares to restructure 2.4bn euros-worth of debts, following recent progress in turning its business around. The sale is the last part of a plan to avoid insolvency. EuroDisney remains Europe's largest single tourist attraction, attracting 12.4 million visitors annually.

Title: UK young top Euro earnings league

Summary: British children between 10 and 17 have the highest average annual income in Europe, with £775, according to a report by Datamonitor. The majority of their spending goes to personal care, soft drinks, and food. The report also notes that British teenagers are popular among cosmetics manufacturers due to their willingness to experiment with products.

Title: Swiss cement firm in buying spree

Summary: Swiss cement firm Holcim has bid $800m to buy two Indian cement firms and a holding company in the country. The deal will give Holcim an entry into the UK market and boost its presence in the US. Shares in ACC fell 5.5% as investors deemed the offer underpriced.

Title: India's Reliance family feud heats up

The board considered Anil's resignation and Anil's demand to remove a board member, Anand Jain, who is accused of creating a rift in the Ambani family. The Ambani family controls 48% of the Reliance Group, worth $17bn.

Title: World leaders gather to face uncertainty
