Summary: More than 2,000 business and political leaders are gathering in Davos for the World Economic Forum, discussing issues like China's economic power and Iraq's future after elections. The event will feature prominent leaders like Tony Blair, Thabo Mbeki, and Viktor Yushchenko, and will focus on business issues with a lack of an overarching theme.

Title: US budget deficit to reach $368bn
Article_Text: The US budget deficit is set to hit a worse-than-expected $368bn (£197bn) this year, officials said on Tuesday.  The cost of military operations still needs to be factored in, with analysts saying the...
Summary: The US budget deficit is projected to reach $368bn (£197bn) this year, surpassing previous forecasts of $348bn, with analysts warning that military costs could add an additional $100bn. The deficit has widened to a record $60bn in November, driven by twin deficits in trade and military operations, and is expected to decline in the next two years. The Congressional Budget Office forecasts a total shortfall of $855bn from 2006 to 2015, but analysts warn that the actual figure could be higher due to the costs of the president's pension and tax cut plans.

Title: Criminal probe on Citigroup deals
Article_Text: Traders at US banking giant Citigroup are facing a criminal investigation in Germany over a controversial bond deal.  The deal saw the sale of 11bn euros ($14.4bn; £7.6bn) of government bonds in a few...
Summary: Traders at Citigroup are facing a criminal investigation in Germany over a controversial bond deal, with evidence of possible market manipulation found by the German regulator BaFin. The deal saw the sale and subsequent buyback of 11 billion euros worth of government bonds in a short period. Citigroup has agreed to cooperate with the authorities.

Title: Brazil jobless rate hits new low
Article_Text: Brazil's unemployment rate fell to its lowest level in three years in December, according to the government.  The Brazilian Institute for Geography and Statistics (IBGE) said it fell to 9.6% in Decemb...
Summary: Brazil's unemployment rate fell to 9.6% in December, its lowest level in three years, according to the Brazilian Institute for Geography and Statistics (IBGE). The rate has been declining since April 2004, when it reached a peak of 13.1%, and is attributed to the country's strong economic growth, which registered a 5.2% growth in 2004. The government expects the economy to grow by 4% this year, but some analysts predict a possible increase in unemployment in the next months.

Title: Indonesia 'declines debt freeze'
Article_Text: Indonesia no longer needs the debt freeze offered by the Paris Club group of creditors, Economics Minister Aburizal Bakrie has reportedly said.  Indonesia, which originally accepted the debt moratoriu...
Summary: Indonesia no longer needs a debt freeze offer from the Paris Club group of creditors due to a $1.7bn donors' aid package, according to Economics Minister Aburizal Bakrie. The package, combined with a previously-pledged $3.4bn, will be used to finance the country's budget deficit and rebuild Aceh province. Indonesia is still considering the Paris Club offer, but has not yet decided on the details.

Title: Parmalat bank barred from suing

Summary: Bank of America has been barred from suing Parmalat due to a judge's ruling, while other parties involved in the case are still allowed to pursue damages. The bank and auditors claim to have been victims of fraud. Parmalat collapsed in 2003 after an accounting scandal.

Summary: China's economy expanded by 9.5% in 2004, faster than predicted, but with slowing industrial growth and rising consumer prices, which could lead to higher interest rates and inflation.

Summary: A BBC World Service poll found that most respondents believe the world economy is worsening, but a majority in 14 countries are positive about their family's financial outlook. The poll was conducted in 22 countries and involved 23,000 people. The results suggest that people are pessimistic about the world economy, but optimistic about their own families' financial conditions.

Summary: Two senior officials at Bank of China have disappeared after funds worth up to $120m went missing, amid concerns over regulatory requirements and bad debt. China's banking sector is burdened with bad debt, with one in five loans not being repaid.

Title: Low-cost airlines hit Eurotunnel

Summary: Eurotunnel's sales fell 4% in 2004 to 789m euros due to the rise of low-cost airlines, with income from its shuttle services down 7% despite a 2% rise in railway revenue. The company is struggling with debts of over 6bn euros and is kept afloat by its banks. Eurotunnel's future is uncertain.

Title: Water firm Suez in Argentina row

Summary: A conflict between the Argentine government and water firm Aguas Argentinas, controlled by France's Suez, is ongoing over a proposed 60% tariff rise to fund water-supply improvements. The government has rejected the rise and wants Aguas Argentinas to make an annual investment of 400m pesos, with Planning Minister Julio De Vido offering State help in return for a board seat. The firm has refused to accept any change to its legal structure, which rules out State participation on its board.

Summary: Algeria experienced violent protests over government plans to raise gas prices, with demonstrators blocking roads and attacking public buildings. Protests flared up in several regions, including Bouira, Tiaret, and Maghnia.

Title: India's Maruti sees profits jump

Summary: Maruti, India's biggest carmaker, reported a sharp increase in quarterly profit due to a booming economy and low interest rates. Net profit surged 70% to 2.39bn rupees, driven by demand for cheap, fuel-efficient vehicles. The company's sales rose 27% to 30.1bn rupees.

Summary: China surpassed the US as Japan's largest trading partner in 2004, with 20.1% of Japan's trade, according to Japan's Finance Ministry. This marks a significant shift in Japan's trade dynamics, driven by China's growing economic importance. Japan's trade surplus with China also increased by 17.9% in 2004.

Summary: More than 90% of large companies worldwide are optimistic about their economic prospects, with over-regulation, low-cost competition, and oil prices being their biggest concerns. Firms in Western Europe, except the UK, lack confidence due to slow growth. Global business leaders face a two-pronged regulatory assault, with some companies moving operations to low-wage countries to combat low-cost competition.

Blair denied attacking Howard politically and said he would never comment on his Jewish beliefs.

Title: Parties' plans for council tax
Article_Text: Anger at council tax rises spilled over into mass protests in 2003, when the average English bill rose 12.9%.  Pensioners' protests spread - some marched, others simply refused to pay the increase. So...
Summary: Mass protests in 2003 were sparked by council tax rises, with pensioners refusing to pay the increase. The Tories propose a rebate for pensioners, while the Liberal Democrats want to abolish the council tax and introduce a local income tax.

Title: Labour in constituency race row
Article_Text: Labour's choice of a white candidate for one of the UK's most multi-racial seats proves the need for all-black short lists, says a race group.  Local councillor Lyn Brown was selected for West Ham, ea...
Summary: A race group is calling for all-black shortlists after a Labour councillor from a multi-racial seat was selected from a mixed group of candidates. Summary: A cross-party group of MPs has published a blueprint for reforming the House of Lords, proposing a smaller second chamber with 70% elected members. The government has postponed plans to remove hereditary peers, citing opposition from the Lords. The group believes its plan would win support from a large majority of MPs.

Title: Hague's six-figure earnings shown
Article_Text: The rewards of leaving front-bench politics are shown in the latest annual register of members' interests.  The register shows former Tory leader William Hague earning up to £820,000 on top of his MPs...
Summary: The latest annual register of members' interests shows former politicians earning significant amounts from speaking fees, book sales, and other activities after leaving front-bench politics.

Title: Schools to take part in mock poll
Article_Text: Record numbers of schools across the UK are to take part in a mock general election backed by the government.  Some 600 schools have already signed up for the Y Vote Mock Elections 2005 run by the Han...
Summary: Record numbers of schools in the UK are participating in a mock general election to boost interest in politics among young people. The Y Vote Mock Elections 2005 initiative, run by the Hansard Society, aims to teach pupils about the democratic process and encourage them to participate in future elections. The mock elections will take place around May 5, coinciding with the expected date of the general election.

Title: Parties build up poll war chests
Article_Text: The Labour Party received more than £5m in donations in the final quarter of 2004, new figures show.  This is nearly half of the £11,724,929 received by 16 political parties listed by the Electoral Co...
Summary: The Labour Party received over £5m in donations in the final quarter of 2004, with the majority coming from affiliated trade unions and individuals such as Lord Drayson and Sir Christopher Ondaatje. The Conservatives received £4,610,849, while the Liberal Democrats received just over £1m. The UK Independence Party received £63,081, mostly in gifts in kind.

Title: Kennedy predicts bigger turnout
Article_Text: Voters' "pent up passion" could confound predictions of a low turnout in the coming general election, Charles Kennedy has said.  The Liberal Democrat leader predicted concerns over Iraq and other inte...
Summary: Liberal Democrat leader Charles Kennedy and ex-foreign secretary Robin Cook expressed concerns about low voter turnout in the coming general election, citing the need for politicians to connect with the public and avoid negative campaigning.

Title: Iraq advice claim sparks new row

Summary: The Tories and Liberal Democrats are calling for the publication of the full legal advice given by the Attorney General Lord Goldsmith on the Iraq war, while the government has consistently refused to release the documents, citing confidentiality. Lord Goldsmith has denied being 'leaned on' in drafting the advice. Ex-foreign secretary Robin Cook says all the advice should be published.

Title: UKIP could sue Veritas defectors
Article_Text: The UK Independence Party could take legal action to unseat two London Assembly members who defected to Robert Kilroy Silk's Veritas Party.  Damian Hockney, now Veritas deputy leader, and Peter Hulme-...
Summary: The UK Independence Party is considering legal action against two London Assembly members who defected to Robert Kilroy Silk's Veritas Party, arguing they should give up their seats as they won them as UKIP representatives. Summary: Michael Howard accuses Tony Blair of playing politics with the security of the nation by pushing through anti-terror measures without proper debate. The prime minister claims the opposition is playing politics with the issue, while the Liberal Democrats say the government's instinct is authoritarian.

Summary: The attorney general has denied drafting his statement to Parliament about the legality of the Iraq war with Downing Street officials, claiming it represented his own view on the matter. The government has resisted calls to publish the full advice, citing confidentiality.

Title: Goldsmith: 'I was not leant on'

Summary: The attorney general has denied being influenced by Downing Street in drafting the legal case for invading Iraq, claiming the written answer was his independent view. Title: Tory expert denies defeat warning

Summary: The Conservatives' campaign director Lynton Crosby denied a report claiming he warned Michael Howard the party could not win the next general election.

Title: Manchester wins Labour conference

Summary: The Labour Party has decided to hold its 2006 autumn conference in Manchester instead of Blackpool, a break from the traditional seaside venue choice. Title: Labour attacked on Howard poster

Summary: Labour's election campaign posters were defended by Alan Milburn amid claims they were anti-Semitic, with the party withdrawing two controversial designs and launching new ones that target Tory leader Michael Howard personally.

Title: Kilroy names election seat target

Summary: Robert Kilroy-Silk, a former UK Independence Party (UKIP) member, is contesting the Derbyshire seat of Erewash at the next general election, launching his new party Veritas. Kilroy-Silk, who quit UKIP last week, aims to "change the face" of UK politics with Veritas, which plans to contest most seats at the general election. The move comes after UKIP's leader Roger Knapman expressed relief at Kilroy-Silk's departure, citing concerns over his loyalty to the party.

Title: Immigration to be election issue
Article_Text: Immigration and asylum have normally been issues politicians from the big parties have tiptoed around at election time.  But no longer. Both Labour and the Tories have signalled their intention of mak...
Summary: Immigration and asylum are becoming central issues in the UK election campaigns, with both Labour and the Tories proposing tough policies. Summary: Liberal Democrat leader Charles Kennedy is on a week-long tour to persuade voters that his party is the real opposition, visiting constituencies in Somerset and Hampshire, as well as targeted areas for Labour and the Conservatives. Summary: The Liberal Democrats have unveiled plans to build 100,000 new affordable homes on publicly owned land, allowing people to buy a share in a home through a mutual home ownership trust. Summary: The Liberal Democrats are launching a manifesto for women, pledging policies such as a maternity income guarantee and a pension system based on years of residence, to appeal to female voters. Summary: Gordon Brown outlined his vision for New Labour's next general election bid, focusing on key themes such as ensuring every child in Britain has the best start in life and promoting lifelong education and good health. Summary: The UK government plans to lower the minimum age for becoming an MP from 21 to 18, following a recommendation by the Electoral Commission. The campaign will focus on examining the opposition's policies and past record.

Summary: Gordon Brown has issued a rallying cry to supporters, warning of the high stakes in the next general election and promising a Labour government that will reform and renew public services, while the Conservatives and Lib Dems claim Labour will lead to higher taxes and means-testing.

Summary: Tony Blair has backed Chancellor Gordon Brown's pre-Budget report, which forecasts UK growth at 3-3.5% for next year. The report has been met with skepticism from some experts, who fear tax rises or spending cuts. Labour's next election campaign is already well advanced.

Summary: Ministers are unhappy about plans to use Whitehall cash to keep council tax bills down, local government minister Nick Raynsford has acknowledged. Summary: Gordon Brown is expected to use his pre-election budget to offer vote-winning sweeteners, breaking historical precedent if he doesn't. Summary: Spain won the Davis Cup for the second time in their history, beating the USA 3-2 in the final. Carlos Moya defeated Andy Roddick in the fourth rubber, while Mardy Fish won the final dead rubber. The final was played in Seville, with a record crowd of 27,000 spectators.

Summary: Jennifer Capriati has withdrawn from the Australian Open due to a shoulder injury, joining other absentees including last year's champion Justin Henin-Hardenne and runner-up Kim Clijsters.

Summary: Tim Henman won his 2005 campaign with a 6-1 7-5 victory over David Nalbandian at the Kooyong Classic exhibition tournament. He will next play Roger Federer at the Australian Open warm-up event on Friday. Roger Federer also won his match, beating Gaston Gaudio, while Andre Agassi defeated Nicolas Massu.

Summary: The United States kept the Davis Cup final alive with a victory in the doubles rubber, leaving Spain 2-1 ahead going into the final day. The Bryans thrashed Juan Carlos Ferrero and Tommy Robredo in Seville, while Rafael Nadal was rested for the doubles match.

Title: Faultless Federer has no equal

Summary: Roger Federer is considered the best tennis player, with an open-era record of 11 titles from 11 finals and 13 final victories in a row. He is also a prominent ambassador for tennis, promoting the sport off court and conducting numerous interviews.

Title: Mauresmo opens with victory in LA
Article_Text: Amelie Mauresmo and Maria Sharapova won their opening matches at the Tour Championships in Los Angeles.  France's Mauresmo routed Vera Zvonareva 6-1 6-0, while Wimbledon champion Sharapova was a 6-1 6...
Summary: Amelie Mauresmo, Maria Sharapova, and Serena Williams won their opening matches at the Tour Championships in Los Angeles. Mauresmo defeated Vera Zvonareva 6-1 6-0, while Sharapova beat Svetlana Kuznetsova 6-1 6-4. The event is split into two groups of four, with the top two from each advancing to the semi-finals, as Mauresmo seeks to regain the number one spot.

Title: Agassi fear for Melbourne
Article_Text: Andre Agassi's involvement in the Australian Open was put in doubt after he pulled out of the Kooyong Classic with a hip injury.  Agassi was serving at 5-6 down in the first set to fellow American And...
Summary: Andre Agassi pulled out of the Kooyong Classic with a hip injury, citing cramping that made it uncomfortable to continue playing. He plans to undergo an MRI scan to determine the extent of the damage. The injury is not the same as the one that forced him to miss Wimbledon last year.

Title: Henman to face Saulnier test

Summary: British tennis player Tim Henman will face France's Cyril Saulnier in the first round of the Australian Open next week. Henman, the seventh seed, is looking forward to the match, having previously defeated Saulnier in the first round of the French Open last year. Henman's opponent, Saulnier, is considered a tough player on any surface, and Henman will need to play well from the outset to overcome him.

Title: Moya suffers shock loss
Article_Text: Fifth seed Carlos Moya was the first big name to fall at the Australian Open as he went down to fellow Spaniard Guillermo Garcia-Lopez on Monday.  Moya began the year with victory at the Chennai Open ...
Summary: Carlos Moya lost to Guillermo Garcia-Lopez in the Australian Open, while Andre Agassi won his match despite a hip injury. Other players made progress in the tournament.

Title: Clijsters hope on Aussie Open
Article_Text: Kim Clijsters has denied reports that she has pulled out of January's Australian Open because of her persistent wrist injury.  Open chief Paul McNamee had said: "Kim's wrist obviously isn't going to b...
Summary: Kim Clijsters has denied reports that she has pulled out of the Australian Open due to a wrist injury, saying she has simply delayed submitting her entry. The Open chief, Paul McNamee, had stated that Clijsters' wrist injury would not be rehabilitated. Clijsters is still ranked 22nd in the world despite only playing a handful of matches last season.

Title: Clijsters could play Aussie Open

Summary: Kim Clijsters has denied reports that she has pulled out of the Australian Open due to a wrist injury, saying she has simply delayed submitting her entry. The Open chief, Paul McNamee, had expressed doubts about her ability to play. Clijsters is still ranked 22nd in the world despite a recent injury.

Title: Edgy Agassi struggles past Dent
Article_Text: Andre Agassi put in an erratic display before edging into the fourth round of the Australian Open with victory over Taylor Dent.  The 34-year-old American, seeded eighth, made a poor start, dropping s...
Summary: Andre Agassi edged into the fourth round of the Australian Open with a 7-5 7-6 (7-3) 6-1 win over Taylor Dent, while Rafael Nadal survived an injury scare to beat Mario Ancic. Roger Federer also advanced with a 6-3 5-2 win over Jarkko Nieminen, and Dominik Hrbaty defeated 10th seed Marat Safin in a five-set match.

Title: Roddick splits from coach Gilbert

Summary: Andy Roddick has ended his 18-month association with coach Brad Gilbert, citing what he believes is best for his game. Roddick won 121 of his 147 matches with Gilbert, including the US Open title. The split comes after Gilbert's departure from Roger Federer's coaching team.

Title: Roddick in talks over new coach

Summary: Andy Roddick is reportedly close to confirming US Davis Cup assistant Dean Goldfine as his new coach, ending his 18-month partnership with Brad Gilbert.

Title: Hewitt survives Nalbandian epic

Summary: Lleyton Hewitt defeated David Nalbandian in a five-set match to reach the Australian Open semi-finals. Hewitt dominated the first two sets but allowed Nalbandian to come back in the third set. He eventually won the match in four hours and five minutes.

Title: Sydney return for Henin-Hardenne
Article_Text: Olympic champion Justine Henin-Hardenne will return to action in January's Sydney International tournament.  The Belgian has not competed since losing her top world ranking at the US Open in September...
Summary: Olympic champion Justine Henin-Hardenne will return to action in January's Sydney International tournament, while world number one Lindsay Davenport and French Open champion Anastasia Myskina will also compete. Men's event will be defended by Lleyton Hewitt and Carlos Moya, who had to retire with an ankle injury in the Davis Cup final.

Title: Koubek suspended after drugs test

Summary: Stefan Koubek has been banned for three months by the International Tennis Federation after testing positive for a banned substance

Title: Hewitt fights back to reach final
Article_Text: Lleyton Hewitt kept his dream of an Australian Open title alive with a four-set win over Andy Roddick in Friday's second semi-final.  The home favourite will face Marat Safin in Sunday's final after c...
Summary: Lleyton Hewitt won a four-set match against Andy Roddick to reach the Australian Open final, where he will face Marat Safin. Hewitt fought back from a set down to win the match. He is aiming to be the first Australian winner since 1976.

Title: Officials respond in court row

Summary: Australian tennis official Geoff Pollard defended the Australian Open courts at Melbourne Park after criticism from Lleyton Hewitt, who said the surface was not worthy of the tournament. Pollard said the surface had been speeded up since last year's tournament following complaints from Australian players. The tournament starts on January 17.

Title: Williams battles to Aussie title

Summary: Serena Williams made a remarkable recovery to beat Lindsay Davenport and win her second Australian Open title, claiming her seventh Grand Slam title. Williams had a rib injury but came back to win the match 2-6 6-3 6-0. Davenport praised Williams for her comeback.

Title: Safin cool on Wimbledon

Summary: Marat Safin has ruled out winning Wimbledon, citing his struggles on grass courts, but is hopeful that winning the Australian Open will give him the confidence to win more Grand Slam titles.

Summary: Marat Safin has ruled out winning Wimbledon, citing his struggles on grass courts, but is hopeful that winning the Australian Open will give him the confidence to win more Grand Slam titles.

Summary: Rafael Nadal of Spain beats Andy Roddick of the USA in the second singles match rubber of the 2004 Davis Cup final in Seville, Spain, leading Spain to a 2-0 lead in the tie.

Title: Henman & Murray claim LTA awards
Article_Text: Tim Henman was named player of the year for 2004 by the Lawn Tennis Association at Wimbledon on Monday.  The Briton was recognised for the best year of his career, which saw him reach the semis at the...
Summary: Tim Henman was named player of the year for 2004 by the Lawn Tennis Association at Wimbledon, recognizing his best year, which included reaching the semis at the French and US Opens. Andrew Murray was named young player of the year after winning the US Open juniors and a Futures event in Italy, while Peter Norfolk won disabled player of the year after claiming his third US Open crown. Henman plans to start his 2005 campaign at the Kooyong event on January 12, aiming to improve on his previous Australian Open performance.

Title: Connors' rallying cry for British tennis
Article_Text: "Do you have it in your heart? How much guts do you have? How much do you hate to lose?"  These are the questions Jimmy Connors will be asking of Britain's brightest tennis hopes in the months, and po...
Summary: Jimmy Connors has announced a long-term relationship with the Lawn Tennis Association, aiming to help Britain's young players develop their skills and 'will to win'. Connors praises the LTA's performance director David Felgate and his team, citing a positive attitude towards finding the next Wimbledon champion.

Title: Roche 'turns down Federer offer'

Summary: Australian tennis coach Tony Roche has turned down an offer to coach Roger Federer full-time due to health concerns, but will work with him on a casual basis.

Title: Federer joins all-time greats
Article_Text: The last year has seen one player dominate men's tennis, and one country dominate the women's game.  Roger Federer became the first man since Mats Wilander in 1988 to win three Grand Slams in one seas...
Summary: Roger Federer dominated men's tennis, winning three Grand Slams in one season, while Anastasia Myskina led the Russian women to a Grand Slam sweep. Tim Henman had a standout year, and Greg Rusedski made a remarkable comeback from a doping offense. Meanwhile, Justine Henin-Hardenne won Olympic gold, but suffered a virus, and Lindsay Davenport held off the new wave of Russian players, including Maria Sharapova and Svetlana Kuznetsova.

Title: Philippoussis doubt over Open bid
Article_Text: Mark Philippoussis is almost certain to miss the Australian Open after suffering a groin injury during the Hopman Cup loss to the Netherlands.  The 28-year-old suffered two tears to the adductor muscl...
Summary: Mark Philippoussis is unlikely to play in the Australian Open due to a groin injury, while Tommy Haas is also a doubt after picking up a thigh injury. Both players suffered injuries during the Hopman Cup.

Title: Slovakia reach Hopman Cup final
Article_Text: Slovakia will play Argentina in the final of the Hopman Cup after beating Group B rivals the Netherlands 3-0.  Daniela Hantuchova defeated Michaella Krajicek 6-4 6-2 to give the Slovaks the perfect st...
Summary: Slovakia will play Argentina in the Hopman Cup final after beating the Netherlands 3-0. Daniela Hantuchova defeated Michaella Krajicek and Dominik Hrbaty won against Peter Wessels. Argentina claimed top spot in Group A with three wins.

Summary: American Taylor Dent reached the final of the Australian hardcourt event in Adelaide after defeating Juan Ignacio Chela and Olivier Rochus

Title: Moya sidesteps Davis Cup in 2005
Article_Text: Carlos Moya has chosen not to help Spain try and defend the Davis Cup crown they won in Seville in November.  Moya led Spain to victory over the USA but wants to focus on the Grand Slams in 2005, alth...
Summary: Carlos Moya has chosen not to help Spain defend the Davis Cup crown, instead focusing on the Grand Slams in 2005. He has been working on his condition and game to be in top form for major events. Moya won the Chennai Open at the start of 2005.

Title: Henman decides to quit Davis Cup
Article_Text: Tim Henman has retired from Great Britain's Davis Cup team.  The 30-year-old, who made his Davis Cup debut in 1994, is now set to fully focus on the ATP Tour and on winning his first Grand Slam event....
Summary: Tim Henman has retired from Great Britain's Davis Cup team, citing a desire to focus on the ATP Tour and winning his first Grand Slam event. He leaves with an impressive record of 36 wins in 50 matches. Captain Jeremy Bates has praised Henman's contributions to the team and expressed optimism about the future of British Davis Cup tennis.

Title: Ivanovic seals Canberra victory

Summary: Serbia's Ana Ivanovic won her first WTA title with a straight-sets victory over Hungarian Melinda Czink in the Canberra Classic final.

Title: Minister digs in over doping row

Summary: Belgian sports minister Claude Eerdekens refuses to apologize for allegations against Russian tennis player Svetlana Kuznetsova, who tested positive for ephedrine at an exhibition event. Kuznetsova claims the stimulant was in a cold remedy she took, while Eerdekens says he made the statement to protect other players. French player Nathalie Dechy and Russian player Elena Dementieva are upset with Eerdekens' comments.

Title: Safin relieved at Aussie recovery
Article_Text: Marat Safin admitted he thought he was suffering another Australian Open final nightmare when he lost the opening set to Lleyton Hewitt.  The Russian, who lost the 2002 and 2004 finals, fought back br...
Summary: Marat Safin won the Australian Open final against Lleyton Hewitt, coming back from a set down to take the match 1-6 6-3 6-4 6-4. Safin attributed his loss to nerves and pressure, but ultimately played some of his best tennis to secure the victory.

Title: Veteran Martinez wins Thai title

Summary: Conchita Martinez won her first title in almost five years with a victory over Anna-Lena Groenefeld at the Volvo Women's Open in Pattaya, Thailand.

Title: Soderling wins tense Milan final
