Summary: Robin Soderling won the Milan Indoors title with a dramatic win over Radek Stepanek, edging the final set tie-break for a 6-3 6-7 (2-7) 7-6 (7-5) victory.

Title: Rusedski forced out in Marseille
Article_Text: Greg Rusedski was forced to withdraw from the Open 13 in Marseille on Thursday with a rib injury.  The British number two had been scheduled to play qualifier Sebastien de Chaunac, who beat world numb...
Summary: Greg Rusedski withdrew from the Open 13 in Marseille due to a rib injury, while American Taylor Dent caused a shock by defeating second seed David Nalbandian. Third seed Joachim Johansson also made it through the tournament. Other notable winners included Feliciano Lopez, Karol Beck, and Ivan Ljubicic and Mario Ancic.

Title: Big guns ease through in San Jose
Article_Text: Top-seeded Americans Andy Roddick and Andre Agassi survived minor scares to reach the last eight of the SAP Open.  Agassi endured early problems against left-handed Dane Kenneth Carlsen before sealing...
Summary: Top-seeded Americans Andy Roddick and Andre Agassi reached the quarter-finals of the SAP Open, overcoming minor setbacks. Agassi defeated Kenneth Carlsen, while Roddick pulled out a win over Hyung-Taik Lee. Roddick also broke a racket in frustration.

Title: Almagro continues Spanish surge
Article_Text: Unseeded Nicolas Almagro became the fifth Spaniard to reach the last eight at the Buenos Aires Open, ousting eighth seed Mariano Zabaleta.  He showed admirable resolve to win a rain-affected match 6-7...
Summary: Nicolas Almagro and Rafael Nadal reached the last eight at the Buenos Aires Open, defeating Mariano Zabaleta and Potito Starace respectively. The matches were affected by rain, but both players showed resilience to win. Gaston Gaudio also advanced to the next round.

Title: Melzer shocks Agassi in San Jose
Article_Text: Second seed Andre Agassi suffered a comprehensive defeat by Jurgen Melzer in the quarter-finals of the SAP Open.  Agassi was often bamboozled by the Austrian's drop shots in San Jose, losing 6-3 6-1. ...
Summary: Andre Agassi lost to Jurgen Melzer in the quarter-finals of the SAP Open, while Andy Roddick beat Thomas Enqvist and Cyril Saulnier beat Vincent Spadea and Tommy Haas beat Max Mirnyi.

Title: Mirza makes Indian tennis history
Article_Text: Teenager Sania Mirza completed a superb week at the Hyderabad Open by becoming the first Indian in history to win a WTA singles title.  In front of a delirious home crowd, the 18-year-old battled past...
Summary: Sania Mirza won the Hyderabad Open, becoming the first Indian to win a WTA singles title, defeating Alyona Bondarenko 6-4 5-7 6-3. Mirza, ranked 134 in the world, celebrated her victory in front of a home crowd.

Title: Roddick to face Saulnier in final
Article_Text: Andy Roddick will play Cyril Saulnier in the final of the SAP Open in San Jose on Sunday.  The American top seed and defending champion overcame Germany's Tommy Haas, the third seed, 7-6 (7-3) 6-3. "I...
Summary: Andy Roddick will play Cyril Saulnier in the final of the SAP Open in San Jose on Sunday after defeating Tommy Haas in the semifinals.

Title: Ink helps drive democracy in Asia
Article_Text: The Kyrgyz Republic, a small, mountainous state of the former Soviet republic, is using invisible ink and ultraviolet readers in the country's elections as part of a drive to prevent multiple voting. ...
Summary: The Kyrgyz Republic is using invisible ink and ultraviolet readers in its elections to prevent multiple voting, as part of a drive to show commitment towards more open elections. The technology is causing both worries and guarded optimism among the population. The US government has agreed to fund the expenses associated with this decision.

Title: China net cafe culture crackdown
Article_Text: Chinese authorities closed 12,575 net cafes in the closing months of 2004, the country's government said.  According to the official news agency most of the net cafes were closed down because they wer...
Summary: Chinese authorities closed 12,575 net cafes in the closing months of 2004 due to operating illegally, with the goal of creating a safer environment for young people. The government has been cracking down on net cafes since 2002, citing concerns over their influence on young people. The crackdown is part of a broader effort to control the types of computer games people can play and limit exposure to violence.

Title: Microsoft seeking spyware trojan
Article_Text: Microsoft is investigating a trojan program that attempts to switch off the firm's anti-spyware software.  The spyware tool was only released by Microsoft in the last few weeks and has been downloaded...
Summary: Microsoft is investigating a Trojan program that attempts to disable its anti-spyware software, which has been downloaded by six million people. The program, called Bankash-A Trojan, may steal online banking passwords or personal information. Microsoft plans to offer its own paid-for anti-virus software.

Title: Digital guru floats sub-$100 PC
Article_Text: Nicholas Negroponte, chairman and founder of MIT's Media Labs, says he is developing a laptop PC that will go on sale for less than $100 (£53).  He told the BBC World Service programme Go Digital he h...
Summary: Nicholas Negroponte is developing a laptop PC that will be sold for less than $100, aiming to use it as an education tool in developing countries. The device will run a Linux-based operating system and be exported as a kit of parts to be assembled locally. Negroponte believes the laptops can become more common than mobile phones.

Title: Technology gets the creative bug
Article_Text: The hi-tech and the arts worlds have for some time danced around each other and offered creative and technical help when required.  Often this help has come in the form of corporate art sponsorship or...
Summary: BT has launched its Connected World initiative to shape a 21st Century model that combines art, technology, and business. The initiative aims to understand the creative industry's potential in broadband technology and create immersive art installations using BT's technology. The partnership between artists and technologists is part of trying to understand the creative potential of technologies like broadband net.

Title: Wi-fi web reaches farmers in Peru
Article_Text: A network of community computer centres, linked by wireless technology, is providing a helping hand for poor farmers in Peru.  The pilot scheme in the Huaral Valley, 80 kilometres north of the capital...
Summary: A network of community computer centres in Peru is providing poor farmers with access to information on agricultural market prices and trends, as well as training on computers and internet skills. The project, led by the non-government organisation Cepes, aims to make the network self-sustainable within three years. The network has been three years in the making and was officially inaugurated in September.

Title: Microsoft releases bumper patches
Article_Text: Microsoft has warned PC users to update their systems with the latest security fixes for flaws in Windows programs.  In its monthly security bulletin, it flagged up eight "critical" security holes whi...
Summary: Microsoft has warned PC users to update their systems with the latest security fixes for flaws in Windows programs, including Internet Explorer, media player, and instant messaging. The company has released eight critical security patches and four other important fixes. If not updated, users may be vulnerable to viruses or malicious attacks.

Title: Virus poses as Christmas e-mail
Article_Text: Security firms are warning about a Windows virus disguising itself as an electronic Christmas card.  The Zafi.D virus translates the Christmas greeting on its subject line into the language of the per...
Summary: Security firms warn about a Windows virus disguising itself as an electronic Christmas card, spreading widely online due to its multilingual ability. The virus, Zafi.D, infects Microsoft Outlook and sends itself to new victims via email attachments. It disables anti-virus and firewall software, and opens a backdoor on infected machines.

Title: Apple laptop is 'greatest gadget'
Article_Text: The Apple Powerbook 100 has been chosen as the greatest gadget of all time, by US magazine Mobile PC.  The 1991 laptop was chosen because it was one of the first "lightweight" portable computers and h...
Summary: The Apple Powerbook 100 has been chosen as the greatest gadget of all time by US magazine Mobile PC, due to its innovative design and impact on the development of future notebook PCs. The magazine compiled an all-time top 100 list of gadgets, which includes devices such as the Sony Walkman and the 1956 Zenith remote control. The list was compiled based on the inclusion of gadgets that were "self-contained apparatus that can be used on its own" and had moving parts and/or electronics.

Title: Google's toolbar sparks concern
Article_Text: Search engine firm Google has released a trial tool which is concerning some net users because it directs people to pre-selected commercial websites.  The AutoLink feature comes with Google's latest t...
Summary: Google has released a trial tool called AutoLink that directs users to pre-selected commercial websites based on information contained in webpages. The feature is available only in the US and has raised concerns about Google's dominant position in the search engine market. Google says the feature is still in beta and users can choose to disable it.

Title: UK net users leading TV downloads
Article_Text: British TV viewers lead the trend of illegally downloading US shows from the net, according to research.  New episodes of 24, Desperate Housewives and Six Feet Under, appear on the web hours after the...
Summary: British TV viewers are leading the trend of illegally downloading US shows from the internet, with 18% of downloaders coming from within the UK. Downloads of TV programmes have increased by 150% in the last year, with 70% using file-sharing program BitTorrent. The internet is making it easy for people to watch TV shows before they are shown in the UK.

Title: IBM puts cash behind Linux push
Article_Text: IBM is spending $100m (£52m) over the next three years beefing up its commitment to Linux software.  The cash injection will be used to help its customers use Linux on every type of device from handhe...
Summary: IBM is investing $100m over three years to boost its commitment to Linux software, responding to customer demand for the open source software. The investment will fund technical, research, and marketing initiatives to increase Linux use across various devices. This move builds on IBM's existing efforts to promote Linux, which began in 2001.

Title: UK pioneers digital film network
Article_Text: The world's first digital cinema network will be established in the UK over the next 18 months.  The UK Film Council has awarded a contract worth £11.5m to Arts Alliance Digital Cinema (AADC), who wil...
Summary: The UK Film Council has awarded a contract to Arts Alliance Digital Cinema to establish the world's first digital cinema network, which will be set up over the next 18 months. The network will have up to 250 screens and will show mainly British and specialist films. The digital network will improve access to films across the UK.

Title: EU software patent law faces axe
Article_Text: The European Parliament has thrown out a bill that would have allowed software to be patented.  Politicians unanimously rejected the bill and now it must go through another round of consultation if it...
Summary: The European Parliament has rejected a bill that would have allowed software to be patented, sending it back for re-consultation. The bill was backed by some tech firms but opposed by others who said it could stifle innovation and be abused by firms to protect existing monopolies. The bill's progress was delayed twice and the European Legal Affairs Committee recommended re-drafting the law.

Title: Xbox power cable 'fire fear'
Article_Text: Microsoft has said it will replace more than 14 million power cables for its Xbox consoles due to safety concerns.  The company said the move was a "preventative step" after reports of fire hazard pro...
Summary: Microsoft is recalling over 14 million Xbox power cables due to safety concerns, with reports of fire hazard problems and minor injuries. The recall affects almost three quarters of all Xboxes sold worldwide since 2001. Consumers can order a free replacement cord from the Xbox website or by phone.

Title: Global blogger action day called
Article_Text: The global web blog community is being called into action to lend support to two imprisoned Iranian bloggers.  The month-old Committee to Protect Bloggers' is asking those with blogs to dedicate their...
Summary: The Committee to Protect Bloggers is calling on the global web blog community to support two imprisoned Iranian bloggers, Mojtaba Saminejad and Arash Sigarchi, on February 22. The group is asking bloggers to dedicate their sites to the cause and raise awareness about the plight of cyber-dissidents.

Title: Finding new homes for old phones
Article_Text: Re-using old mobile phones is not just good for the environment, it has social benefits too.  Research has found that in some developing nations old mobile phones can help close the digital divide. Th...
Summary: Research found that reusing old mobile phones can help close the digital divide in developing nations, with low-cost recycled handsets providing a useful second life. In the UK, only 25% of old phones are recycled or reused, contributing to a growing mass of unrecycled waste. The Forum for the Future report highlights the social benefits of reusing old phones, particularly in poorer nations where affordable mobile phones are in high demand.

Title: PlayStation 3 chip to be unveiled
Article_Text: Details of the chip designed to power Sony's PlayStation 3 console will be released in San Francisco on Monday.  Sony, IBM and Toshiba, who have been working on the Cell processor for three years, wil...
Summary: Details of the Cell processor chip designed for Sony's PlayStation 3 console will be released in San Francisco, showcasing its potential for faster processing and graphics capabilities.

Title: Intel unveils laser breakthrough
Article_Text: Intel has unveiled research that could mean data is soon being moved around chips at the speed of light.  Scientists at Intel have overcome a fundamental problem that before now has prevented silicon ...
Summary: Intel has overcome a fundamental problem to use silicon to generate and amplify laser light, which could enable faster data transfer between chips and fibre optic cables.

Title: Security scares spark browser fix
Article_Text: Microsoft is working on a new version of its Internet Explorer web browser.  The revamp has been prompted by Microsoft's growing concern with security as well as increased competition from rival brows...
Summary: Microsoft is revamping its Internet Explorer web browser due to growing security concerns and increased competition from rival browsers. The new version, IE 7, will include new protections against viruses, spyware, and phishing scams. Test versions are expected to be released by the summer.

Title: Britons fed up with net service
Article_Text: A survey conducted by PC Pro Magazine has revealed that many Britons are unhappy with their internet service.  They are fed up with slow speeds, high prices and the level of customer service they rece...
Summary: A survey by PC Pro Magazine found that many Britons are unhappy with their internet service due to slow speeds, high prices, and poor customer service. 17% of readers have switched suppliers, and 16% are considering changing in the near future. The survey highlights the competitive nature of broadband providers in the UK.

Title: Sun offers processing by the hour
Article_Text: Sun Microsystems has launched a pay-as-you-go service which will allow customers requiring huge computing power to rent it by the hour.  Sun Grid costs users $1 (53p) for an hour's worth of processing...
Summary: Sun Microsystems has launched a pay-as-you-go service called Sun Grid, allowing customers to rent computing power by the hour for $1. The system relies on Solaris and could mature like utilities, according to Sun's chief operating officer Jonathan Schwartz. The company has interest from customers in the oil, gas and financial services industries.

Title: Lasers help bridge network gaps
Article_Text: An Indian telecommunications firm has turned to lasers to help it overcome the problems of setting up voice and data networks in the country.  Tata Teleservices is using the lasers to make the link be...
Summary: Tata Teleservices is using lasers to set up voice and data networks in India, overcoming challenges of digging and laying cables. The laser bridges work across distances up to 4km and can be set up faster than cable connections. This has helped the firm expand its network to over 700 locations in 12 months.

Title: Game firm holds 'cast' auditions
Article_Text: Video game firm Bioware is to hold open auditions for people to become cast members for future games.  The company, which makes role playing games such as Knights of the Old Republic and Neverwinter N...
Summary: Bioware is holding open auditions for people to become cast members for future games, seeking individuals aged 18-99 with interesting faces to use as face models for characters.

Title: Sony PSP console hits US in March
Article_Text: US gamers will be able to buy Sony's PlayStation Portable from 24 March, but there is no news of a Europe debut.  The handheld console will go on sale for $250 (£132) and the first million sold will c...
Summary: US gamers will be able to buy Sony's PlayStation Portable starting March 24, with a price tag of $250 (£132). The console will come with Spider-Man 2 on UMD for the first million sold. Sony has sold over 800,000 units in Japan and is entering a market dominated by Nintendo.

Title: Warnings about junk mail deluge
Article_Text: The amount of spam circulating online could be about to undergo a massive increase, say experts.  Anti-spam group Spamhaus is warning about a novel virus which hides the origins of junk mail. The prog...
Summary: Experts warn of a potential increase in spam circulation due to a new virus that hides the origins of junk mail, making it harder to filter out. The virus routes junk mail through legitimate mail servers, potentially causing problems for email sending infrastructure. Experts disagree on the impact of the new technique, with some predicting it could lead to email meltdown and others saying it won't significantly affect spam filtering.

Title: Warning over tsunami aid website
Article_Text: Net users are being told to avoid a scam website that claims to collect cash on behalf of tsunami victims.  The site looks plausible because it uses an old version of the official Disasters Emergency ...
Summary: A scam website claiming to collect cash for tsunami victims has been identified, using a fake version of the Disasters Emergency Committee webpage. The site has been contacted by DEC and the police, and efforts are being made to shut it down. Similar scams have been circulating, including spam emails with poor grammar and attachments that spread malware.

Title: Piero gives rugby perspective
Article_Text: BBC Sport unveils its new analysis tool Piero at the Wales v England rugby union match on Saturday. But what does it do and how does it work?  Picture the scene - Wales are camped on the England line ...
Summary: BBC Sport has unveiled its new analysis tool Piero, which uses virtual stadium technology to track player movements and provide detailed analysis of sports broadcasts.

Title: Open source leaders slam patents
Article_Text: The war of words between Microsoft and the open source movement heated up this week as Linux founder Linus Torvalds led an attack on software patents.  In a panel discussion at a Linux summit in Calif...
Summary: Linux founder Linus Torvalds criticized software patents, while Mitchell Kapor warned that Microsoft could use patent lawsuits in the future. IBM has made 500 of its patents freely available, and some companies are expected to follow suit. Microsoft did not comment directly on the issue.

Title: Reboot ordered for EU patent law
Article_Text: A European Parliament committee has ordered a rewrite of the proposals for controversial new European Union rules which govern computer-based inventions.  The Legal Affairs Committee (JURI) said the C...
Summary: A European Parliament committee has ordered a rewrite of the Computer Implemented Inventions Directive, which aims to offer patent protection to inventions that use software to achieve their effect. The directive has faced criticism from small firms and open-source software innovators, who fear it could favour large firms. The EU's decision is seen as a chance to have fuller debates about the directive's implications.

Title: Solutions to net security fears
Article_Text: Fake bank e-mails, or phishing, and stories about ID theft are damaging the potential of using the net for online commerce, say e-business experts.  Trust in online security is falling as a result. Al...
Summary: A survey of over 1,000 people found that 43% are not willing to share personal information online due to concerns about online security. Security experts say that scare stories and vulnerabilities are being taken seriously by banks, and companies are working on improving security measures, such as one-time passcode generation services and biometric authentication.

Title: Mobile networks seek turbo boost
Article_Text: Third-generation mobile (3G) networks need to get faster if they are to deliver fast internet surfing on the move and exciting new services.  That was one of the messages from the mobile industry at t...
Summary: The mobile industry is shifting focus from current 3G networks to faster, higher bandwidth services. Companies like Siemens and Motorola are developing new technologies, such as High Speed Downlink Packet Access (HSDPA), to improve data speeds. HSDPA can transmit data at speeds of up to 14 megabits per second, more than double the capacity of current 3G networks.
Key_Entities: Fraunhofer German-Sino Lab for Mobile Communications
Institute for Applied Radio System Technology

Title: Global digital divide 'narrowing'
Article_Text: The "digital divide" between rich and poor nations is narrowing fast, according to a World Bank report.  The World Bank questioned a United Nation's campaign to increase usage and access to technology...
Summary: The World Bank report states that the digital divide between rich and poor nations is narrowing, with half the world's population having access to a fixed-line telephone and 77% to a mobile network. The report's figures surpass a UN campaign goal, and the UN hopes to use technology to eradicate poverty. A meeting of the WSIS agreed to create a Digital Solitary Fund to help narrow the divide.
Key_Entities: World Summit on the Information Society
World Summit for the Information Society

Title: UK gets official virus alert site
Article_Text: A rapid alerting service that tells home computer users about serious internet security problems is being launched by the UK government.  The service, IT Safe, will issue warnings about damaging virus...
Summary: The UK government is launching a rapid alerting service called IT Safe to inform home computer users about serious internet security problems. The service will issue warnings about damaging viruses, software vulnerabilities, and weaknesses on devices such as mobile phones. It will be free and available via email or text alerts.

Title: Iran jails blogger for 14 years
Article_Text: An Iranian weblogger has been jailed for 14 years on charges of spying and aiding foreign counter-revolutionaries.  Arash Sigarchi was arrested last month after using his blog to criticise the arrest ...
Summary: An Iranian weblogger, Arash Sigarchi, has been jailed for 14 years on charges of spying and aiding foreign counter-revolutionaries. The sentence was criticized by human rights watchdog Reporters Without Borders. Iranian authorities have recently clamped down on weblogs, restricting access to major blogging sites from within Iran.

Title: Microsoft seeking spyware trojan
Article_Text: Microsoft is investigating a trojan program that attempts to switch off the firm's anti-spyware software.  The spyware tool was only released by Microsoft in the last few weeks and has been downloaded...
Summary: Microsoft is investigating a Trojan program that attempts to disable its anti-spyware software, which has been downloaded by six million people. The program, called Bankash-A Trojan, may steal online banking passwords or personal information. Microsoft plans to offer its own paid-for anti-virus software.

Title: US woman sues over cartridges
Article_Text: A US woman is suing Hewlett Packard (HP), saying its printer ink cartridges are secretly programmed to expire on a certain date.  The unnamed woman from Georgia says that a chip inside the cartridge t...
Summary: A US woman is suing Hewlett Packard, alleging its printer ink cartridges are programmed to expire prematurely, while HP has declined to comment on the lawsuit. The lawsuit seeks to represent anyone in the US who purchased an HP inkjet printer since February 2001. The cost of printer cartridges has been a contentious issue in Europe.

Title: Movie body hits peer-to-peer nets
Article_Text: The movie industry has struck out at file-sharing networks with another round of lawsuits in the US.  The Motion Picture Association of America (MPAA) also said it had succeeded in getting a network c...
Summary: The MPAA has filed lawsuits against file-sharing networks using BitTorrent, including LokiTorrent, and given operators of eDonkey servers 'take down' notices. The MPAA aims to stunt file-sharers' ability to swap content using BitTorrent systems. The film industry claims illegal file-sharing costs them billions every year.

Title: Security warning over 'FBI virus'
Article_Text: The US Federal Bureau of Investigation is warning that a computer virus is being spread via e-mails that purport to be from the FBI.  The e-mails show that they have come from an fbi.gov address and t...
Summary: The FBI is warning about a computer virus being spread via e-mails that appear to be from the FBI, and is investigating the incident.

Title: Apple iPod family expands market
Article_Text: Apple has expanded its iPod family with the release of its next generation of the digital music players.  Its latest challenges to the growing digital music gadget market include an iPod mini model wh...
Summary: Apple has released its next generation of iPods with improved storage capacity, longer battery life, and lower prices. The company aims to maintain its dominant position in the digital music market. Analysts expect increased competition from mobile phone operators offering streaming services.
Key_Entities: Pew Internet and American Life Project

Title: T-Mobile bets on 'pocket office'
Article_Text: T-Mobile has launched its latest "pocket office" third-generation (3G) device which also has built-in wi-fi - high-speed wireless net access.  Unlike other devices where the user has to check which hi...
Summary: T-Mobile has launched its latest 3G device with built-in Wi-Fi, allowing users to access high-speed wireless networks automatically. The device features a swivelled display and a Qwerty keyboard, and is part of the company's push for 'Office in a Pocket' devices. T-Mobile also announced plans to expand its Wi-Fi hotspots and introduce a new tariff for UK customers.

Title: Hotspot users gain free net calls
Article_Text: People using wireless net hotspots will soon be able to make free phone calls as well as surf the net.  Wireless provider Broadreach and net telephony firm Skype are rolling out a service at 350 hotsp...
Summary: Wireless provider Broadreach and net telephony firm Skype are launching a service allowing users to make free phone calls and surf the net via wi-fi at 350 hotspots around the UK. The service requires a Skype account and will also allow users to make calls to landlines and mobiles for a fee. Skype has 28 million users worldwide.

Title: DVD copy protection strengthened
Article_Text: DVDs will be harder to copy thanks to new anti-piracy measures devised by copy protection firm Macrovision.  The pirated DVD market is enormous because current copy protection was hacked more than fiv...
Summary: Macrovision has introduced RipGuard technology to thwart DVD ripping and supply chain theft, with the goal of reducing piracy and increasing revenue from DVD sales. The new technology will be applied to DVDs starting in the middle of 2005. Macrovision aims to evolve RipGuard beyond anti-piracy to enable legitimate online transactions and interoperability.

Title: Apple attacked over sources row
Article_Text: Civil liberties group the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) has joined a legal fight between three US online journalists and Apple.  Apple wants the reporters to reveal 20 sources used for stories ...
Summary: The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) is representing three US online journalists in a legal fight against Apple, which is seeking to reveal the sources of leaked information about forthcoming products. The EFF argues that the journalists are protected by the American constitution and that the case threatens the basic freedoms of the press. The case will examine whether online journalists have the same privileges and protections as those writing for newspapers and magazines.

Title: Sony PSP tipped as a 'must-have'
Article_Text: Sony's Playstation Portable is the top gadget for 2005, according to a round-up of ultimate gizmos compiled by Stuff Magazine.  It beats the iPod into second place in the Top Ten Essentials list which...
Summary: The Sony Playstation Portable is the top gadget for 2005, according to Stuff Magazine's Top Ten Essentials list, beating the iPod into second place. Owning all 10 gadgets will cost £7,455. The list predicts that portable gadgets will dominate 2006, with the Xbox 2, high-definition TV, and MP3 mobiles among the must-haves.

Title: BBC leads interactive Bafta wins
Article_Text: The BBC and the National Theatre have led the field at this year's Interactive Bafta awards.  The National Theatre's Stagework website picked up the prize for best learning as well as top factual site...
Summary: The BBC and the National Theatre won top awards at the Interactive Bafta awards, including best learning and top factual site. The BBC also won awards for its online entertainment and news and sport coverage. The awards recognize the best in digital media.

Title: Millions buy MP3 players in US
Article_Text: One in 10 adult Americans - equivalent to 22 million people - owns an MP3 player, according to a survey.  A study by the Pew Internet and American Life Project found that MP3 players are the gadget of...
Summary: A survey by the Pew Internet and American Life Project found that 22 million Americans own MP3 players, with 59% of owners being men and 41% women. The survey also found that MP3 players are more common among affluent young Americans and those with broadband access. The ease of use and growth of music available on the net are the main factors for the upsurge in ownership.
Key_Entities: Pew Internet and American Life Project

Title: 'No re-draft' for EU patent law
Article_Text: A proposed European law on software patents will not be re-drafted by the European Commission (EC) despite requests by MEPs.  The law is proving controversial and has been in limbo for a year. Some ma...
Summary: A proposed European law on software patents will not be re-drafted by the European Commission despite requests by MEPs, who fear it could hurt smaller tech firms. The law aims to offer patent protection to inventions that use software to achieve their effect. The Commission has supported the agreement reached by ministers in May 2004, but will review all aspects of the directive.

Title: Domain system scam fear
Article_Text: A system to make it easier to create website addresses using alphabets like Cyrillic could open a back door for scammers, a trade body has warned.  The Internationalised Domain Names system has been a...
Summary: A new system for creating website addresses using alphabets like Cyrillic could make it easier for scammers to create fake sites, a trade body has warned. The system, approved by the Internet Electronic Task Force, uses a hybrid of ASCII and Unicode codes, which could be used to create fake domains that look identical to legitimate sites. A fake PayPal domain has already been registered and handed back to the company.
Key_Entities: Council of European National Top Level Domain Registries

Title: Cheaper chip for mobiles
Article_Text: A mobile phone chip which combines a modem and a computer processor on one bit of silicon instead of two could make phones cheaper and more powerful.  The specially-designed chip, developed by Texas I...
Summary: A new mobile phone chip, OMAP-Vox, developed by Texas Instruments, combines a modem and a computer processor on one chip, making phones cheaper and more powerful. The technology is being tested and could appear by the end of the year. The chip uses less power than conventional chips, making it suitable for 3D gaming and 30-frame-a-second video.

Title: Blind student 'hears in colour'
Article_Text: A blind student has developed software that turns colours into musical notes so that he can read weather maps.  Victor Wong, a graduate student from Hong Kong studying at Cornell University in New Yor...
Summary: A blind student, Victor Wong, has developed software that translates colors into musical notes, allowing him to read weather maps and study space weather. The software assigns piano notes to individual pixels based on their color, with red corresponding to the highest note. The technology is still in its infancy and requires further development to be commercially viable.

Title: Xbox 2 may be unveiled in summer
Article_Text: Details of the next generation of Microsoft's Xbox games console - codenamed Xenon - will most likely be unveiled in May, according to reports.  It was widely expected that gamers would get a sneak pr...
Summary: Details of Microsoft's next-generation Xbox console, codenamed Xenon, are expected to be unveiled in May, possibly at the Electronic Entertainment Expo (E3) in Los Angeles. The console is expected to be released at the end of the year, with Sony and Nintendo also planning to release their own consoles in the next 18 months. The new console will have more processing and graphical power, as well as additional features.

Title: Microsoft launches its own search
Article_Text: Microsoft has unveiled the finished version of its home-grown search engine.  The now formally launched MSN search site takes the training wheels off the test version unveiled in November 2003. The re...
Summary: Microsoft has launched its revamped MSN search engine, which indexes more pages than before and can give direct answers to factual questions. The engine faces challenges competing with Google, but Microsoft aims to make it a significant rival. The search engine can also answer specific queries directly and features tools to refine results.

Title: Moving mobile improves golf swing
Article_Text: A mobile phone that recognises and responds to movements has been launched in Japan.  The motion-sensitive phone - officially titled the V603SH - was developed by Sharp and launched by Vodafone's Japa...
Summary: A motion-sensitive mobile phone has been launched in Japan by Sharp and Vodafone's Japanese division, featuring a tiny motion-control sensor and a display screen that can rotate 180 degrees. The phone is designed for mobile gaming and other activities, and will be available in Japan starting in mid-February. It has also been compared to a sports-leisure gadget used by fishing enthusiasts in South Korea.

Title: Junk e-mails on relentless rise
Article_Text: Spam traffic is up by 40%, putting the total amount of e-mail that is junk up to an astonishing 90%.  The figures, from e-mail management firm Email Systems, will alarm firms attempting to cope with t...
Summary: Spam traffic has increased by 40% to 90% of total email traffic, with virus traffic slowing down and denial of service attacks on the rise. Email Systems, a UK-based firm, received 12 million emails in January. The type of spam has shifted to health-related and pornographic offers.

Title: Sporting rivals go to extra time
Article_Text: The current slew of sports games offers unparalleled opportunities for fans who like to emulate on-field action without ever moving from the couch.  The two giants in the field - ESPN and EA Sports - ...
Summary: ESPN sold EA the rights to its TV branding and on-air talent, changing the future of ESPN games, which may lead to EA's monopolization of the sports gaming landscape.

Title: Half-Life 2 sweeps Bafta awards
Article_Text: PC first person shooter Half-Life 2 has won six Bafta Awards, including best game and best online game.  The title, developed by Valve, was released last year to universal acclaim - receiving special ...
Summary: Half-Life 2 won six Bafta Awards, including best game and best online game, at a ceremony in London on Tuesday. The game, developed by Valve, received praise for its immersive plot and physics engine, while other winners included Burnout 3, Halo 2, and Prince of Persia: Warrior Within. The Bafta Games Awards recognized the diversity and progress of the interactive entertainment industry, with a notable increase in non-traditional games and awards for handheld and mobile titles.

Title: BT boosts its broadband packages
Article_Text: British Telecom has said it will double the broadband speeds of most of its home and business customers.  The increased speeds will come at no extra charge and follows a similar move by internet servi...
Summary: British Telecom will double broadband speeds for most customers, starting with 2Mbps download speeds, with no extra charge, and will begin enforcing usage allowances in the summer. The new speeds will start on 17 February for home customers and 1 April for businesses. BT's managing director, Duncan Ingram, said the increases will give customers more opportunities with their broadband connections.

Title: Mobiles 'not media players yet'
Article_Text: Mobiles are not yet ready to be all-singing, all-dancing multimedia devices which will replace portable media players, say two reports.  Despite moves to bring music download services to mobiles, peop...
Summary: Mobiles are not yet ready to support multimedia services due to size and battery life limitations, according to reports by Jupiter and Gartner. Technical issues and standards must be resolved before real-time TV broadcasts can be offered to mobiles in Europe until 2007. The mobile industry is keen to get into music downloading, but limited storage and other issues must be addressed.

Title: Microsoft releases patches
Article_Text: Microsoft has warned PC users to update their systems with the latest security fixes for flaws in Windows programs.  In its monthly security bulletin, it flagged up eight "critical" security holes whi...
Summary: Microsoft has warned PC users to update their systems with the latest security fixes for flaws in Windows programs, including Internet Explorer, media player, and instant messaging. The company has released eight critical security patches and four other important fixes. If not updated, users may be vulnerable to viruses or malicious attacks.

Title: Concern over RFID tags
Article_Text: Consumers are very concerned about the use of radio frequency ID (RFID) tags in shops, a survey says.  More than half of 2,000 people surveyed said they had privacy worries about the tags, which can b...
Summary: A survey by Capgemini found that over half of consumers are concerned about the use of RFID tags in shops, citing privacy worries. The tags are used to monitor stock and can potentially be used to track consumers. Retailers need to educate consumers about RFID to gain acceptance.
Key_Entities: Consumers Against Supermarket Privacy Invasion and Numbering

Title: Ask Jeeves joins web log market
Article_Text: Ask Jeeves has bought the Bloglines website to improve the way it handles content from web journals or blogs.  The Bloglines site has become hugely popular as it gives users one place in which to read...
Summary: Ask Jeeves has acquired Bloglines to improve its content handling and utilize its 300 million archived articles to enhance its web index. The acquisition aims to help users find information rather than write it. No immediate changes are planned for Bloglines.

Title: Digital guru floats sub-$100 PC
Article_Text: Nicholas Negroponte, chairman and founder of MIT's Media Labs, says he is developing a laptop PC that will go on sale for less than $100 (£53).  He told the BBC World Service programme Go Digital he h...
Summary: Nicholas Negroponte is developing a laptop PC that will be sold for less than $100, aiming to use it as an education tool in developing countries. The device will run a Linux-based operating system and be exported as a kit of parts to be assembled locally. Negroponte believes the laptops can become more common than mobile phones.

Title: Looks and music to drive mobiles
Article_Text: Mobile phones are still enjoying a boom time in sales, according to research from technology analysts Gartner.  More than 674 million mobiles were sold last year globally, said the report, the highest...
Summary: Mobile phone sales reached a record high of 674 million globally last year, surpassing predictions and driven by good design and new services like music downloads. However, some markets are seeing a slowdown in replacement sales, and mobile companies must offer compelling reasons to upgrade. Third generation mobiles and music services are expected to drive sales in 2005.
Key_Entities: Motorola four gigabyte storage capacity music players

Title: Yahoo celebrates a decade online
Article_Text: Yahoo, one of the net's most iconic companies, is celebrating its 10th anniversary this week.  The web portal has undergone remarkable change since it was set up by Stanford University students David ...
Summary: Yahoo is celebrating its 10th anniversary, having undergone significant changes since its founding by Stanford University students David Filo and Jerry Yang in 1994. The company has grown from a small venture to a large employer with 7,600 workers. Yahoo faces intense rivalry from other internet firms.

Title: Kenyan school turns to handhelds
Article_Text: At the Mbita Point primary school in western Kenya students click away at a handheld computer with a stylus.  They are doing exercises in their school textbooks which have been digitised. It is a pilo...
Summary: EduVision is piloting a project to digitize school textbooks using low-cost computer systems and satellite radio, aiming to increase access to knowledge in rural developing countries.

Title: Tough rules for ringtone sellers
Article_Text: Firms that flout rules on how ringtones and other mobile extras are sold could be cut off from all UK phone networks.  The rules allow offenders to be cut off if they do not let consumers know exactly...
Summary: Firms that sell mobile extras without transparently disclosing their services and terms may be cut off from UK phone networks. The new rules aim to protect consumers from potential harm. The first month under the new regime has seen at least ten firms suspended.

Title: Creator of first Apple Mac dies
Article_Text: Jef Raskin, head of the team behind the first Macintosh computer, has died.  Mr Raskin was one of the first employees at Apple and made many of the design decisions that made the Mac so distinctive wh...
Summary: Jef Raskin, the head of the team behind the first Macintosh computer, has died at the age of unknown. He was a key figure in the design of the Macintosh computer, which was released in 1984 and introduced a graphical interface and mouse. The Macintosh was a pioneering computer that made computers easy to use.

Title: 'Friends fear' with lost mobiles
Article_Text: People are becoming so dependent on their mobile phones that one in three are concerned that losing their phone would mean they lose their friends.  More than 50% of mobile owners reported they had ha...
Summary: A survey found that over 50% of mobile owners have had their phone stolen or lost in the last three years, and many rely on their phones as address books. Mobile operators offer various back-up services, including web-based and Sim back-up devices. The survey also highlighted the growing dependence on mobile phones in modern relationships.

Title: Telewest to challenge Sky Plus
Article_Text: Cable firm Telewest is to offer a personal video recorder (PVR) in a set -top box to challenge Sky Plus.  Sky Plus is the market leader in the field of digital video recorders in the UK, with 474,000 ...
Summary: Telewest is set to launch a personal video recorder (PVR) in a set-top box to challenge Sky Plus, the market leader in digital video recorders in the UK. The PVR will offer a 160GB hard drive and three tuners, allowing viewers to record multiple channels simultaneously. Sky Plus boxes come in two versions, with prices starting at £99 for a 20GB version.

Title: Games enter the classroom
Article_Text: Video games could soon be transplanted from their natural habitat to the more academic atmosphere of the classroom.  With violent titles continuing to top the charts, gaming and learning have not alwa...
Summary: Research by the London Institute of Education suggests that video games can have a valid place in the classroom, teaching life skills such as decision making and problem solving. A game called Racing Academy is being used to test the viability of using gaming in the classroom, requiring players to understand physics and engineering to win races. The game has been trialled in two secondary schools in Bristol and feedback from students has been positive.

Title: Gadget growth fuels eco concerns
Article_Text: Technology firms and gadget lovers are being urged to think more about the environment when buying and disposing of the latest hi-tech products.  At the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas earlier ...
Summary: Technology firms and gadget lovers are being urged to think more about the environment when buying and disposing of the latest hi-tech products. Several hi-tech firms were recognised for their strategies to help the environment, and Ebay announced the Rethink project to promote recycling. The US consumer electronics market is set to grow by over 11% in 2005, but more awareness is needed about how and where old gadgets can be recycled.

Title: 'Evil twin' fear for wireless net
Article_Text: People using wireless high-speed net (wi-fi) are being warned about fake hotspots, or access points.  The latest threat, nicknamed evil twins, pose as real hotspots but are actually unauthorised base ...
Summary: People using wireless high-speed net are being warned about fake hotspots, or access points, known as evil twins, which can intercept sensitive data. Wi-fi is becoming increasingly popular, with over 1,000 hotspots in London and expected to reach 200,000 by 2008. Experts advise users to activate security measures and use personal firewalls to protect themselves.

Title: China 'to overtake US net use'
Article_Text: The Chinese net-using population looks set to exceed that of the US in less than three years, says a report.  China's net users number 100m but this represents less than 8% of the country's 1.3 billio...
Summary: China's net users are expected to surpass the US in less than three years, with a growing population using the internet for different purposes than in Western nations. The report highlights the unique characteristics of internet use in China, including the prevalence of net cafes and limited use of credit cards. The internet is seen as a valuable source of information and a symbol of social status.

Title: US peer-to-peer pirates convicted
Article_Text: The first convictions for piracy over peer-to-peer networks have been handed down in the US.  New Yorker William Trowbridge and Texan Michael Chicoine have pleaded guilty to charges that they infringe...
Summary: Two US men, William Trowbridge and Michael Chicoine, have pleaded guilty to piracy charges related to peer-to-peer networks, facing up to five years in jail and a $250,000 fine. The charges stem from their involvement in the Underground Network, a piracy community that shared copyrighted files. The US Department of Justice has announced the guilty pleas and scheduled sentencing for April 29.

Title: Google launches TV search service
Article_Text: The net search giant Google has launched a search service that lets people look for TV programmes.  The service, Google Video beta, searches closed caption information that comes with programmes. It o...
Summary: Google has launched Google Video beta, a search service that lets people look for TV programmes using closed caption information. The service currently only searches US channel content, but plans to expand to include more channels over time. The results include programme and episode information, as well as links to watch the programme locally.

Title: Rich pickings for hi-tech thieves
Article_Text: Viruses, trojans and other malicious programs sent on to the net to catch you out are undergoing a subtle change.  The shift is happening as tech savvy criminals turn to technology to help them con pe...
Summary: Criminals are shifting from spreading viruses to using malware for direct criminal ends, with firms tightening up networks to combat the new wave of malicious code.

Title: Blog reading explodes in America
Article_Text: Americans are becoming avid blog readers, with 32 million getting hooked in 2004, according to new research.  The survey, conducted by the Pew Internet and American Life Project, showed that blog read...
Summary: A survey by the Pew Internet and American Life Project found that 32 million Americans became avid blog readers in 2004, with a 58% increase in readership over the last year. Blogs have become a source of immediate news and information, with 6 million Americans using RSS aggregators. Reading blogs remains more popular than writing them.

Title: Software watching while you work
Article_Text: Software that can not only monitor every keystroke and action performed at a PC but also be used as legally binding evidence of wrong-doing has been unveiled.  Worries about cyber-crime and sabotage h...
Summary: A new software system has been unveiled that can monitor employee activity and store data for legal use, amid concerns over cyber-crime and employee privacy.

Title: New delay hits EU software laws
Article_Text: A fresh delay has hit controversial new European Union rules which govern computer-based inventions.  The draft law was not adopted by EU ministers as planned at a Brussels meeting on Monday during wh...
Summary: The European Union's draft law on computer-based inventions has been delayed after Polish officials expressed concerns for the second time in two months, citing potential favoritism towards large companies and impact on open-source software innovation. The law, which aims to align with US patent laws, has sparked debate among critics and supporters, with Poland's backing crucial to its adoption. The EU has not set a new date for discussion of the law, leaving its future uncertain.

Title: Savvy searchers fail to spot ads
Article_Text: Internet search engine users are an odd mix of naive and sophisticated, suggests a report into search habits.  The report by the US Pew Research Center reveals that 87% of searchers usually find what ...
Summary: A report by the US Pew Research Center found that 87% of searchers usually find what they were looking for, but few can spot the difference between paid-for and organic results. Most users trust search engines, but would stop using them if they knew information about paid results was being hidden.

Title: Games firms 'face tough future'
Article_Text: UK video game firms face a testing time as they prepare for the next round of games consoles, the industry warns.  Fred Hasson, head of Tiga, which represents independent developers, said that more UK...
Summary: UK video game firms are preparing for the release of new consoles, which will increase development costs and demands, potentially leading to more closures and a need for developers to adapt to new tools and business practices.

Title: Microsoft makes anti-piracy move
Article_Text: Microsoft says it is clamping down on people running pirated versions of its Windows operating system by restricting their access to security features.  The Windows Genuine Advantage scheme means peop...
Summary: Microsoft is restricting access to security features for people running pirated versions of its Windows operating system, requiring them to prove their software is genuine starting from mid-2005. While they will still receive some security fixes via automatic updates, their options will be limited. This move aims to tackle security threats while cracking down on pirated software.

Title: Nintendo handheld given Euro date
Article_Text: Nintendo's new handheld console, the DS, will launch in Europe on 11 March, the company has announced.  The portable games machine, which features touch-screen control, will retail for £99 in the UK (...
Summary: Nintendo's new handheld console, the DS, will launch in Europe on 11 March, featuring touch-screen control and 15 games available at launch. The console will retail for £99 in the UK and is expected to compete with Sony's PSP. Nintendo has sold over 2.8 million DS consoles worldwide since its release in 2004.

Title: Smart search lets art fans browse
Article_Text: If you don't know art but know what you like, new search technology could prove a useful gateway to painting.  ArtGarden, developed by BT's research unit, is being tested by the Tate as a new way of b...
Summary: ArtGarden, a new search technology, is being tested by the Tate to provide a more intuitive way of browsing its online collection of paintings. The technology uses artificial intelligence and random selection to show users a selection of pictures, allowing them to discover new works. The Tate aims to make its art more accessible with this technology.

Title: Warning over Windows Word files
Article_Text: Writing a Microsoft Word document can be a dangerous business, according to document security firm Workshare.  Up to 75% of all business documents contained sensitive information most firms would not ...
Summary: A survey by Workshare found that up to 75% of business documents contain sensitive information, with 90% of companies unaware of confidential leaks. Microsoft Word's editing history can lead to sensitive information being preserved. The company recommends using the Remove Hidden Data add-in to fix the issue.

Title: Net regulation 'still possible'
Article_Text: The blurring of boundaries between TV and the internet raises questions of regulation, watchdog Ofcom has said.  Content on TV and the internet is set to move closer this year as TV-quality video onli...
Summary: Ofcom has raised questions about regulation of TV and internet content as boundaries between the two blur. The watchdog is considering adopting rules to regulate TV content or self-regulation. Internet service providers and media companies are streaming video content on the web, raising concerns about responsibility and regulation.

Title: Voters flock to blog awards site
Article_Text: Voting is under way for the annual Bloggies which recognise the best web blogs - online spaces where people publish their thoughts - of the year.  Nominations were announced on Sunday, but traffic to ...
Summary: The Bloggies, an annual award recognizing the best web blogs, is currently underway with voting open in 30 categories. The awards, which were first held in 2000, have seen a surge in nominations, with over 12,000 new blogs added daily, according to Technorati. The winners will be chosen by public voting, which closes on February 3, and the awards will be announced between March 13 and 15.

Title: Latest Opera browser gets vocal
Article_Text: Net browser Opera 8.0, due for official release at the end of next month, will be "the most accessible browser on the market", according to its authors.  The latest version of the net browser can be c...
Summary: Opera 8.0 browser is set to be released with voice command and reading features, aiming to provide a more accessible internet experience. The browser can magnify text and create custom style sheets. However, its accessibility features may not be suitable for blind users due to compatibility issues with screen reader software.

Title: Web radio takes Spanish rap global
Article_Text: Spin the radio dial in the US and you are likely to find plenty of Spanish-language music. But what you will not find is much Spanish-language hip-hop.  Hip-hop and rap are actually quite popular in t...
Summary: A US company is launching a website to bring Spanish-language hip-hop and rap to global audiences, making it easier for fans to access music from Latin American artists.

Title: Movie body targets children's PCs
Article_Text: The body that represents the US movie industry has released its latest tool in its campaign to clamp down on movie file-sharing, aimed at parents.  The Movie Association for America's (MPAA) free Pare...
Summary: The MPAA has released a new tool to help parents detect and remove peer-to-peer programs and copyrighted files from their children's computers. The software, called Parent File Scan, identifies and lists files, but some users have reported false positives. The MPAA aims to combat movie piracy, which cost the industry £3.7bn in 2003.

Title: Norway upholds 'Napster' ruling
Article_Text: A Norwegian student who ran a website which linked to downloadable MP3 files has been ordered to pay compensation by the country's Supreme Court.  Frank Allan Bruvik was ordered to pay 100,000 kroner ...
Summary: A Norwegian student, Frank Allan Bruvik, has been ordered to pay 100,000 kroner to the music industry for copyright violation after his website allowed users to submit and receive links to MP3 files. The ruling was upheld by the Supreme Court, which stated that Bruvik's actions were premeditated. The case is seen as an important test of principle for the music industry.

Title: The future in your pocket
Article_Text: If you are a geek or gadget fan, the next 12 months look like they are going to be a lot of fun.  The relentless pace of development in the hi-tech world and rampant competition in many of its sectors...
Summary: 2005 is expected to be a significant year for mobile phones, with the launch of 3G networks and the introduction of new technologies such as WiMax and Voice over IP (Voip). These advancements will bring faster data transmission speeds, multimedia capabilities, and increased competition among operators. Meanwhile, the convergence of mobile and fixed phones, and the rise of portable media players, will continue to shape the tech industry.

Title: What high-definition will do to DVDs
Article_Text: First it was the humble home video, then it was the DVD, and now Hollywood is preparing for the next revolution in home entertainment - high-definition.  High-definition gives incredible, 3D-like pict...
Summary: High-definition technology is set to revolutionize home entertainment with its 3D-like pictures and surround sound. The technology is still being developed, but it will change the way films are produced and consumed. High-definition DVDs can hold up to six times more data than current DVDs, making it possible to show films in their original form without compression.

Title: Mobile games come of age
Article_Text: The BBC News website takes a look at how games on mobile phones are maturing. A brief round-up follows but you can skip straight to the reviews by clicking on the links below.  If you think of Snake w...
Summary: Mobile games have matured significantly over the past year, with a wide range of titles available for download, including ports of PC and arcade classics, and novel games exclusive to handsets. The ease of access and growing capabilities of mobile phones have contributed to the success of mobile games, with many titles now featuring 3D graphics and online multiplayer capabilities.

Title: California sets fines for spyware
Article_Text: The makers of computer programs that secretly spy on what people do with their home PCs could face hefty fines in California.  From 1 January, a new law is being introduced to protect computer users f...
Summary: A new law in California aims to protect computer users from spyware, a type of software that secretly spies on users' activities. The law, approved by Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger, bans the installation of software that takes control of another computer and requires companies to disclose whether their systems will install spyware. Consumers can seek up to $1,000 in damages if they think they have fallen victim to spyware.

Title: Web helps collect aid donations
Article_Text: The web is helping aid agencies gather resources to help cope with the aftermath of the tsunami disaster.  Many people are making donations via websites or going online to see how they can get involve...
Summary: The web is helping aid agencies gather resources to cope with the aftermath of the tsunami disaster by collecting donations via websites and online platforms. High-profile web portals are gathering links to aid and relief organisations, while some companies are modifying their homepages to include links to aid agencies. The Disasters Emergency Committee has received almost £8 million in donations.

Title: Mobiles rack up 20 years of use
Article_Text: Mobile phones in the UK are celebrating their 20th anniversary this weekend.  Britain's first mobile phone call was made across the Vodafone network on 1 January 1985 by veteran comedian Ernie Wise. I...
Summary: Mobile phones in the UK are celebrating their 20th anniversary, with the first call made in 1985. The industry has come a long way, with mobile phones becoming an integral part of modern life and now almost 90% of Britons owning a handset. The first commercial mobile service was launched in 1985, and digital technology has since introduced features such as text messaging and roaming.

Title: Blogs take on the mainstream
Article_Text: Web logs or blogs are everywhere, with at least an estimated five million on the web and that number is set to grow.  These online diaries come in many shapes and styles, ranging from people willing t...
Summary: The number of blogs on the web is estimated to be around five million, with the number growing exponentially. Blogs have become an important source of information, offering a critical eye on news events and providing an avenue for people to have a say in politics. The blogging movement has been building up for years, with experts arguing that it is here to stay.

Title: Honour for UK games maker
Article_Text: Leading British computer games maker Peter Molyneux has been made an OBE in the New Year Honours list.  The head of Surrey's Lionhead Studios was granted the honour for services to the computer games ...
Summary: Peter Molyneux, the head of Lionhead Studios, has been awarded an OBE for his services to the computer games industry. He is credited with helping to create and popularise the god-game genre. Molyneux has been a pivotal figure in the industry for almost 20 years.

Title: Bush website blocked outside US
Article_Text: Surfers outside the US have been unable to visit the official re-election site of President George W Bush.  The blocking of browsers sited outside the US began in the early hours of Monday morning. Si...
Summary: The official re-election site of President George W Bush has been blocked for international visitors, with attempts to view the site from outside the US resulting in an 'authorisation' error message. The blocking appears to be a policy decision rather than a result of a hacking attack. The site can still be accessed using anonymous proxy services in the US.

Title: Blogger grounded by her airline
Article_Text: A US airline attendant is fighting for her job after she was suspended over postings on her blog, or online diary.  Queen of the Sky, otherwise known as Ellen Simonetti, evolved into an anonymous semi...
Summary: A US airline attendant, Ellen Simonetti, was suspended by Delta Airlines after posting pictures of herself in uniform on her blog, leading to concerns about conflicts of interest, employment law, and free speech.

Title: Camera phones are 'must-haves'
Article_Text: Four times more mobiles with cameras in them will be sold in Europe by the end of 2004 than last year, says a report from analysts Gartner.  Globally, the number sold will reach 159 million, an increa...
Summary: Gartner predicts that nearly 70% of all mobile phones sold will have a built-in camera by 2008, with image quality improving over the next few years. Camera phones are becoming increasingly popular, with many manufacturers introducing design features and improvements to make them easier to use. The technology is also being used in the art world, with an upcoming exhibition featuring images taken from camera phones.

Title: Games 'deserve a place in class'
Article_Text: Computer games could enhance learning and have a legitimate place in the classroom, say researchers.  Academics from the Institute of Education at London University found that "games literacy" was a k...
Summary: Researchers from the Institute of Education at London University found that computer games can enhance learning and have a legitimate place in the classroom. Games literacy is a key skill for youngsters, and games can be used in different areas of the curriculum and as a legitimate area of study. The researchers also found that girls are often excluded from the male-dominated world of game playing.
Key_Entities: Entertainment and Leisure Software Publishers Association

Title: Nuclear body seeks new tech
Article_Text: The computer systems used to monitor the world's nuclear power installations are so outdated that they are hampering the work of inspectors.  A spokesman for the International Atomic Energy Agency (IA...
Summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency is upgrading its outdated computer systems to improve inspections of nuclear power installations worldwide. The current system is over 20 years old and hampers inspectors' work. The agency is seeking $40m to complete the four-year project.

Title: Web logs aid disaster recovery
Article_Text: Some of the most vivid descriptions of the devastation in southern Asia are on the internet - in the form of web logs or blogs.  Bloggers have been offering snapshots of information from around the re...
Summary: Bloggers in southern Asia are providing vivid descriptions of the devastation caused by the tsunami, with one blogger, Morquendi, sending SMS text messages from the affected areas of Sri Lanka, and others creating online resources to help with relief efforts.

Title: Pandas benefit from wireless net
Article_Text: The world's dwindling panda population is getting a helping hand from a wireless internet network.  The Wolong Nature Reserve in the Sichuan Province of southwest China is home to 20% of the remaining...
Summary: The Wolong Nature Reserve in China is using a wireless internet network to monitor and research giant pandas, improving their chances of survival. The network, developed by Intel, allows staff to share data and images with colleagues worldwide. It also includes a children's learning lab to foster cultural links globally.

Title: Search wars hit desktop PCs
Article_Text: Another front in the on-going battle between Microsoft and Google is about to be opened.  By the end of 2004 Microsoft aims to launch search software to find any kind of file on a PC hard drive. The m...
Summary: Microsoft plans to launch desktop search software by the end of 2004, responding to Google's release of its own search tool. The move aims to help people find files on PC hard drives. Microsoft's software will compete with programs from Google, AOL, Yahoo, and other firms.

Title: Home phones face unclear future
Article_Text: The fixed line phone in your home could soon be an endangered species.  Research by handset maker Nokia shows that more and more people are using their mobile phone for every call they make or take. A...
Summary: Research by Nokia shows that more people are using their mobile phones for every call, with over 45 million people in the UK, Germany, US, and South Korea now only using a mobile. People prefer fixed line phones due to lower call charges, but most see the future in mobiles. Mobiles are used for shorter calls and internet access, while fixed phones are used for longer calls and reliability.

Title: Podcasts mark rise of DIY radio
Article_Text: An Apple iPod or other digital music players can hold anything up to 10,000 songs, which is a lot of space to fill.  But more and more iPod owners are filling that space with audio content created by ...
Summary: Podcasting is a growing trend where individuals create and share audio content online, often for free, using technology such as XML and RSS. Former MTV host Adam Curry is a strong proponent of podcasting, which he believes is an extension of his childhood love of radio gadgetry. Curry has created software called iPodder to automate the process of downloading podcasts to MP3 players.

Title: Sony wares win innovation award
Article_Text: Sony has taken the prize for top innovator at the annual awards of PC Pro Magazine.  It won the award for taking risks with products and for its "brave" commitment to good design. Conferring the award...
Summary: Sony has won the top innovator award at the PC Pro Magazine awards for taking risks with products and commitment to good design. The electronics giant beat off strong competition to take the gong. PC Pro's staff praised Sony's innovative products, including the Vaio W1 desktop computer.

Title: Portable PlayStation ready to go
Article_Text: Sony's PlayStation Portable (PSP) will go on sale in Japan on 12 December.  The long-awaited handheld game playing gadget will cost about 19,800 yen (145 euros) when it hits the shelves. At launch 21 ...
Summary: Sony's PlayStation Portable (PSP) will launch in Japan on December 12, with 21 games available at launch, including Need for Speed and Metal Gear Acid. The PSP's release in Europe and the US is expected in early 2005. Meanwhile, Halo 2 has broken video game records with over 1.5 million pre-orders in the US.

Title: Viewers to be able to shape TV
Article_Text: Imagine editing Titanic down to watch just your favourite bits or cutting out the slushier moments of Star Wars to leave you with a bare bones action-fest.  Manipulating your favourite films to make a...
Summary: A 7.5m euro project funded by the European Union aims to develop a new media genre that allows audiences to create their own media worlds based on their specific interests or tastes. The project, New Media for a New Millennium, will work on seven productions and develop software tools that enable viewers to edit content to their needs.

Title: Games maker fights for survival
Article_Text: One of Britain's largest independent game makers, Argonaut Games, has been put up for sale.  The London-based company behind the Harry Potter games has sacked about 100 employees due to a severe cash ...
Summary: Argonaut Games, a London-based independent game maker behind the Harry Potter games, has been put up for sale due to a severe cash crisis. The company has sacked about 100 employees and warned of £6m losses in the financial year. Administrators have concluded that selling the business is the only way to save it.

Title: Pompeii gets digital make-over
Article_Text: The old-fashioned audio tour of historical places could soon be replaced with computer-generated images that bring the site to life.  A European Union-funded project is looking at providing tourists w...
Summary: A European Union-funded project is developing a computer-generated image technology to bring historical places to life, combining digital and real views for tourists.

Title: Fast moving phone bugs appear
Article_Text: Security firms are warning about several mobile phone viruses that can spread much faster than similar bugs.  The new strains of the Cabir mobile phone virus use short-range radio technology to leap t...
Summary: Security firms are warning about new strains of the Cabir mobile phone virus that can spread via Bluetooth technology, affecting high-end handsets running Symbian Series 60 operating system. The new variants have corrected a mistake from the original Cabir worm, allowing them to infect multiple phones. Users can protect themselves by altering a setting on Symbian phones.

Title: Joke e-mail virus tricks users
Article_Text: A virus that disguises itself as a joke is spreading rapidly across the net.  Anti-virus firms are issuing high-level warnings about the new version of the Bagle e-mail program that seems to be catchi...
Summary: A new version of the Bagle e-mail virus is spreading rapidly across the net, infecting computers running Windows 95-XP, and disabling security measures to spread itself to new victims.

Title: Progress on new internet domains
Article_Text: By early 2005 the net could have two new domain names.  The .post and .travel net domains have been given preliminary approval by the net's administrative body. The names are just two of a total of 10...
Summary: The Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (Icann) has given preliminary approval to two new domain names, .post and .travel, which are expected to be used for postal services and travel organizations, respectively. Icann is considering proposals for another eight domains, including a .xxx domain for pornographic websites, which has been met with resistance due to the difficulty of making pornographers sign up and use it.
Key_Entities: Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers

Title: Argonaut founder rebuilds empire
Article_Text: Jez San, the man behind the Argonaut games group which went into administration a week ago, has bought back most of the company.  The veteran games developer has taken over the Cambridge-based Just Ad...
Summary: Jez San, the founder of Argonaut games group, has bought back most of the company after it went into administration due to a severe cash crisis. The group had warned of annual losses of £6m and had to fire about half of its staff. San has re-emerged, buying back two of the company's subsidiaries, Morpheme and Just Add Monsters.

Title: Dozens held over ID fraud site
Article_Text: Twenty-eight people, including a Briton, have been arrested after a global operation against a website allegedly involved in identity fraud.  Those arrested are accused of operating Shadowcrew.com, wh...
Summary: Twenty-eight people, including a Briton, have been arrested in a global operation against Shadowcrew.com, a website allegedly involved in identity fraud. The operation, led by the US Secret Service, involved seven nations and resulted in the disruption of organised criminals using the internet for profit. The authorities estimate the fraud caused losses of more than $4m.

Title: Robots learn 'robotiquette' rules
Article_Text: Robots are learning lessons on "robotiquette" - how to behave socially - so they can mix better with humans.  By playing games, like pass-the-parcel, a University of Hertfordshire team is finding out ...
Summary: A University of Hertfordshire team is studying how to program robots to behave socially and respect human personal spaces, as part of the European Cogniron robotics project.

Title: Concerns over Windows ATMs

Summary: Cash machine networks may become more vulnerable to computer viruses as banks switch to Windows operating systems, but experts say the risks are small and banks are taking precautions.

Summary: The official re-election site of President George W Bush is blocking visits from overseas users for security reasons, but alternative domains and proxy services have found ways to bypass the block

Title: Loyalty cards idea for TV addicts
