Summary: Loyalty cards are being introduced to TV set-top boxes, allowing viewers to earn rewards for watching specific channels or programs. Sky will activate a spare slot on set-top boxes in January, and broadcasters may offer loyalty points in return for watching certain content. The new system could lead to increased revenue for Sky and other broadcasters.

Title: The Force is strong in Battlefront
Article_Text: The warm reception that has greeted Star Wars: Battlefront is a reflection not of any ingenious innovation in its gameplay, but of its back-to-basics approach and immense nostalgia quotient.  Geared t...
Summary: The article discusses the game Star Wars: Battlefront, its nostalgic value, and its gameplay, which is based on gunfights and familiar elements from the Star Wars films. The game is designed for online multiplayer action but can also be played offline.

Title: 'Ultimate game' award for Doom 3
Article_Text: Sci-fi shooter Doom 3 has blasted away the competition at a major games ceremony, the Golden Joystick awards.  It was the only title to win twice, winning Ultimate Game of the year and best PC game at...
Summary: Doom 3 won two awards at the Golden Joystick awards, including Ultimate Game of the year and best PC game, beating out other highly anticipated titles like Halo 2 and Half-Life 2. The game was developed over four years and is thought to have cost around $15m. Electronic Arts was named top publisher of the year.

Title: Gadget show heralds MP3 season
Article_Text: Partners of those who love their hi-tech gear may want to get their presents in early as experts predict a gadget shortage this Christmas.  With Apple's iPod topping wish lists again, there may not be...
Summary: Experts predict a gadget shortage this Christmas, with Apple's iPod topping wish lists again. A best-of gadget show in London will feature Sony's Qrio Robot and other digital music players. Demand for MP3 players is huge, and gadgets are becoming lifestyle products.

Title: Commodore finds new lease of life
Article_Text: The once-famous Commodore computer brand could be resurrected after being bought by a US-based digital music distributor.  New owner Yeahronimo Media Ventures has not ruled out the possibility of a ne...
Summary: The Commodore computer brand may be revived after being bought by Yeahronimo Media Ventures, a US-based digital music distributor. The new owner plans to develop a 'worldwide entertainment concept' with the brand. The Commodore 64, a pioneering home computer, was launched in 1982 and remains one of the best-selling single computer systems.

Title: Broadband in the UK growing fast
Article_Text: High-speed net connections in the UK are proving more popular than ever.  BT reports that more people signed up for broadband in the last three months than in any other quarter. The 600,000 connection...
Summary: BT reports a record number of broadband connections in the UK, with 600,000 new sign-ups in the last quarter, taking the total to almost 3.3 million. The UK now has the highest number of broadband connections in Europe, surpassing Germany. BT's expansion of ADSL technology led to the surge in demand.

Title: Slim PlayStation triples sales
Article_Text: Sony PlayStation 2's slimmer shape has proved popular with UK gamers, with 50,000 sold in its first week on sale.  Sales have tripled since launch, outstripping Microsoft's Xbox, said market analysts ...
Summary: The Sony PlayStation 2's slim design has been popular with UK gamers, with 50,000 units sold in its first week and sales tripling since launch. The console's success is attributed to the release of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, which broke the UK sales record for video games. Sony is now reaching the seven million barrier for UK sales of the console.
Key_Entities: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King

Title: Seamen sail into biometric future

Summary: The luxury cruise liner Crystal Harmony is testing prototype versions of the world's first internationally issued biometric ID cards, the seafarer's equivalent of a passport. The cards are due to be issued in February next year and are designed to ensure interoperable standards. The International Labour Organisation will publish the results of the current tests by the end of November.

Title: US duo in first spam conviction
Article_Text: A brother and sister in the US have been convicted of sending hundreds of thousands of unsolicited e-mail messages to AOL subscribers.  It is the first criminal prosecution of internet spam distributo...
Summary: A brother and sister in the US have been convicted of sending hundreds of thousands of unsolicited e-mail messages to AOL subscribers. They were found guilty under a state law that bars the sending of bulk e-mails using fake addresses. The brother, Jeremy Jaynes, was sentenced to nine years in prison, while his sister, Jessica DeGroot, was fined $7,500.

Title: US blogger fired by her airline
Article_Text: A US airline attendant suspended over "inappropriate images" on her blog - web diary - says she has been fired.  Ellen Simonetti, known as Queen of the Sky, wrote an anonymous semi-fictional account o...
Summary: Ellen Simonetti, a US airline attendant known as Queen of the Sky, was suspended by Delta Airlines in September over 'inappropriate images' on her blog. She has since been fired and is initiating legal action against the airline for 'wrongful termination'. The airline has declined to elaborate on the reason for her suspension.

Title: Gates opens biggest gadget fair
Article_Text: Bill Gates has opened the Consumer Electronics Show (CES) in Las Vegas, saying that gadgets are working together more to help people manage multimedia content around the home and on the move.  Mr Gate...
Summary: Bill Gates opened the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, highlighting trends in digital imaging, storage technologies, and gaming. He emphasized the importance of seamless technology and social gaming. The show features over 120,000 attendees and 50,000 new products.

Title: GTA sequel is criminally good
Article_Text: The Grand Theft Auto series of games have set themselves the very highest of standards in recent years, but the newest addition is more than able to live up to an increasingly grand tradition.  The 18...
Summary: The article discusses the latest addition to the Grand Theft Auto series, GTA: San Andreas, and how it builds upon the previous games, offering a massive 3D environment and improved gameplay mechanics. The game's setting, San Andreas, is a fictional representation of Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Las Vegas, with a focus on its ambience and graphical detail. The game's violence and dark tone are also highlighted.

Title: BT offers free net phone calls
Article_Text: BT is offering customers free internet telephone calls if they sign up to broadband in December.  The Christmas give-away entitles customers to free telephone calls anywhere in the UK via the internet...
Summary: BT is offering free internet telephone calls to customers who sign up for broadband in December, with the promotion limited to the first 50,000 people. The offer requires customers to use BT's internet telephony software and have a microphone and speakers or headset on their PC. BT aims to increase broadband adoption and retain market share.

Title: When invention turns to innovation

Summary: Nick Donofrio, senior vice-president of technology and manufacturing at IBM, argues that future technological inventions will not have the same transformative impact as past inventions, but rather will bring about subtle and pervasive changes that will improve people's lives. He emphasizes the importance of deep computing, pervasive computing, and global diversity in the tech industry.

Title: Firefox browser takes on Microsoft
Article_Text: Microsoft's Internet Explorer has a serious rival in the long-awaited Firefox 1.0 web browser, which has just been released.  Few people get excited when some new software is released, especially when...
Summary: Firefox 1.0 has been released, gaining popularity and winning users away from Internet Explorer, with the Mozilla Foundation claiming it has been downloaded almost eight million times.

Title: Halo fans' hope for sequel

Summary: The Xbox video game Halo 2 has been released in the US and UK, and is considered one of the most anticipated games of all time due to its high production values, immersive gameplay, and innovative features such as online multiplayer and physics engine.

Title: Players sought for $1m prize

The event will be filmed and made available online, with the first stop on the world tour taking place in Istanbul, Turkey from February 10-13.

Summary: Football Manager 2005 is a realistic and satisfying football management game that has been released earlier than expected. The game is a spiritual successor to Championship Manager and has been developed by Sports Interactive.

Title: Musicians 'upbeat' about the net

Summary: A survey by Pew Internet found that musicians are embracing the internet as a way to reach new fans and sell more music, with most seeing it as a positive force rather than a threat to their livelihood. The survey found that most artists saw file-sharing as both good and bad, but most agreed it should be illegal. However, many disagreed with the lawsuits launched against downloaders.

Summary: The number of Europeans with broadband has increased by 60% over the past year, with 54 million people now hooked up to the net, according to market analysts Nielsen/NetRatings. The report predicts that broadband will continue to grow, challenging traditional media industries.

The report also found that broadband is encouraging people to take a more active role online.

Despite their limited reach, blogs have become a powerful tool for people to express themselves and give their voice to marginalized communities.

Mobile marketing is becoming increasingly popular, with firms using text messages to promote special offers and services.

Summary: Half-Life 2 is a highly-anticipated computer game that exceeds its promise, offering a vivid and convincing virtual world that immerses the player in a movie-like experience. The game's sophistication and attention to detail make it a standout in its genre.

Exeem will use a decentralized tracker system and a rating system to ensure files are high-quality copies. The system is currently being tested and will be released in late January.

Summary: Online games broke into the political arena in 2004, with the US presidential election providing a showcase for many games aimed at a younger audience. The results show promise for a non-invasive brain control interface.

The brother, Jeremy Jaynes, was sentenced to nine years in prison, while his sister, Jessica DeGroot, was fined $7,500.

Sony is now reaching the seven million barrier for UK sales of the console.

Title: How to make a gigapixel picture

Summary: Researchers in the Netherlands created the largest digital panoramic photo in the world, a 2.5 billion pixel image of Delft, by stitching together 600 single snaps. The image can be explored online and has already attracted over 200,000 daily visitors. The project was completed using automatic techniques and upgraded technologies.

Title: Remote control rifle range debuts
Article_Text: Soon you could go hunting via the net.  A Texas company is considering letting web users use a remote-controlled rifle to shoot down deer, antelope and wild pigs. For a small fee users will take contr...
Summary: A Texas company is considering allowing web users to control a remote-controlled rifle to hunt deer, antelope, and wild pigs on a 133-hectare ranch for a small fee. The idea came to the company's founder after watching a webcam of deer on another website. The remote hunting system is still in development and has cost $10,000. The company plans to charge $150 per session, with additional fees for meat processing and taxidermy work.

Title: Gangsters dominate gaming chart
Article_Text: Video games on consoles and computers proved more popular than ever in 2004.  Gamers spent more than £1.34bn in 2004, almost 7% more than they did in 2003 according to figures released by the UK gamin...
Summary: The UK gaming industry saw a significant increase in sales in 2004, with gamers spending £1.34bn on video games, a 7% rise from the previous year. The top-selling game of the year was GTA: San Andreas, which sold over 1.75 million copies. The industry's trade body noted that the market continued to be buoyant despite the lack of new generation consoles.
Key_Entities: Entertainment and Leisure Software Publishers Association

Title: British Library gets wireless net
Article_Text: Visitors to the British Library will be able to get wireless internet access alongside the extensive information available in its famous reading rooms.  Broadband wireless connectivity will be made av...
Summary: The British Library will offer wireless internet access in its reading rooms, auditorium, and outdoor areas, with pricing starting at £4.50 per hour or £35 per month. The service has been successful, with 1,200 sessions per week and 86% of visitors carrying laptops. The Library aims to improve services with technology.

Title: UK broadband gets speed injection
Article_Text: Broadband's rapid rise continues apace as speeds gear up a notch.  An eight megabit service has been launched by internet service provider UK Online. It is 16 times faster than the average broadband p...
Summary: UK Online has launched an 8 megabit broadband service, 16 times faster than the average broadband package, with a £39.99 monthly price tag. The service will be available in metropolitan areas and will pave the way for services like video-on-demand and broadband TV. It will initially be available to 4.4 million households within a 2km radius of 230 telephone exchanges.

Title: Row brewing over peer-to-peer ads
Article_Text: Music download networks are proving popular not just with an audience of youngsters keen to take advantage of free music but with advertisers equally keen to reach out to a captive audience.  The deba...
Summary: Music download networks are popular among both young users and advertisers, but the music industry is threatening to close them down due to copyright concerns. Advertisers are caught between supporting legitimate services and reaching a captive audience, with some companies unaware of their ads appearing on peer-to-peer networks.

Title: How to smash a home computer
Article_Text: An executive who froze his broken hard disk thinking it would be fixed has topped a list of the weirdest computer mishaps.  Although computer malfunctions remain the most common cause of file loss, da...
Summary: A list of the top 10 global data disasters was compiled by recovery company Ontrack, highlighting common causes of file loss including human behavior and computer malfunctions. Data recovery experts stress the importance of backing up and protecting important files. Human error, including 'computer rage', is a growing problem in data loss cases.

Title: Mobile picture power in your pocket
Article_Text: How many times have you wanted to have a camera to hand to catch an unexpected event that would make headlines?  With a modern mobile phone that has a camera built in, you no longer need to curse, you...
Summary: The use of mobile phones with cameras is becoming increasingly common in news gathering, allowing for immediate capture of breaking news events. This trend is expected to continue as higher resolution phone cameras become more widespread. The phenomenon has both positive and negative aspects, including the potential for increased immediacy and the risk of nuisance for public figures.

Title: Man auctions ad space on forehead
Article_Text: A 20-year-old US man is selling advertising space on his forehead to the highest bidder on website eBay.  Andrew Fisher, from Omaha, Nebraska, said he would have a non-permanent logo or brand name tat...
Summary: A 20-year-old US man, Andrew Fisher, is selling advertising space on his forehead for 30 days on eBay, with the highest bid currently at over $322. Fisher, from Omaha, Nebraska, plans to use the money to pay for college and study graphic design. The auction, which started on eBay, has received 39 bids, with the winner able to choose a logo or brand name to be tattooed on Fisher's forehead.

Title: Toxic web links help virus spread
Article_Text: Virus writers have begun using the power of the web to spread their malicious wares.  A Windows virus called Bofra is turning infected machines into distributors of its malicious code. Those clicking ...
Summary: A Windows virus called Bofra is spreading malicious code by turning infected machines into distributors of its code, exploiting a Windows vulnerability discovered recently. The virus uses fake web links to trick users into downloading it. Anti-virus firms are warning of the need for deep defences to prevent its spread.

Title: Millions to miss out on the net
Article_Text: By 2025, 40% of the UK's population will still be without internet access at home, says a study.  Around 23 million Britons will miss out on a wide range of essential services such as education and me...
Summary: By 2025, 40% of the UK's population will still be without internet access at home, according to a study by BT. The report predicts that 23 million Britons will miss out on essential services. The digital divide is expected to worsen unless the government and telecoms industry come up with new ways to address the issue.

Title: Lifestyle 'governs mobile choice'
Article_Text: Faster, better or funkier hardware alone is not going to help phone firms sell more handsets, research suggests.  Instead, phone firms keen to get more out of their customers should not just be pushin...
Summary: Research by Ericsson suggests that phone firms should focus on how handsets fit into customers' lifestyles rather than just pushing technology for its own sake. A study of 14,000 mobile phone owners found that people's habits remain the same, but they move activities into their phones for convenience. New handset technologies can drive new habits and lifestyles, but only when a significant number of users adopt them.

Title: Search sites get closer to users
Article_Text: Search sites want to get to know you better.  Not content with providing access to the millions of websites, many now offer ways that do a better job of remembering, cataloguing and managing all the i...
Summary: Search sites like Ask Jeeves and Blinkx are releasing utilities to help users remember and manage their web searches, allowing them to save websites of interest and search through previously found sites more easily.

Title: Anti-spam screensaver scrapped
Article_Text: A contentious campaign to bump up the bandwidth bills of spammers by flooding their sites with data has been dropped.  Lycos Europe's Make Love, Not Spam campaign began in late November but its tactic...
Summary: A campaign by Lycos Europe to flood spam sites with data to increase bandwidth bills has been dropped after controversy and criticism from net veterans and security organisations.

Title: Europe backs digital TV lifestyle
Article_Text: How people receive their digital entertainment in the future could change, following the launch of an ambitious European project.  In Nice last week, the European Commission announced its Networked & ...
Summary: The European Commission has launched the Networked & Electronic Media (NEM) initiative to create a seamless digital entertainment experience. The project aims to bring together experts and companies to develop standards for digital media distribution. The Commission wants to make digital formats open to all and work on any gadget, a move that could please consumers who feel that content holders' wishes are prioritized over theirs.

Title: TV future in the hands of viewers
Article_Text: With home theatre systems, plasma high-definition TVs, and digital video recorders moving into the living room, the way people watch TV will be radically different in five years' time.  That is accord...
Summary: New technologies such as digital and personal video recorders (DVR and PVR) are changing the way people watch TV, allowing for more personalized viewing experiences and on-demand content delivery. The US is leading the trend, with companies like TiVo and Sky+ offering DVR capabilities, while European broadcasters are concerned about the impact on advertising revenues and brand identity.

Title: Cyber criminals step up the pace
Article_Text: So-called phishing attacks that try to trick people into handing over confidential details have boomed in 2004, say security experts.  The number of phishing e-mail messages stopped by security firm M...
Summary: Phishing attacks have increased significantly in 2004, with security firm MessageLabs detecting over 18 million phishing e-mail messages. Phishing gangs are using sophisticated techniques to harvest information, and customised attacks are becoming more common. Viruses and spam remain popular among cyber-criminals.

Title: Gritty return for Prince of Persia
Article_Text: Still basking in the relatively recent glory of last year's Sands Of Time, the dashing Prince of Persia is back in Warrior Within, and in a more bellicose mood than last time.  This sequel gives the f...
Summary: The Prince of Persia: Warrior Within game is a sequel to the Sands of Time, with a grim and gritty new look, increased action and violence, and a time-traveling plot. The game features meticulously-animated acrobatic moves and a variety of combat techniques. However, the game's graphics and mechanics are not quite as engaging as they should be, resulting in a less enjoyable experience.

Title: Disney backs Sony DVD technology
Article_Text: A next generation DVD technology backed by Sony has received a major boost.  Film giant Disney says it will produce its future DVDs using Sony's Blu-ray Disc technology, but has not ruled out a rival ...
Summary: Film giant Disney has backed Sony's Blu-ray Disc technology, while rival format HD-DVD is backed by Toshiba and other studios. The two formats promise high-quality pictures and sound, and the studios prefer a single standard to maximize revenue. Several studios have already chosen a side in the format battle.

Title: Britons growing 'digitally obese'
Article_Text: Gadget lovers are so hungry for digital data many are carrying the equivalent of 10 trucks full of paper in "weight".  Music, images, e-mails, and texts are being hoarded on mobiles, cameras laptops a...
Summary: A Toshiba study found that people are carrying large amounts of digital data on their devices, equivalent to 10 trucks full of paper, due to the increasing trend of portable devices with built-in hard drives. The study suggests that this trend will continue, with the number of hard drives in consumer electronics gadgets expected to grow from 17 million to 55 million in 2006. The cost of making hard drives has dropped, making them more cost-effective than other forms of memory.

Title: Halo 2 heralds traffic explosion
Article_Text: The growing popularity of online gaming could spell problems for net service firms, warns network monitoring company Sandvine.  It issued the warning following analysis which shows that traffic on the...
Summary: Network monitoring company Sandvine warns that the growing popularity of online gaming could spell problems for net service firms due to increased traffic and demands for bandwidth. The Xbox game network experienced a fourfold increase in traffic on the launch day of Halo 2, and service providers must ensure their networks can cope with these demands. Intelligent networks that prioritize or reserve bandwidth for games may become common.

Title: Media gadgets get moving
Article_Text: Pocket-sized devices that let people carry around video and images are set to have a big year in 2005, according to industry experts.  Last year saw the emergence of portable media players, such as th...
Summary: Portable media players are expected to become smarter and more connected in 2005, allowing users to find more video content to watch on the go. Archos launched its Linux-based portable media device with Wi-Fi capability, while Microsoft announced content deals with TiVo and other companies.

Title: Satellite mapping aids Darfur relief
Article_Text: Aid workers trying to house, feed and clothe millions of homeless refugees in the Sudanese region of Darfur are getting a helping hand from advanced mapping technology.  A European consortium of compa...
Summary: A European consortium called Respond is using advanced mapping technology to help aid workers in Darfur, Sudan, by providing accurate and up-to-date maps to overcome logistical challenges.

Title: Spam e-mails tempt net shoppers
Article_Text: Computer users across the world continue to ignore security warnings about spam e-mails and are being lured into buying goods, a report suggests.  More than a quarter have bought software through spam...
Summary: A report suggests that computer users worldwide are ignoring security warnings about spam e-mails, with over a quarter buying software and 24% buying clothes or jewelry through spam e-mails. Organised crime rings use spam to glean personal information and drive advertising traffic. Experts warn consumers to stay alert and exercise caution.

Title: More power to the people says HP
Article_Text: The digital revolution is focused on letting people tell and share their own stories, according to Carly Fiorina, chief of technology giant Hewlett Packard.  The job of firms such as HP now, she said ...
Summary: Carly Fiorina, CEO of Hewlett Packard, emphasized the importance of the digital revolution in making people the center of technology, with a focus on convergence of digital and physical worlds. She also highlighted the need for standardization in the technology industry to ensure seamless gadget functionality. Fiorina showcased new products, including HP digital cameras and a visual radio service for mobiles, and announced partnerships with Nokia and MTV.

Title: Robotic pods take on car design
Article_Text: A new breed of wearable robotic vehicles that envelop drivers are being developed by Japanese car giant Toyota.  The company's vision for the single passenger in the 21st Century involves the driver c...
Summary: Toyota is developing wearable robotic vehicles that envelop drivers, including a four-wheeled leaf-like device and an egg-shaped cocoon that walks upright on two feet. The prototypes will be demonstrated at the Expo 2005 in Aichi, Japan, and are designed as personal mobility devices with various features and capabilities.
Key_Entities: University of the West of England

Title: Hi-tech posters guide commuters
Article_Text: Interactive posters are helping Londoners get around the city during the festive season.  When interrogated with a mobile phone, the posters pass on a number that people can call to get information ab...
Summary: Interactive posters are being used by Transport for London to provide information on safe routes home for Londoners, especially women, during the festive season. The posters can beam information to phones with IR ports, and will run until Boxing Day. The technology is being used in conjunction with a campaign to cut the number of sexual assaults by unlicensed minicab drivers.

Title: Parents face video game lessons
Article_Text: Ways of ensuring that parents know which video games are suitable for children are to be considered by the games industry.  The issue was discussed at a meeting between UK government officials, indust...
Summary: The UK government is considering ways to ensure parents know which video games are suitable for children, following concerns over violent games and their potential impact on young players. The issue was discussed at a meeting between government officials, industry representatives, and the British Board of Film Classification. Possible measures include a campaign to explain the games rating system and changes to labelling.
Key_Entities: Entertainment and Leisure Software Publishers Association

Title: BBC web search aids odd queries
Article_Text: The BBC's online search engine was used a record amount in 2004, helping with enquires both simple and strange.  More than 277 million enquiries were made, asking for informaton of a wide range of sub...
Summary: The BBC's online search engine received a record 277 million enquiries in 2004, including requests for information on various subjects and strange queries with spelling and grammar errors.

Title: 2D Metal Slug offers retro fun
Article_Text: Like some drill sergeant from the past, Metal Slug 3 is a wake-up call to today's gamers molly-coddled with slick visuals and fancy trimmings.  With its hand-animated sprites and 2D side-scrolling, th...
Summary: Metal Slug 3 is a frantic 2D side-scrolling shooter that challenges players with hordes of enemies and few lives. The game features ultra-responsive controls and a variety of vehicles to commandeer. It is considered a retro game due to its hand-animated sprites and 2D gameplay.

Title: Mobile multimedia slow to catch on
Article_Text: There is no doubt that mobile phones sporting cameras and colour screens are hugely popular. Consumers swapping old phones for slinkier, dinkier versions are thought to be responsible for a 26% increa...
Summary: Mobile phone users are not sending multimedia messages due to lack of knowledge and technical issues. Operators are finding alternative technologies to overcome bandwidth limitations. A new broadcast system is being used to get multimedia to customers, increasing engagement.

Title: Internet boom for gift shopping
Article_Text: Cyberspace is becoming a very popular destination for Christmas shoppers.  Forecasts predict that British people will spend £4bn buying gifts online during the festive season, an increase of 64% on 20...
Summary: British people are expected to spend £4bn on online Christmas gifts, a 64% increase from 2003, with 85% of online shoppers planning to do most of their gift buying online. Online shopping is becoming increasingly popular, with Britons leading Europe in their affection for online shopping.

Title: Google to scan famous libraries
Article_Text: The libraries of five of the world's most important academic institutions are to be digitised by Google.  Scanned pages from books in the public domain will then be made available for search and readi...
Summary: Google is digitising the libraries of five major academic institutions, including Michigan and Stanford universities, and making their public domain books available for search and reading online. The project aims to bring offline information online. Online pages from scanned books will not have adverts but will have links to online stores.

Title: Microsoft takes on desktop search
Article_Text: Microsoft has entered the desktop search fray, releasing a test version of its tool to find documents, e-mails and other files on a PC hard drive.  The beta program only works on PCs running Windows X...
Summary: Microsoft has released a test version of its desktop search tool, which can be used on PCs running Windows XP or Windows 2000. The tool is part of a growing market for desktop search software, with Google and Yahoo also launching similar products. Microsoft's program can be used as a toolbar or within the Outlook e-mail program.

Title: Gamers snap up new Sony PSP
Article_Text: Gamers have bought almost all of the first batch of Sony's new PlayStation Portable (PSP) games console, which went on sale in Japan on Sunday.  Thousands of people queued for hours to get hold of one...
Summary: Gamers in Japan have bought almost all of the first batch of Sony's new PlayStation Portable (PSP) games console, which went on sale on Sunday. The handheld console can play games, music, and movies and is set to go on sale in Europe and North America next year. Sony plans to ship three million PSPs by March 2005.

Title: Go-ahead for new internet names
Article_Text: The internet could soon have two new domain names, aimed at mobile services and the jobs market.  The Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (Icann) has given preliminary approval to two ...
Summary: The Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (Icann) has given preliminary approval to two new domain names, .mobi and .jobs, aimed at mobile services and the jobs market. The process to see the new domain names go live in cyberspace could take months. The .mobi domain would be aimed at websites and other services that work specifically around mobile phones.
Key_Entities: Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers

Title: Set your television to wow
Article_Text: Television started off as a magical blurry image. Then came the sharpness, the colour and the widescreen format. Now the TV set is taking another leap forward into a crystal clear future, although tho...
Summary: High-definition TV (HDTV) is finally taking off in a handful of countries, mainly the US and Japan, with viewers in these countries enjoying sharper images than standard TV. However, TV viewers in Europe will have to wait, with only 12% of homes expected to have HDTV capable TVs by 2008.

Title: Hollywood to sue net film pirates
Article_Text: The US movie industry has launched legal action to sue people who facilitate illegal film downloading.  The Motion Picture Association of America wants to stop people using the program BitTorrent to s...
Summary: The Motion Picture Association of America is suing people who facilitate illegal film downloading using BitTorrent and other file-sharing programs. Over 100 server operators have been targeted in the US and UK. The industry aims to cut off users of illegal movies at source.

Title: PC ownership to 'double by 2010'
Article_Text: The number of personal computers worldwide is expected to double by 2010 to 1.3 billion machines, according to a report by analysts Forrester Research.  The growth will be driven by emerging markets s...
Summary: The number of personal computers worldwide is expected to double by 2010 to 1.3 billion machines, driven by emerging markets such as China, Russia, and India. Low-priced computers made by local companies are expected to dominate in these markets. The report comes after IBM sold its PC hardware division to Lenovo.

Title: PC photo printers challenge pros
Article_Text: Home printed pictures can be cheaper and higher quality than those from High Street developers, tests shows.  A survey carried out by PC Pro magazine looked at which of 100 home photo printers offered...
Summary: A survey by PC Pro magazine found that home photo printers can be cheaper and higher quality than those from High Street developers, with some printers producing images that last longer than professionally produced photographs.

Title: The gaming world in 2005
Article_Text: If you have finished Doom 3, Half Life 2 and Halo 2, don't worry. There's a host of gaming gems set for release in 2005.   WORLD OF WARCRAFT   The US reception to this game from developers Blizzard ha...
Summary: Several highly anticipated games are set to be released in 2005, including World of Warcraft, Ico 2, The Legend of Zelda, Advance Wars DS, S.T.A.L.K.E.R., Metal Gear Solid: Snake Eater, Dead or Alive Ultimate, and Knights of the Old Republic II.

Title: Bond game fails to shake or stir
Article_Text: For gaming fans, the word GoldenEye evokes excited memories not only of the James Bond revival flick of 1995, but also the classic shoot-em-up that accompanied it and left N64 owners glued to their co...
Summary: The game GoldenEye: Rogue Agent fails to deliver on its promise, struggling to capture the fun of its namesake, and is marred by poor gameplay, graphical bugs, and a lack of confidence in its design. Despite featuring iconic Bond villains, the game's flaws make it a disappointment for most players.

Title: Humanoid robot learns how to run
Article_Text: Car-maker Honda's humanoid robot Asimo has just got faster and smarter.  The Japanese firm is a leader in developing two-legged robots and the new, improved Asimo (Advanced Step in Innovative Mobility...
Summary: Honda's humanoid robot Asimo has improved its speed and agility, running and interacting with people, and is expected to find gainful employment in homes and offices.
Key_Entities: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe

Title: Nintendo adds media playing to DS
Article_Text: Nintendo is releasing an adapter for its DS handheld console so it can play music and video.  The add-on for the DS means people can download TV programmes, film clips or MP3 files to the adaptor and ...
Summary: Nintendo is releasing a media adapter for its DS handheld console to play music and video, aiming to protect its dominance in the handheld gaming market. The adapter will be available in Japan from February and will work with the GameBoy Advance SP. The move is seen as a response to the Sony PSP's multi-purpose media player and game gadget.

Title: Apple sues to stop product leaks
Article_Text: Computer firm Apple has issued a lawsuit to prevent online leaks of information about future products.  The lawsuit, against an unidentified individual, comes just weeks before the MacWorld conference...
Summary: Apple has filed a lawsuit against an unidentified individual for leaking confidential information about future products, just weeks before the MacWorld conference in San Francisco.

Title: Gamer buys $26,500 virtual land
Article_Text: A 22-year-old gamer has spent $26,500 (£13,700) on an island that exists only in a computer role-playing game (RPG).  The Australian gamer, known only by his gaming moniker Deathifier, bought the isla...
Summary: A 22-year-old gamer, Deathifier, spent $26,500 on a virtual island in the game Project Entropia. The island, which includes a castle and beaches, can be developed and sold to other players. The game's economy allows players to exchange real currency for virtual PEDs, which can be used to buy items and land.

Title: Microsoft sets sights on spyware
Article_Text: Windows users could soon be paying Microsoft to keep PCs free of spyware.  Following the takeover of anti-spyware firm Giant, Microsoft said it would soon release a toolkit that strips machines of the...
Summary: Microsoft plans to release a toolkit to clean up Windows machines from spyware, initially free but potentially charging for future updates. A recent survey found that 90% of PCs are infested with spyware, with an average of 28 separate programs on each machine. The company is working out pricing and licensing issues.

Title: Video phone help for deaf people
Article_Text: Deaf people who prefer to communicate using British Sign Language (BSL) could soon be having their phone conversations relayed using webcams or videophones and an interpreter.  The Video Relay Service...
Summary: The Royal National Institute for Deaf People is piloting a Video Relay Service to relay phone conversations for deaf people using British Sign Language, urging telecoms regulator Ofcom to reduce the cost to match ordinary phone calls.
Key_Entities: Royal National Institute for Deaf People

Title: Virus poses as Christmas e-mail
Article_Text: Security firms are warning about a Windows virus disguising itself as an electronic Christmas card.  The Zafi.D virus translates the Christmas greeting on its subject line into the language of the per...
Summary: Security firms warn about a Windows virus disguising itself as an electronic Christmas card, spreading widely online due to its multilingual ability. The virus, Zafi.D, infects Microsoft Outlook and sends itself to new victims via email attachments. It disables anti-virus and firewall software, and opens a backdoor on infected machines.

Title: Fast lifts rise into record books
Article_Text: Two high-speed lifts at the world's tallest building have been officially recognised as the planet's fastest.  The lifts take only 30 seconds to whisk passengers to the top of the 508m tall TFC 101 To...
Summary: Two high-speed lifts at the TFC 101 Tower in Taipei, Taiwan have been officially recognized as the planet's fastest, reaching speeds of 17m per second and 38mph. The lifts take 30 seconds to ascend to the top of the 508m tower and have a pressure control system to prevent ear popping. The tower is due to be officially opened on December 31.

Title: Broadband in the UK gathers pace
Article_Text: One person in the UK is joining the internet's fast lane every 10 seconds, according to BT.  The telecoms giant said the number of people on broadband via the telephone line had now surpassed four mil...
Summary: The number of people in the UK with broadband connections has surpassed four million, with almost six million having fast, always-on connections. The growth is driven by fierce competition and falling prices, with BT aiming to extend its reach to 99.4% of homes and businesses by next summer. The company expects to hit its five million target earlier than expected.

Title: Hollywood campaign hits websites
Article_Text: Movie studio efforts to stop pirated films being shared on peer-to-peer networks have claimed a high-profile victim.  The campaign of legal action is thought to be behind the closure of the widely use...
Summary: The Suprnova.org website, a popular BitTorrent site, has closed down following a legal campaign by the Motion Picture Association of America. The MPAA launched 100 lawsuits against BitTorrent server operators, targeting the servers rather than end users. This move is believed to be having an effect, with other popular BitTorrent sites such as Phoenix Torrents also shutting down.

Title: Poles play with GameBoy 'blip-pop'

Summary: A group of artists in Poland has created a unique sound by combining the sounds of Nintendo GameBoy consoles to create 'blip-pop' music, with the Gameboyzz Orchestra Project taking the game sounds to a new level.

Title: Santy worm makes unwelcome visit
Article_Text: Thousands of website bulletin boards have been defaced by a virus that used Google to spread across the net.  The Santy worm first appeared on 20 December and within 24 hours had successfully hit more...
Summary: A virus known as the Santy worm has defaced thousands of websites by exploiting a vulnerability in phpBB software, but its spread has been stopped after Google blocked infected sites searching for new victims. The worm was able to infect over 40,000 websites within 24 hours. Google's security team has acknowledged that its response time could be improved.

Title: EU software patent law delayed
Article_Text: Controversial new EU rules for the patenting of computer-based inventions have been put on hold due to a last minute intervention from Poland.  Poland - a large and therefore crucial EU member - has r...
Summary: EU rules for patenting computer-based inventions have been put on hold due to Poland's request for more time to consider the issue, particularly regarding software patenting. Critics argue the law would favor large companies over small, innovative ones. Polish ministers want to change the text to exclude software patenting.

Title: Apple sues 'Tiger' file sharers
Article_Text: Apple has taken more legal action to stop online leaks of its new products.  The computer giant has sued three men for releasing preview versions of its latest Mac OSX software onto file-sharing sites...
Summary: Apple has sued three men for releasing preview versions of its latest Mac OSX software onto file-sharing sites prior to its release. The company has taken legal action to protect its intellectual property and future financial results. The lawsuit comes just weeks before the MacWorld conference in San Francisco.

Title: Apple unveils low-cost 'Mac mini'

Summary: Apple has unveiled a new, low-cost Macintosh computer called the Mac mini, priced at $499, and a new iPod shuffle music player, priced at $99-$149. The Mac mini is designed to appeal to PC users looking for an affordable, easy-to-use computer. The new products mark a shift for Apple into the mass market, a move analysts say is a sensible business decision.

Title: Speech takes on search engines
Article_Text: A Scottish firm is looking to attract web surfers with a search engine that reads out results.  Called Speegle, it has the look and feel of a normal search engine, with the added feature of being able...
Summary: A Scottish firm, CEC Systems, has launched a search engine called Speegle that reads out results, aiming to attract web surfers with visual impairments. The site uses speech technology to convert web text into synthesised speech. Experts question whether talking search engines are of real benefit to people with visual impairments.
Key_Entities: Royal National Institute of the Blind

Title: Broadband steams ahead in the US
Article_Text: More and more Americans are joining the internet's fast lane, according to official figures.  The number of people and business connected to broadband jumped by 38% in a year, said the US Federal Comm...
Summary: The number of broadband connections in the US increased by 38% in a year, reaching 32.5 million by the end of June 2004. The US is still behind other nations in terms of broadband adoption. The FCC reports that broadband is becoming increasingly popular for research, shopping, and entertainment.

Google has shown that search can be a lucrative business, with targeted ads helping the company reach revenues of $805.9m for the three months to September.

Title: US hacker breaks into T-Mobile

T-Mobile has confirmed that the US Secret Service is investigating whether Jacobsen accessed photos taken by T-Mobile subscribers.

The technology is currently being used in a limited capacity in the UK and Europe.

The club aims to increase disabled people's participation in motorsport at all levels.

Both games have their strengths and weaknesses.

The format is seen as crucial for the gaming industry, which is a $20 billion market.
