The mobile industry is keen to get into music downloading, but limited storage and other issues must be addressed.

Title: Blind student 'hears in colour'
Article_Text: A blind student has developed software that turns colours into musical notes so that he can read weather maps.  Victor Wong, a graduate student from Hong Kong studying at Cornell University in New Yor...
Summary: A blind student, Victor Wong, has developed software that translates colors into musical notes, allowing him to read weather maps and study space weather. The software assigns piano notes to individual pixels based on their color, with red corresponding to the highest note. The technology is still in its infancy and requires further development to be commercially viable.

Title: Apple attacked over sources row
Article_Text: Civil liberties group the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) has joined a legal fight between three US online journalists and Apple.  Apple wants the reporters to reveal 20 sources used for stories ...
Summary: The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) is representing three US online journalists in a legal fight against Apple, which is seeking to reveal the sources of leaked information about forthcoming products. The EFF argues that the journalists are protected by the American constitution and that the case threatens the basic freedoms of the press. The case will examine whether online journalists have the same privileges and protections as those writing for newspapers and magazines.

Title: Mobile audio enters new dimension
Article_Text: As mobile phones move closer to being a ubiquitous, all-in-one media player, audio is becoming ever more important. But how good can that sound be from such a small device?  The sound of a buzzing bee...
Summary: Sonaptic is developing 3D audio technology for mobile phones, which can create a surround sound effect from a small device. The company has partnered with Japanese mobile network NTT DoCoMo to set standards for 3D audio on mobile phones. The technology has been released in Japan and is expected to be available in the UK in the next six months.

Title: DVD copy protection strengthened
Article_Text: DVDs will be harder to copy thanks to new anti-piracy measures devised by copy protection firm Macrovision.  The pirated DVD market is enormous because current copy protection was hacked more than fiv...
Summary: Macrovision has introduced a new anti-piracy measure called RipGuard to prevent DVD copying, which will be rolled out on DVDs starting from the middle of 2005. The technology is designed to reduce DVD ripping and supply of illegal peer-to-peer files. It will work in nearly all current DVD players, but may not be compatible with some machines, including those running Linux.

Title: Millions buy MP3 players in US
Article_Text: One in 10 adult Americans - equivalent to 22 million people - owns an MP3 player, according to a survey.  A study by the Pew Internet and American Life Project found that MP3 players are the gadget of...
Summary: A survey by the Pew Internet and American Life Project found that 22 million Americans own MP3 players, with 59% of owners being men and 41% women. The survey also found that MP3 players are more common among affluent young Americans and those with broadband access. The ease of use and growth of music available on the net are the main factors for the upsurge in ownership.
Key_Entities: Pew Internet and American Life Project

Title: Britons fed up with net service
Article_Text: A survey conducted by PC Pro Magazine has revealed that many Britons are unhappy with their internet service.  They are fed up with slow speeds, high prices and the level of customer service they rece...
Summary: A survey by PC Pro Magazine found that many Britons are unhappy with their internet service due to slow speeds, high prices, and poor customer service. 17% of readers have switched suppliers, and 16% are considering changing in the near future. The survey highlights the competitive nature of broadband providers in the UK.

Title: Intel unveils laser breakthrough
Article_Text: Intel has said it has found a way to put a silicon-based laser on a chip, raising hopes of much faster networks.  Scientists at Intel have overcome a fundamental problem that before now has prevented ...
Summary: Intel has developed a way to put a silicon-based laser on a chip, which could lead to faster networks and the integration of fibre optic cables with computer chips.

Title: EU software patent law faces axe
Article_Text: The European Parliament has thrown out a bill that would have allowed software to be patented.  Politicians unanimously rejected the bill and now it must go through another round of consultation if it...
Summary: The European Parliament has rejected a bill that would have allowed software to be patented, sending it back for re-consultation. The bill was backed by some tech firms but opposed by others who said it could stifle innovation and be abused by firms to protect existing monopolies. The bill's progress was delayed twice and the European Legal Affairs Committee recommended re-drafting the law.

Title: IBM puts cash behind Linux push
Article_Text: IBM is spending $100m (£52m) over the next three years beefing up its commitment to Linux software.  The cash injection will be used to help its customers use Linux on every type of device from handhe...
Summary: IBM is investing $100m over three years to boost its commitment to Linux software, responding to customer demand for the open source software. The investment will fund technical, research, and marketing initiatives to increase Linux use across various devices. This move builds on IBM's existing efforts to promote Linux, which began in 2001.

Title: Apple iPod family expands market
Article_Text: Apple has expanded its iPod family with the release of its next generation of the digital music players.  Its latest challenges to the growing digital music gadget market include an iPod mini model wh...
Summary: Apple has released its next generation of iPods with improved storage capacity, longer battery life, and lower prices. The company aims to maintain its dominant position in the digital music market. Analysts expect increased competition from mobile phone operators offering streaming services.
Key_Entities: Pew Internet and American Life Project

Title: US woman sues over ink cartridges
Article_Text: A US woman is suing Hewlett Packard (HP), saying its printer ink cartridges are secretly programmed to expire on a certain date.  The unnamed woman from Georgia says that a chip inside the cartridge t...
Summary: A US woman is suing Hewlett Packard, alleging its printer ink cartridges are programmed to expire prematurely, while HP has declined to comment on the lawsuit. The lawsuit seeks to represent anyone in the US who purchased an HP inkjet printer since February 2001. The cost of printer cartridges has been a contentious issue in Europe.

Title: Security warning over 'FBI virus'
Article_Text: The US Federal Bureau of Investigation is warning that a computer virus is being spread via e-mails that purport to be from the FBI.  The e-mails show that they have come from an fbi.gov address and t...
Summary: The FBI is warning about a computer virus being spread via e-mails that appear to be from the FBI, and is investigating the incident.

Title: Mobile networks seek turbo boost
Article_Text: Third-generation mobile (3G) networks need to get faster if they are to deliver fast internet surfing on the move and exciting new services.  That was one of the messages from the mobile industry at t...
Summary: The mobile industry is shifting focus from current 3G networks to faster, higher bandwidth services. Companies like Siemens and Motorola are developing new technologies, such as one gigabit per second transmission, to meet growing demand for mobile internet and video. However, these systems are not yet commercially available.
Key_Entities: Fraunhofer German-Sino Lab for Mobile Communications
Institute for Applied Radio System Technology

Title: Mac Mini heralds mini revolution
Article_Text: The Mac Mini was launched amid much fanfare by Apple and great excitement by Apple watchers last month. But does the latest Macintosh justify the hype? Let us get a few things dealt with at the outset...
Summary: The Mac Mini is a small computer designed by Apple, featuring a G4 processor, CD/DVD player, and operating system, bundled with iLife software suite. It is not the fastest computer for the money but offers a good balance of power and price. The Mac Mini has encouraged users to experiment with their Macs, and its small size makes it a practical solution for in-car entertainment.

Title: Can Yahoo dominate next decade?
Article_Text: Yahoo has reached the grand old age of 10 and, in internet years, that is a long time.  For many, Yahoo remains synonymous with the internet - a veteran that managed to ride the dot-com wave and the s...
Summary: Yahoo is celebrating its 10th anniversary as a major internet brand, but its future is threatened by Google's growing influence. Yahoo's initial decision to outsource its search engine to Google has been seen as a mistake by some analysts. Despite this, Yahoo remains a dominant brand in the web portal market, thanks to its strategic acquisitions and business savvy.

Title: Looks and music to drive mobiles
Article_Text: Mobile phones are still enjoying a boom time in sales, according to research from technology analysts Gartner.  More than 674 million mobiles were sold last year globally, said the report, the highest...
Summary: Mobile phone sales reached a record high of 674 million globally last year, surpassing predictions and driven by good design and new services like music downloads. However, some markets are seeing a slowdown in replacement sales, and mobile companies must offer compelling reasons to upgrade. Third generation mobiles and music services are expected to drive sales in 2005.

Title: Hotspot users gain free net calls
Article_Text: People using wireless net hotspots will soon be able to make free phone calls as well as surf the net.  Wireless provider Broadreach and net telephony firm Skype are rolling out a service at 350 hotsp...
Summary: Wireless provider Broadreach and net telephony firm Skype are launching a service allowing users to make free phone calls and surf the net via wi-fi at 350 hotspots around the UK. The service requires a Skype account and will also allow users to make calls to landlines and mobiles for a fee. Skype has 28 million users worldwide.

Title: Domain system opens door to scams
Article_Text: A system to make it easier to create website addresses using alphabets like Cyrillic could open a back door for scammers, a trade body has warned.  The Internationalised Domain Names system has been a...
Summary: A new system for creating website addresses using alphabets like Cyrillic could make it easier for scammers to create fake sites, a trade body has warned. The system, approved by the Internet Engineering Task Force, uses a hybrid of ASCII and Unicode codes, which could be used to create fake domains that look identical to legitimate sites. A fake PayPal domain has already been registered and handed back to the company.
Key_Entities: Council of European National Top Level Domain Registries

Title: Sony PSP tipped as a 'must-have'
Article_Text: Sony's Playstation Portable is the top UK gadget for 2005, according to a round-up of ultimate gizmos compiled by Stuff Magazine.  It beats the iPod into second place in the Top Ten Essentials list wh...
Summary: The Sony Playstation Portable is the top UK gadget for 2005, according to Stuff Magazine's Top Ten Essentials list, beating the iPod into second place. Owning all 10 gadgets will cost £7,455. The list predicts that portable gadgets will dominate 2006, with the Xbox 2, high-definition TV, and MP3 mobiles among the must-haves.

Title: 'No re-draft' for EU patent law
Article_Text: A proposed European law on software patents will not be re-drafted by the European Commission (EC) despite requests by MEPs.  The law is proving controversial and has been in limbo for a year. Some ma...
Summary: A proposed European law on software patents will not be re-drafted by the European Commission despite requests by MEPs, who fear it could hurt smaller tech firms. The law aims to offer patent protection to inventions that use software to achieve their effect. The European Commission has supported the agreement reached by ministers in May 2004, but the directive still needs approval from both the Parliament and the Council of Ministers.

Title: Ultra fast wi-fi nears completion
Article_Text: Ultra high speed wi-fi connections moved closer to reality on Thursday when Intel said it would list standards for the technology later this year.  Intel is developing ultra-wideband technology (UWB) ...
Summary: Intel announced it will list standards for ultra-wideband technology (UWB) later this year, which could enable fast data transfer with low power needs. UWB is being developed by Intel and rival groups, and has the potential to transmit hundreds of megabits of data per second. The technology could replace cables and simplify setup in consumer electronics.

Title: Virgin Radio offers 3G broadcast
Article_Text: UK broadcaster Virgin Radio says it will become the first station in the world to offer radio via 3G mobiles.  The radio station, in partnership with technology firm Sydus, will broadcast on selected ...
Summary: UK broadcaster Virgin Radio will become the first station to offer radio via 3G mobiles, partnering with technology firm Sydus to broadcast on selected networks. Listeners will be able to download software to access the service. The move aims to tap into a new audience and keep radio relevant.

Title: More movies head to Sony's PSP
Article_Text: Movies Open Water and Saw are among those to be made available for Sony's PSP games console.  Film studio Lions Gate entertainment has announced an initial list of 12 movies that will be on the UMD fo...
Summary: Lions Gate Entertainment has announced 12 movies for Sony's PSP games console, including Open Water and Saw, with the first million customers in the US receiving Spider-Man 2 on UMD. The movies will be available in the UMD format, which is smaller than DVDs and can hold up to 1.8GB of data. The disks will cost between $10 to $30.
Key_Entities: Once Upon a Time in Mexico

Title: Warnings on woeful wi-fi security
Article_Text: Companies are getting worse at keeping their wireless data networks secure.  A survey of wi-fi networks in London, Frankfurt, New York and San Francisco by RSA Security found more than a third had bas...
Summary: A survey by RSA Security found that more than a third of wi-fi networks in London, Frankfurt, New York, and San Francisco had basic security features turned off, despite warnings about the dangers of 'drive-by hacking'. The survey also found that many firms were taking unnecessary risks by using default settings and not turning on encryption. The growth rate of wireless networks has increased, making it more likely that insecure networks will be found and exploited.

Title: Cebit opens to mobile music tune
Article_Text: Cebit, the world's largest hi-tech fair, has opened its doors in Hanover for a look at the latest technologies for homes and businesses.  There are more than 6,000 exhibitors registered and about 500,...
Summary: Cebit, the world's largest hi-tech fair, has opened its doors in Hanover, showcasing the latest technologies for homes and businesses, including third generation mobiles, digital home, and broadband. Key themes include camera phones, music-enabled mobiles, and TV-enabled mobiles. The show is expected to feature innovative products and technologies, including HSDPA and low-cost net telephony.

Title: Game makers get Xbox 2 sneak peek
Article_Text: Microsoft has given game makers a glimpse of the new Xbox 2 console.  Some details of the Xbox's performance and what gaming will be like with the device were given at the annual Game Developers Confe...
Summary: Microsoft has shown the Xbox 2 console's capabilities at the Game Developers Conference, with a focus on high-definition graphics and ease of use for game developers and players. The console is expected to be released in November and will support online play and customization options. Microsoft is saving the official unveiling for the E3 show in May.

Title: Broadband set to revolutionise TV
Article_Text: BT is starting its push into television with plans to offer TV over broadband.  As a telecoms company, BT is moving to a content distribution strategy, Andrew Burke, chief of BT's new Entertainment un...
Summary: BT plans to offer TV over broadband, a content distribution strategy, as it seeks to make money from its investment in broadband technology. The BBC is also trialling a similar service, with successful technical trials and upcoming consumer trials, aiming to offer value for money and more control to viewers. The move is part of the changing TV technology landscape, with IPTV expected to account for 10% of the digital TV market in Europe by the end of the decade.

Title: Chip maker backs net phone calls
Article_Text: Rich Templeton, the head of giant chip maker Texas Instruments, has given his backing to the growing sector of Voice over Internet Telephony (Voip)  Voip allows PC users, and in some cases those with ...
Summary: Rich Templeton, head of Texas Instruments, supports the growing Voip sector, while Wanadoo launches its broadband telephony service in the UK, offering free evening and weekend calls. Eric Abensur, Wanadoo's CEO, believes Voip will have a dramatic impact on the telecommunications industry. AOL plans to launch a net-based phone service for its members within a month.

Title: Nintendo DS makes its Euro debut
Article_Text: Nintendo's DS handheld game console has officially gone on sale in Europe.  Many stores around the UK opened at midnight to let keen gamers get their hands on the device. The two-screen clamshell gadg...
Summary: Nintendo's DS handheld game console has launched in Europe, with a price of £99 and 15 games available at launch. The device is expected to compete with Sony's PSP console, which is set to release soon. Nintendo aims to continue its dominance of the handheld gaming market.

Title: Slow start to speedy net services
Article_Text: Faster broadband in the UK is becoming a reality as more internet providers offer super-fast services.  Some lucky Britons can already take advantage of UK Online's 8 megabits per second service, whic...
Summary: Faster broadband services are becoming available in the UK, with BT Retail and Wanadoo planning trials and national rollouts. BT Retail aims to differentiate itself with its 8 megabits per second service, while Wanadoo plans to offer speeds of up to 15 megabits per second. Cable firms ntl and Telewest are also expected to increase bandwidth in the future.

Title: Anti-tremor mouse stops PC shakes
Article_Text: A special adaptor that helps people with hand tremors control a computer mouse more easily has been developed.  The device uses similar "steady cam" technology found in camcorders to filter out shakin...
Summary: A special adaptor called the Assistive Mouse Adapter (AMA) has been developed to help people with hand tremors control a computer mouse more easily. The device uses 'steady cam' technology to filter out shaking hand movements. The AMA will be produced by IBM and a UK-based electronics firm, Montrose Secam, and will cost around £70.

Title: The pirates with no profit motive
Article_Text: Two men who were part of a huge network of internet software pirates, known as Drink Or Die, have been convicted at the Old Bailey. BBC News investigates how the network worked and what motivated thos...
Summary: Two men involved in the Drink Or Die network of internet software pirates have been convicted at the Old Bailey. The network, known as Drink Or Die, was a group of computer buffs who cracked codes protecting copyrighted software and shared them with each other. The authorities considered it software piracy and took action against the network.

Title: Apple makes blogs reveal sources
Article_Text: Apple has won its legal fight to make three bloggers reveal who told them about unreleased products.  The bid to unmask the employees leaking information was launched in December 2004 following online...
Summary: Apple has won its legal fight to make three bloggers reveal who told them about unreleased products, and can now access their e-mail records to identify the leakers. The ruling sets a precedent that could harm all news reporters, according to a lawyer for the bloggers. Apple sued the PowerPage and Apple Insider sites, while a separate case against Think Secret remains unresolved.

Title: Hitachi unveils 'fastest robot'
Article_Text: Japanese electronics firm Hitachi has unveiled its first humanoid robot, called Emiew, to challenge Honda's Asimo and Sony's Qrio robots.  Hitachi said the 1.3m (4.2ft) Emiew was the world's quickest-...
Summary: Hitachi has unveiled its first humanoid robot, Emiew, which can move at 3.7m/h and has a vocabulary of about 100 words. The robots will be guests at the World Expo later this month. Emiew's design allows it to move quickly and safely in public spaces.
Key_Entities: American Association for the Advancement of Science

Title: Have hackers recruited your PC?
Article_Text: More than one million computers on the net have been hijacked to attack websites and pump out spam and viruses.  The huge number was revealed by security researchers who have spent months tracking mor...
Summary: More than one million computers have been hijacked to attack websites and pump out spam and viruses. Security researchers tracked over 100 networks of remotely-controlled machines, with the largest network consisting of 50,000 hijacked home computers. The Honeynet Project gathered information using 'honey pot' networks of computers to attract hackers and gather data.

Title: What price for 'trusted PC security'?
Article_Text: You can now buy "trusted computers", but can we really trust the PC vendors, asks technology analyst Bill Thompson.  If you have recently bought an IBM ThinkVantage computer, a Dell Optiplex, or one o...
Summary: A new "trusted computing" chip, called the trusted platform module (TPM), is being integrated into various computer systems, including laptops from major manufacturers such as IBM, Dell, and Samsung. The TPM provides enhanced security features, including hardware-based security, which is less common and more secure than software-based security. However, the increased security may also lead to restrictions on digital content, such as music and movies, and may not be in the best interest of users, who may lose their fair use rights under copyright law.

Title: Gizmondo gadget hits the shelves
Article_Text: The Gizmondo combined media player, phone and gaming gadget goes on sale on Saturday.  Priced at £229, the handheld device is debuting in the UK and goes on sale in the US and mainland Europe in the n...
Summary: The Gizmondo handheld device is going on sale in the UK and will be available in the US and mainland Europe in the coming weeks. It features a range of functions, including gaming, music, movies, and phone capabilities. The device will compete with established brands like Nintendo, Sony, and Nokia.

Title: Confusion over high-definition TV
Article_Text: Now that a critical mass of people have embraced digital TV, DVDs, and digital video recorders, the next revolution for TV is being prepared for our sets.  In most corners of TV and technology industr...
Summary: The TV industry is preparing for the next revolution with high-definition (HDTV) technology, but there is concern about consumer confusion over what devices are truly HD-ready. The BBC is developing plans to produce all its TV output in HDTV by 2010, while BSkyB plans to ship HDTV set-top boxes in early 2006. To address consumer confusion, the industry is introducing a 'HD-Ready' sticker on devices that meet the minimum specification.

Title: Digital UK driven by net and TV
Article_Text: The UK's adoption of digital TV and broadband has helped make it the fourth most digitally-savvy nation in Europe, according a report by Jupiter Research.  But the UK still lags in terms of broadband ...
Summary: The UK's digital adoption has improved its ranking in Europe, but it still lags behind in broadband speeds. The report by Jupiter Research shows that Scandinavian countries are the most digitally sophisticated, while Greece is the least. The UK's broadband adoption is expected to increase, with cable company NTL trialling faster technology.

Title: Bad e-mail habits sustains spam
Article_Text: The 'bad behaviour' of e-mail users is helping to sustain the spam industry, a new study has found.  According to a survey conducted by security firm Mirapoint and market research company the Radicati...
Summary: A new study found that nearly a third of e-mail users have clicked on links in spam messages, and one in ten have bought products advertised in junk mail. This behavior is helping to sustain the spam industry, which costs very little to send out. Experts warn that clicking on spam links can expose users to viruses and alert spammers to live e-mail accounts.

Title: Sony PSP handheld console hits US
Article_Text: The latest handheld gaming gadget, Sony's PlayStation Portable, goes on sale in the US on Thursday.  The entertainment device, which also stores images, music and video, is intended to compete with Ni...
Summary: Sony's PlayStation Portable goes on sale in the US, competing with Nintendo's DS, and features a wireless connection for multiplayer gaming. The device costs $250 and comes with a Spider-Man 2 film on UMD. Sony expects to sell 10 million PSPs worldwide by the end of its fiscal year.

Title: 'Podcasters' look to net money
Article_Text: Nasa is doing it, 14-year-old boys in bedrooms are doing it, couples are doing it, gadget lovers - male and female - are definitely doing it.  It is podcasting - DIY radio in the form of downloadable ...
Summary: Podcasting is a DIY radio format where users can create and distribute downloadable MP3 audio files using simple software and the internet. The medium is gaining momentum, with over 4,300 podcasts listed, and has the potential to disrupt traditional radio business models.

Title: Local net TV takes off in Austria
Article_Text: An Austrian village is testing technology that could represent the future of television.  The people of Engerwitzdorf are filming, editing and producing their own regional news channel. The channel co...
Summary: An Austrian village, Engerwitzdorf, is testing a technology that allows residents to film, edit, and produce their own regional news channel, with Telekom Austria considering setting up similar projects elsewhere.

Title: Rolling out next generation's net
Article_Text: The body that oversees how the net works, grows and evolves says it has coped well with its growth in the last 10 years, but it is just the start.  "In a sense, we have hardly started in reaching the ...
Summary: The Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) has coped well with its growth over the last 10 years, but its chair, Brian Carpenter, says it's just the start. The IETF is working on IPv6, the next generation standard for information transfer and routing across the web, to address the growing challenges of broadband and emerging economies.

Title: Long life promised for laptop PCs
Article_Text: Scientists are working on ways to ensure laptops can stay powered for an entire working day.  Building batteries from new chemical mixes could boost power significantly, say industry experts. The chan...
Summary: Scientists are working on ways to improve laptop battery life, with new chemical mixes and design changes promising to boost power significantly. Industry experts say that current battery life is limited by the technology used, and that new innovations are needed to achieve longer battery life. Intel is working with component makers to test energy consumption and find ways to reduce power usage.

Title: Net fingerprints combat attacks
Article_Text: Eighty large net service firms have switched on software to spot and stop net attacks automatically.  The system creates digital fingerprints of ongoing incidents that are sent to every network affect...
Summary: Eighty large net service firms have switched on software to spot and stop net attacks automatically. The system creates digital fingerprints of ongoing incidents that are sent to every network affected. Firms involved in the smart sensing system believe it will help trace attacks back to their source.

Title: Microsoft plans 'safer ID' system
Article_Text: Microsoft is planning to make Windows and Internet Explorer more secure by including software to give people more control over personal information.  "Info cards" will help people manage personal deta...
Summary: Microsoft is developing a new version of Internet Explorer and Windows to make online services safer by giving users more control over their personal information. The new system, called 'info cards,' will store data on a user's PC, rather than centrally on the net. This will put control of digital IDs into the hands of the end-user.

Title: Court mulls file-sharing future
Article_Text: Judges at the US Supreme Court have been hearing evidence for and against file-sharing networks.  The court will decide whether producers of file-sharing software can ultimately be held responsible fo...
Summary: The US Supreme Court is hearing a case about whether file-sharing networks can be held responsible for copyright infringement, with the court considering the impact on innovation and the entertainment industry's pursuit of individuals who use peer-to-peer networks.

Title: France starts digital terrestrial
Article_Text: France has become the last big European country to launch a digital terrestrial TV (DTT) service.  Initially, more than a third of the population will be able to receive 14 free-to-air channels. Despi...
Summary: France has launched its digital terrestrial TV (DTT) service, known as TNT, which will initially offer 14 free-to-air channels to over a third of the population. The service is a joint venture between France Televisions and cable and satellite operators, and aims to reach 35% of the population at launch. The platform's backers hope to emulate the success of Freeview in the UK.

Title: Text message record smashed again
Article_Text: UK mobile owners continue to break records with their text messaging, with latest figures showing that 26 billion texts were sent in total in 2004.  The figures collected by the Mobile Data Associatio...
Summary: UK mobile owners sent 26 billion texts in 2004, with December's total exceeding 2.4 billion, surpassing predictions. Forecasts predict 30 billion texts for 2005. Mobiles are becoming increasingly sophisticated, with multimedia applications and new uses like booking cinema tickets and donating to charity.

Title: Software watching while you work
Article_Text: Software that can not only monitor every keystroke and action performed at a PC but also be used as legally binding evidence of wrong-doing has been unveiled.  Worries about cyber-crime and sabotage h...
Summary: A new software system has been unveiled that can monitor employee activity and store data for legal use, amid concerns over cyber-crime and employee privacy.

Title: Commodore finds new lease of life
Article_Text: The once-famous Commodore computer brand could be resurrected after being bought by a US-based digital music distributor.  New owner Yeahronimo Media Ventures has not ruled out the possibility of a ne...
Summary: The Commodore computer brand may be revived after being bought by Yeahronimo Media Ventures, a US-based digital music distributor. The new owner plans to develop a 'worldwide entertainment concept' with the brand. The Commodore 64, a pioneering home computer, was launched in 1982 and remains one of the best-selling single computer systems.

Title: Cabs collect mountain of mobiles
Article_Text: Gadgets are cheaper, smaller and more common than ever. But that just means we are more likely to lose them.  In London alone over the past six months more than 63,000 mobile phones have been left in ...
Summary: A survey found that over 63,000 mobile phones were left in black cabs in London over the past six months, with laptops and PDAs also being left behind. The popularity of portable gadgets has grown, but people seem to be forgetting them in larger numbers. A Mobile Equipment National Database has been created to help recover lost gadgets.

Title: T-Mobile bets on 'pocket office'
Article_Text: T-Mobile has launched its latest "pocket office" third-generation (3G) device which also has built-in wi-fi - high-speed wireless net access.  Unlike other devices where the user has to check which hi...
Summary: T-Mobile has launched its latest 3G device with built-in Wi-Fi, allowing users to access high-speed wireless networks automatically. The device features a swivelled display and a Qwerty keyboard, and is part of the company's push for 'Office in a Pocket' devices. T-Mobile also announced plans to expand its Wi-Fi hotspots and introduce a new tariff for UK customers.

Title: California sets fines for spyware
Article_Text: The makers of computer programs that secretly spy on what people do with their home PCs could face hefty fines in California.  From 1 January, a new law is being introduced to protect computer users f...
Summary: A new law in California aims to protect computer users from spyware, a type of software that secretly spies on users' activities. The law, approved by Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger, bans the installation of software that takes control of another computer and requires companies to disclose whether their systems will install spyware. Consumers can seek up to $1,000 in damages if they think they have fallen victim to spyware.

Title: Mobile TV tipped as one to watch
Article_Text: Scandinavians and Koreans, two of the most adventurous groups of mobile users, are betting on mobile TV.  Anders Igels, chief executive of Nordic operator Teliasonera, tipped it as the next big thing ...
Summary: Mobile TV is gaining popularity, with several mobile operators and equipment vendors investing in the technology. The industry is expected to generate $6.6bn in revenue by 2009, with 51 million users worldwide. However, there is a battle for supremacy between two competing standards: DVB-H and DMB.

Title: Apple laptop is 'greatest gadget'
Article_Text: The Apple Powerbook 100 has been chosen as the greatest gadget of all time, by US magazine Mobile PC.  The 1991 laptop was chosen because it was one of the first "lightweight" portable computers and h...
Summary: The Apple Powerbook 100 has been chosen as the greatest gadget of all time by US magazine Mobile PC, due to its innovative design and impact on the development of future notebook PCs. The magazine compiled an all-time top 100 list of gadgets, which includes the Sony Walkman at number three and the 1956 Zenith remote control at two. The list was compiled by the magazine staff, who specified that gadgets needed to be self-contained and mobile.

Title: Sun offers processing by the hour
Article_Text: Sun Microsystems has launched a pay-as-you-go service which will allow customers requiring huge computing power to rent it by the hour.  Sun Grid costs users $1 (53p) for an hour's worth of processing...
Summary: Sun Microsystems has launched a pay-as-you-go service called Sun Grid, allowing customers to rent computing power by the hour for $1. The system relies on Solaris and could mature like utilities, according to Sun's chief operating officer Jonathan Schwartz. The company has interest from customers in the oil, gas and financial services industries.

Title: Kenyan school turns to handhelds
Article_Text: At the Mbita Point primary school in western Kenya students click away at a handheld computer with a stylus.  They are doing exercises in their school textbooks which have been digitised. It is a pilo...
Summary: EduVision is piloting a project to digitize school textbooks using low-cost computer systems and satellite radio, aiming to increase access to knowledge in rural developing countries.

Title: Tough rules for ringtone sellers
Article_Text: Firms that flout rules on how ringtones and other mobile extras are sold could be cut off from all UK phone networks.  The rules allow offenders to be cut off if they do not let consumers know exactly...
Summary: Firms that sell mobile extras without transparently disclosing their services and terms may be cut off from UK phone networks. The new rules aim to protect consumers from potential harm. The first month under the new regime has seen at least ten firms suspended.

Title: Mobile music challenges 'iPod age'
Article_Text: Nokia and Microsoft have agreed a deal to work on delivery of music to handsets, while Sony Ericsson has unveiled its phone Walkman and Motorola is working on an iTunes phone.  Can mobile phones repla...
Summary: Nokia and Microsoft have agreed to work on music delivery to handsets, while Sony Ericsson has unveiled its phone Walkman and Motorola is working on an iTunes phone. The mobile music industry believes that mobile phones can replace MP3 players due to ease of use, low price, and increased access to broadband.

Title: China 'ripe' for media explosion
Article_Text: Asia is set to drive global media growth to 2008 and beyond, with China and India filling the two top spots, analysts have predicted.  Japan, South Korea and Singapore will also be strong players, but...
Summary: Asia is expected to drive global media growth, with China and India leading the way. China's large middle-class population and growing foreign investment are driving demand for media and communications. The country's media market is experiencing explosive growth, particularly in new media such as mobile services and online gaming.

Title: Beckham virus spotted on the net
Article_Text: Virus writers are trading on interest in David Beckham to distribute their malicious wares.  Messages are circulating widely that purport to have evidence of the England captain in a compromising posi...
Summary: Virus writers are using interest in David Beckham to distribute malicious software, which can infect computers and open a backdoor for remote control by hackers. The virus, called Hackarmy, targets Windows users and can be spread through fake image files downloaded from a website. Anti-virus programs have detected the virus since its appearance early this year.

Title: Video phones act as dating tools
Article_Text: Technologies, from e-mail, to net chatrooms, instant messaging and mobiles, have proved to be a big pull with those looking for love.  The lure once was that you could hide behind the technology, but ...
Summary: The world's first video mobile dating event will take place at London's Institute of Contemporary Arts (ICA) on November 30, featuring 100 contestants who have submitted mobile video profiles. The event is organized by 3G network, 3, and aims to provide a safe and interesting way for people to meet using video phone technologies.

Title: Progress on new internet domains
Article_Text: By early 2005 the net could have two new domain names.  The .post and .travel net domains have been given preliminary approval by the net's administrative body. The names are just two of a total of 10...
Summary: The Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (Icann) has given preliminary approval to two new domain names, .post and .travel, which are expected to be used for postal services and travel organizations, respectively. Icann is considering proposals for another eight domains, including a .xxx domain for pornographic websites, which has been met with resistance due to the difficulty of making pornographers sign up and use it.

Title: Camera phones are 'must-haves'
Article_Text: Four times more mobiles with cameras in them will be sold in Europe by the end of 2004 than last year, says a report from analysts Gartner.  Globally, the number sold will reach 159 million, an increa...
Summary: Gartner predicts that nearly 70% of all mobile phones sold will have a built-in camera by 2008, with image quality improving over the next few years. Camera phones are becoming increasingly popular, with many manufacturers introducing design features and improvements to make them easier to use. The technology is also being used in the art world, with an upcoming exhibition featuring images taken from camera phones.

Title: Mobile multimedia slow to catch on
Article_Text: There is no doubt that mobile phones sporting cameras and colour screens are hugely popular.  Consumers swapping old phones for slinkier, dinkier versions are thought to be responsible for a 26% incre...
Summary: Mobile phone users are not sending multimedia messages due to lack of knowledge and technical issues. Operators are finding alternative technologies to overcome bandwidth limitations. A new broadcast system is being used to get multimedia to customers, increasing engagement.

Title: Anti-spam laws bite spammer hard
Article_Text: The net's self-declared spam king is seeking bankruptcy protection.  Scott Richter, the man behind OptInRealBig.com and billions of junk mail messages, said lawsuits had forced the company into Chapte...
Summary: OptInRealBig, a company behind billions of junk mail messages, is seeking bankruptcy protection due to lawsuits, including a legal battle with Microsoft over millions of dollars in damages. The company claims it has assets of less than $10m but debts of over $50m. It aims to resolve its legal problems while continuing to trade.

Title: Peer-to-peer nets 'here to stay'
Article_Text: Peer-to-peer (P2P) networks are here to stay, and are on the verge of being exploited by commercial media firms, says a panel of industry experts.  Once several high-profile legal cases against file-s...
Summary: Industry experts predict that commercial media firms will exploit P2P technology once high-profile legal cases are resolved, and P2P networks will be used to distribute content in various ways, including paid-for-pass-along models and digital rights management.

Title: Broadband fuels online expression
Article_Text: Fast web access is encouraging more people to express themselves online, research suggests.  A quarter of broadband users in Britain regularly upload content and have personal sites, according to a re...
Summary: Research suggests that fast web access is encouraging more people to express themselves online, with a quarter of broadband users in Britain regularly uploading content and having personal sites. Broadband is changing the way people use the internet, with many logging on before breakfast and spending more time online than those on dial-up connections. The report also found that broadband is encouraging people to take a more active role online.

Title: Savvy searchers fail to spot ads
Article_Text: Internet search engine users are an odd mix of naive and sophisticated, suggests a report into search habits.  The report by the US Pew Research Center reveals that 87% of searchers usually find what ...
Summary: A report by the US Pew Research Center found that 87% of searchers usually find what they were looking for, but few can spot the difference between paid-for and organic results. Most users trust search engines, but would stop using them if they knew information about paid results was being hidden.

Title: TV's future down the phone line
Article_Text: Internet TV has been talked about since the start of the web as we know it now.  But any early attempts to do it - the UK's Home Choice started in 1992 - were thwarted by the lack of a fast network. N...
Summary: Internet TV, or IPTV, is becoming a reality as broadband networks improve, allowing telcos to send video, voice, and data down one line. This technology uses the same internet technology as web data, enabling interactive features and instant channel switching. Microsoft and other companies are investing in IPTV, with plans to expand services to more geographies.

Title: Cebit fever takes over Hanover
Article_Text: Thousands of products and tens of thousands of visitors make Cebit the place to be for technology lovers.  "Welcome to CeBit 2005" was the message from the pilot as we landed, the message on flyers at...
Summary: CeBit 2005 is a major technology exhibition in Hanover, Germany, featuring thousands of products and companies showcasing their latest innovations, including digital homes, convergence, and mobile phones. Exhibitors include Intel, Microsoft, Samsung, NEC, and Nokia, with a focus on wireless technology and entertainment PCs. Other companies, such as Creative and Adidas, are also demonstrating their products, including wireless headphones and intelligent shoes.

Title: New consoles promise big problems
Article_Text: Making games for future consoles will require more graphic artists and more money, an industry conference has been told.  Sony, Microsoft and Nintendo will debut their new consoles at the annual E3 ga...
Summary: The next generation of consoles will require more graphic artists and more money to develop, with costs estimated between $10-25m for a single title. Developers are exploring alternative solutions, such as using new development tools and creating games for mobile phones and handheld consoles.

Title: BT program to beat dialler scams
Article_Text: BT is introducing two initiatives to help beat rogue dialler scams, which can cost dial-up net users thousands.  From May, dial-up net users will be able to download free software to stop computers us...
Summary: BT is introducing two initiatives to combat rogue dialler scams, which can cost users thousands. The initiatives include a free software download to block unauthorized numbers and an early warning system to alert customers of unusual activity on their phone bills. The measures aim to protect consumers from premium rate scams.

Title: Spam e-mails tempt net shoppers
Article_Text: Computer users across the world continue to ignore security warnings about spam e-mails and are being lured into buying goods, a report suggests.  More than a quarter have bought software through spam...
Summary: A report suggests that computer users worldwide are ignoring security warnings about spam e-mails, with over a quarter buying software and 24% buying clothes or jewelry through spam e-mails. Organised crime rings use spam to glean personal information and drive advertising traffic. Experts warn consumers to stay alert and exercise caution.

Title: Be careful how you code
Article_Text: A new European directive could put software writers at risk of legal action, warns former programmer and technology analyst Bill Thompson.  If it gets its way, the Dutch government will conclude its p...
Summary: A new European directive on patenting computer programs could put software writers at risk of legal action, as it would allow programs to be patented in Europe just as they are in the US, potentially limiting innovation and damaging the European computer industry.

Title: US cyber security chief resigns
Article_Text: The man making sure US computer networks are safe and secure has resigned after only a year in his post.  Amit Yoran was director of the National Cyber Security Division within the US Department of Ho...
Summary: Amit Yoran, the director of the National Cyber Security Division, has resigned after only a year in his post due to lack of clout within the organization. He oversaw the creation of a cyber alert system and audited US government networks. Yoran left abruptly, reportedly giving only one day's notice.

Title: Losing yourself in online gaming
Article_Text: Online role playing games are time-consuming, but enthralling flights from reality. But are some people taking their fantasy lives too seriously?  When video game World of Warcraft hit the shops in Eu...
Summary: A growing number of people are spending excessive amounts of time playing online role-playing games (MMORPGs), with some experiencing negative impacts on their relationships and daily lives. The article cites concerns from gamers who have become addicted to games like World of Warcraft, EverQuest, and Ultima Online, with some spending up to 40 hours a week playing. While gaming can be a fun and social activity, some individuals are struggling to balance their online gaming habits with real-life responsibilities.
